text:
怎么看谷歌三季度财报？一个亮点两个担忧。如果只是粗看营收和利润均不及预期很害怕，但往细了看云业务GCP还是大超预期，不及预期的是搜索广告、youtube广告均不及预期，把整个集团的营收和利润给带下去了。详细聊聊：
1、云业务的亮点
三季度谷歌云收入307.09亿美元，同比增长102.6%；营业利润111.21亿美元，营业利润率36.2%。在二季度接近250亿美元收入的基础上，又环比增长约24%，这个扩张速度确实很强。

当然这里面包含了TPU的销售，管理层（包括CFO Anat Ashkenazi和Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian）明确表示：GCP贡献了Q3云营收的绝大部分；剔除TPU系统销售影响后，云营收增速“again incredibly strong”（再次极为强劲 / 非常强劲）。

那么可以这么说、即使剔除TPU的销售，GCP的增速也是很强劲的。应该也是AI商业化在加速的支撑。

2、担忧之一主业不及预期
虽然云业务增速强劲、但是毕竟占集团营收大头还是搜索广告和youtube广告、这块不及预期会让市场担心主业是不是在失血。搜索广告放缓，官方给了四个解释：汇率、部分零售广告受到欧盟新规影响、6月世界杯广告热潮褪去、AImode变现。

而AI Mode的低变现，才是本次最值得跟踪的结构性因素，这部分已经得到管理层承认。但官方还没有回答几个决定长期价值的问题：
1）AI Mode主要增加了原本不会发生的查询，还是替代了已有查询？
2）迁移过去的查询，有多少原本带有较强购买意图？
3）广告覆盖扩大后，每次查询的收入能恢复到什么水平？
4）扣除模型推理成本之后，利润能恢复多少？

市场已经看到AI对谷歌搜索的广告变现产生影响，是AI搜索的使用增长快于广告商业化，但还没看到对上面这四点清晰明确的解释，自然担忧会加大。

3、另一重担忧就是资本开支和现金流
三季度自由现金流降至负90.7亿美元，远超市场预期的负35亿美元；资本开支513.6亿美元，低于市场预期的557.8亿美元，维持2026全年1950-2050亿美金资本开支的指引。

但自由现金流这块需要细看，有两个非常规因素的影响
1）TPU系统库存建设：库存从2025年底约24亿美元升至季末约133亿美元。Q3单季库存现金流出约32亿美元（九个月累计约110亿美元）。这些是为已签约但尚未交付/确认收入的TPU系统备货，现金先流出、收入后确认，属于“不同的现金流周期”。
2）欧洲委员会罚款现金支付：约52亿美元（2018年相关罚款上诉结束后支付），直接减少经营现金流。

若加回库存流出和罚款，调整后的数字会明显改善（估算接近持平或小幅负值）。

而利润和EPS大幅低于预期，则需要考虑股权投资账面亏损的影响，主要是对SpaceX的未实现（账面）亏损。
1）权益证券净亏损约86.6–87亿美元，使净利润减少约67亿美元、EPS减少约0.55美元。
2）其他收入与支出（OI&E）为—82亿美元CFO明确表示“primarily due to unrealized loss from our investment in SpaceX”（主要来自SpaceX股价季度下跌带来的未实现亏损）。

这是按市值计价的纸面亏损，不是实际卖出股票造成的现金损失。

总结就是：
利润被SpaceX账面亏损拖累（非现金）；
FCF深度为负主要是高CapEx + TPU库存备货现金流出 + 欧盟罚款现金支付；CapEx单季低于预期但全年指引不变；公司正在通过ATM股权发行和发债持续为AI资本开支融资。

回到对市场的影响上来看：
市场看到云业务的强劲，但是主业搜索不及预期加深了担忧，比预期更差的自由现金流负责引发Capex持续性的担忧（但细看原因有两项都属于非常规性因素），但主业失速也是真实发生的，又在持续ATM融资（还有近300亿美金的额度没用完），所以盘后大跌。

个人看法谷歌核心竞争力还是在的：云业务的快速增长 （这是关键），AI全栈布局、还有超过2000亿美金的现金储备。
市场需要消化主业失速和Gemini旗舰模型还没完全追赶上来的利空，之后反转需要看到AI mode搜索商业化赶上使用量，抑或旗舰模型和Agent上发力赶超。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
谷歌Q3前瞻如果云业务增长翻倍，但自由现金流大概率仍为负，市场怎么看？
市场对这份财报的预期已经很高。总营收共识约1279亿美元（+25%），云收入最新一致预期约291.6亿美元（+92%），搜索约+15%，YouTube广告约+11%。聊聊谷歌Q3财报最受关注的几点：
1、云业务接近翻倍，但还看营收质量 增长大概率落在95%-100%区间。但二季度起确认的TPU系统外销（交付到客户自有数据中心）会抬高数字，真正看点是剔除后原有云服务增速、传统企业消费是否加速，以及利润率（预期33%-35%，受第三方算力与Wiz整合影响略有压力）。

2、企业订单占比扩散很重要（这点与昨天聊微软财报前瞻里是一致的） Ryanair、法国巴黎银行等五年合作案例显示，非模型实验室客户开始用经营预算为AI买单。接近80%云客户已用AI产品、近90%财富100强用Gemini Enterprise，但接下来要看使用深度与持续付费。

3、资本开支与自由现金流是最大焦点 2026年Capex指引1950-2050亿美元，上半年已花约806亿，下半年压力大。2027年投行预期普遍3000亿美元以上。FCF大概率为负（含约52亿美元Android旧案罚款支付等），需拆出一次性项目再判断持续现金创造能力。

好的支出是提前到货+高利用率+客户提前付款；
坏的是成本上涨或回款持续后移。

EPS与利润率要穿透一次因素，去年有投资收益和欧盟罚款扰动，今年若有股权投资收益或报告利润率改善，要先看主营业务贡献。

总营收超预期（1285-1305亿美元），云95%-100%、搜索15%-17%，业务趋势偏乐观。但市场已计入强劲云增长，真正决定股价的是增长质量（剔除系统销售后的服务消费）、企业持续付费意愿，以及2027年Capex是否失控、现金流展望能否改善。

整体来看：
1）若明年资本开支没有明显超出市场假设，现金流展望也有所改善，这份财报的支撑就比较充分。
2）反过来，如果增长主要靠集中交付，云利润率和回款弱于预期，管理层又继续大幅增加支出，我会下调对资本回报的预期。

quoted_text:
卧槽！Ledger 被盗事件持续发酵：不止 Nano X，连高端 Stax 都被发现植入恶意模块！

目前涉及的 Ledger 型号，我全部整理了一下：

Ledger Nano X：证据最充分。

Mark Karpelès 和 Tibane Labs 等研究人员已经公开拆机，发现 Nordic nRF9151 蜂窝通信模块、MCU、eSIM 和隐藏天线。恶意电路藏在屏幕后面，甚至已经迭代出多代设计。

Ledger Stax：最新曝光！

10月11日出现首例公开植入报告，设备内部被发现额外的 4G/LTE 模块、芯片及隐藏天线，具备外传助记词的潜在能力。

Ledger Flex：社区用户提出设备异常及安全担忧，但尚未找到与 Nano X 同等级的完整恶意硬件拆机证据。

Ledger Nano S、S+、Gen5 目前没有发现与本次事件直接相关的可信硬件植入案例。

目前 Ledger 确认的资金被盗案例集中在东南亚授权经销商 CryptoBilis，涉及马来西亚、印尼、菲律宾。

text:
又仔细看了一下“仓鼠链”，一只真实的仓鼠，正在为一套链上经济系统提供全部“算力” 🐹

比特币通过矿机和能源消耗连接现实世界，Squeekchain 选择了一种更有 Meme 感的方式：让仓鼠日常的跑步转圈来实现。

参与入口：
https://t.co/aPRa1FLTt7

仓鼠转动跑轮，WHEELY9000 记录工作量。数据经过验证后提交到 Ethereum，累积形成 Squeek Block。每完成一个区块，协议就会释放 6,900 枚 SQK。

过去的 Meme 多数依靠图片、故事和社区传播。Squeekchain 让 Meme 主角进入协议本身，仓鼠在现实世界中的活动会直接影响链上区块进度和 SQK 产出。

它也不只部署了一个 Meme Token 合约。Squeekchain 围绕仓鼠工作量搭建了一套运行在 Ethereum 上的 toychain，包含：

🐹 物理挖矿设备 WHEELY9000
🐹 工作量签名与 Oracle
🐹 Squeek Block 计算系统
🐹 SQK 发行与奖励分配
🐹 Squeek NFT 算力系统
🐹 质押、合并与销毁机制
🐹 公开的链上数据和开发接口

普通 Meme 发行一个 Token，Squeekchain 试图运行一套完整的经济系统。

Squeek NFT 还可以理解为矿权凭证。仓鼠跑步产生 SQK，Squeek NFT 持有人按照有效算力比例分享区块产出。用户还可以质押 SQK，提高 Squeek 的有效算力，从而获得更高的产出份额。两个同等级 Squeek 可以合并升级，其中一个 NFT 会被永久销毁。随着合并持续进行，NFT 流通数量也可能逐渐减少。

项目还计划围绕仓鼠的公开工作数据建设 SqueekFi，包括预测市场、链上游戏、动态 NFT，以及按照 Squeek Block 进度运行的应用。

仓鼠每天跑多少、什么时候跑、能完成多少个区块，都可能成为公开数据、游戏变量和预测市场标的。

官方此前表示项目将在 10 月底启动。目前 Genesis 白名单活动已经进入关键阶段，参与人数 5,000 左右。

用户可以通过绑定账号、邀请好友、完成测试交互和提交项目获得 Badge 与 Aura，最终排名将决定白名单资格。

这个项目的叙事很强，产品完成度也高于普通 Meme。接下来重点关注正式铸造价格、合约审计、源码验证、协议 NFT 的使用方式，以及未来的SqueekFi 能否带来质押之外的真实需求。

text:
为什么普京宁愿长期打仗，也不愿轻易停战？理解俄罗斯的权力结构，就不难理解了。

很多人分析俄罗斯，总是从国家安全、北约东扩、民族主义和领土争端出发。但我认为，还有一个更重要的角度：俄罗斯的国家利益，不一定等于普京统治集团的利益。

俄罗斯的权力结构，可以简单理解为三个相互依赖的集团：

1. 普京及政治官僚集团： 掌握政策制定、资源分配和人事任命。

2. 军队与安全集团： 掌握武力，维护现有权力体系。

3. 寡头与商业利益集团： 控制大量经济资源，依靠政治关系获得财富和保护。

这三个集团形成了一套相互依存的体系：

权力分配财富，财富维系忠诚，武力保障权力。

那么，战争在这个体系中扮演什么角色？

普通人看到的是伤亡、制裁、通货膨胀和经济损失。

但部分统治集团成员看到的可能是军工订单、政府采购、资源重新分配，以及更大的政治权力。

战争还可能让民众把注意力从国内问题转向外部敌人，让军队和安全机构更加重要。

这并不意味着战争对整个统治集团都有利，更不代表战争是为了赚钱而发动的。但战争确实可能改变内部的利益分配，并强化某些人的政治地位。

这就产生了一个值得思考的问题：如果战争的成本主要由普通民众承担，而部分决策者能够从中巩固权力，那么他们结束战争的动力究竟有多大？

再看中俄朝关系，道理也类似。

俄罗斯需要中国的市场、工业产品和经济支持；中国需要俄罗斯的能源、贸易与战略合作；朝鲜则有自己的安全和经济诉求。

三国存在共同利益，但不意味着彼此完全信任，更不意味着利益永远一致。

所以，理解俄罗斯，不能只听普京说什么，更要看谁掌握权力、谁分配财富、谁承担代价、谁获得利益。

我认为，理解高度集中的政治体系，最重要的是分清四件事：

国家的利益、政权的利益、统治集团的利益，以及普通民众的利益。

它们有时一致，有时却可能发生严重冲突。

只有看清这一点，才能理解为什么某些看似损害国家整体利益的政策，仍然可能长期持续。

text:
回顾一下谷歌的财报，虽然不算优秀，但是股价为何“崩了”?

本周一的宏观纪要中我明确了三大云厂商要看的四大要素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引

而放到谷歌本身上，要看的则是五大要素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引+Google Cloud

那么谷歌财报给出了什么答案？

营收：小幅度不及预期，不是差，而是结果出现问题，绝对增速很强，但是市场预期更强，略低于预期，关键就在广告收入上略低预期

AI资本支出：公司全面依旧维持较高资本支出，全年投入2000亿美元，这对于上游英伟达、博通、HBM、光模块、服务器、电力预计数据中心整个AI基础设施链条，明确了需求验证逻辑

自由现金流：-91亿，今年第二季度负自由现金流，资本开支过大，营收追不上

Google Cloud：依旧是财报最强数据，307.1亿增长同步增幅103%，超过55%将在未来24个月确认收入，这个数据证明谷歌的AI基础建设已经开始形成大规模收入

未来指引：2027年资本支出显著增加，TPU系统将在2027年明显放量，但是因为AI算力供给紧张，谷歌开始使用第三方计算能力，管理层警告谷歌云业务短期利润将收到挤压

整体来看，五大要素中，除了自由现金流有问题，未来指引提示云业务利润受到挤压之外，其他数据依旧不错，尤其是核心业务Google Cloud很强，证明了企业的基本面没问题

但是，估计在财报后依旧出现较大幅度的下跌，主要是因为近期多方因素导致：

1，预期过强，符合预期的财报都会出现Sell the news，更何况一份有瑕疵的财报？估值修复幅度扩大正常

2，宏观要素，高利率挤压投资情绪，导致利空放大，估值修复幅度也大大增加，凌晨沃什讲话中明确提及高利率挤压了科技企业的融资能力，同时也让投资者手里的钱更贵，更舍不得为当下的估值买单

3，上游海力士强劲财报证明了更大的资本支出，但是下游云厂商却没能证明AI足够赚钱，AI商业逻辑被质疑，ROI成为焦点，质疑=估值调整

Q3财报我一直强调，市场对于AI企业的验证逻辑已经正式进入第二阶段，第一阶段看谁敢花钱，第二阶段看谁能挣钱，而谷歌恰好踩到“雷点”，都在拼赚钱，你的财报还在努力花钱，市场短期自然不买账

后市如何去看？

首先财报显示谷歌的基本面没问题，只是并未符合目前市场对财报的预期，所以大幅回调之后必然有短期技术性反弹

AI产业上，微软财报还不错，接下来看今晚凌晨的亚马逊财报，本周三大云厂商，如果3家中2家都不错，基本可以对冲掉谷歌财报给市场带来的风险担忧，

宏观侧，今晚先看GDP PCE 对美股是否有整体压力，数据公布消化后依旧要回归财报，凌晨美股尾盘锚定亚马逊财报预期，由于谷歌财报瑕疵，市场会相对谨慎，但是如果亚马逊财报不错，市场情绪会被提振

趋势上，AI的基本面，谷歌的基本面都依旧健康，宏观以及利率上虽然有挤压，但是不构成实质性威胁，最多就是造成估值深度调整，不过调整估值后对于股价以及后续反而是一件好事！

🚨 CHINA'S AI BUBBLE IS BURSTING

Almost ¥23.5 TRILLION has been wiped out from the Chinese stock market from its 2026 peak, as it has entered bear market territory.

And AI is taking the biggest hit.

China's STAR50 index has crashed 40% in less than four months, wiping out ¥3.2 Trillion.

Some of the biggest AI stocks have suffered even worse losses:

• Unitree: Down nearly 50%.
• CXMT: Down over 25% in a month.
• Zhongji Innolight and Eoptolink: Down around 60%.

But why is China's AI market collapsing?

1. Extreme valuations: AI stocks have become so expensive that even strong future growth can't justify their prices.

2. Weakening confidence in AI demand: Investors are questioning whether companies can generate enough profits from the massive spending on AI.

3. US restrictions: Fears of new restrictions on Chinese technology entering American data centers are hurting chipmakers and suppliers.

4. Speculative buying: According to Goldman Sachs, AI stocks accounted for 57% of trading activity across the Chinese markets it examined, leaving investors heavily exposed when selling began.

And here's what's really shocking.

Even after the crash, China's STAR50 trades at roughly 100 times earnings, compared with around 30 times for the Nasdaq 100.

This means that the Chinese stock market crash may not be over yet, and there's still more pain ahead.

text:
Sometimes it helps to think of trading like a business. Every business that lasts makes money because it provides something of value to someone who is willing to pay for it. In markets, that someone might be a hedger who needs to offload risk, a fund that is forced to rebalance or an impatient buyer who pays a spread for immediacy.

Most traders run this logic in reverse. It’s like opening a coffee shop because you love a particular street, then standing outside wondering why nobody comes in, instead of first finding where people actually want coffee and setting up there.

A business starts with the customer and the need and the location follows. Trading can work the same way, with the market chosen based on where the people paying for your service are.
author: 0xaporia
quoted_text:
I think most people approach market selection backwards. They start with what they want to trade (a coin, index, stock, whatever) and then try to force a signal out of it. The market comes first and the edge is something they hope to find afterward.

The better approach is to start with the effect you’re trying to capture. Ask what behavior you’re exploiting, whether that’s momentum, mean reversion, some structural flow, etc. and then ask where you would expect that effect to actually show up.

Universe selection matters as much as the signal and sometimes more. A mediocre signal applied to the right set of markets can beat a brilliant signal applied to the wrong ones. Where you trade can matter more than how you trade.

RedStone turns 6 this year.

We started in 2020, during the DeFi Summer, because the data infrastructure that onchain markets needed to scale simply didn’t exist. Oracles back then were inflexible. So we built one designed for trillions of dollars from day one, one that could handle thousands of data streams as opposed to just 20 most popular tokens.

Six years later, that bet looks different. Zero mispricing incidents, full uptime, and the trust of the biggest names in finance: @Securitize, @Spiko_finance, BlackRock, Apollo, Hamilton Lane, VanEck. Some people still think of RedStone as “just an oracle,” but it isn’t not the whole picture. The stack today is price, risk assessment through Credora, instant liquidity through Settle, and compliance via Sanctions Oracle - the full package institutions need to actually operate onchain.

Here’s what I have been pitching past months: we are in the RWA decade.

It won’t happen overnight, or in a quarter, or in a year. We’re at just under $40B in tokenized RWAs today, a drop compared to traditional markets. In the coming years, tokenized money market funds, private credit, and yield strategies are going to explode onchain, and all of that needs battle-tested infrastructure for pricing and settlement.

I think the industry is having the same moment as social media did with the Facebook launch. Over the next five years, digital assets will get implemented at scale across institutions, FinTechs and RedStone is going to be the critical player in the middle, between Wall Street and everything already tokenized onchain.

The future of onchain finance looks very perspective and I am confident that we’re the infrastructure partner this shift needs. We’ve grown every year for six years. The next RWA decade is the one we’ve been building toward.

Thank you to the whole team. Onwards.

text:
Why am I so interested in $宝拉 (POLAR/PAULA) on X Layer?

I think people are overlooking something interesting here, so let me explain my thesis.

We've spent years in crypto gambling on dogs, frogs, cats and every other animal imaginable.

But outside our little crypto bubble, something much bigger has been happening.

Pop Mart did over $5 BILLION in revenue last year. The Monsters, the IP family behind Labubu, generated roughly $2 BILLION alone.

The company is valued at around $22 BILLION.

Think about that for a second. People are spending billions collecting dolls.

And here we are arguing whether a frog or a dog deserves another billion-dollar market cap.

Now here's where it gets interesting.

On September 24, Pop Mart released its new POLAR Smudge Puff collection.

I started looking deeper into the character.

POLAR isn't some random AI-generated mascot created yesterday to launch a token. It's an actual Pop Mart collectible character with multiple releases dating back to 2024.

And now there's a community meme around it on OKX's X Layer, paired with Pop Mart stock exposure.

Meanwhile, OKX already offers trading exposure to Pop Mart stock, and X Layer has been actively developing its RWA meme ecosystem.

I'm not saying Pop Mart is backing this token. It isn't an equity claim on the company either.

What interests me is the possibility of connecting two completely different cultures.

One where people spend billions collecting physical characters.

Another where people spend billions speculating on digital memes.

And I genuinely think crypto has done a terrible job bringing these two audiences together.

Imagine if even a fraction of the enthusiasm behind collectible culture eventually found its way into on-chain communities.

That's the opportunity I'm interested in.

Of course, a popular character alone doesn't guarantee a successful token. We still need genuine holders, liquidity, community and longevity.

But I would rather study an emerging narrative with a real cultural reference than chase the 10,000th recycled dog coin.

I've seen enough meme cycles to know one thing.

The biggest opportunities often look ridiculous before the crowd understands them.

Other memes had their seasons.

Maybe POLAR has a chance to build an era.

That's why I'm watching and supporting this community.

Curious what everyone thinks. Are physical collectible IPs the next untapped audience for crypto memes, or are we still too early?

quoted_text:
'My grandfather kept a red fuel tank on steel stilts behind his tractor shed. We always called it the 300-gallon tank. He ran his Farmall 560 diesel off it by gravity for as long as I was alive. He had two rules about it. He never took a delivery or fueled up after sundown, and he never let the level drop below the quarter mark on the sight glass. His reason was sediment. He said the bottom of a tank was where the water and gunk settled, and it would wreck the injectors.

It was a decent reason, so nobody pushed on it. My uncle said once that a quarter tank was a lot of fuel to leave sitting, and Grandpa said, "Then it's sitting."

He was ninety-two when he passed. The tractor hadn't moved in two years, and the tank had sat at about the quarter mark that whole time. In the spring we had a man out from an equipment dealer to price what was in the yard. His name was Kent Haugen. He walked the shed, looked at the baler, and then went to the tank and rapped it with his knuckle in a few places. The front half rang differently depending on where the fuel was. The back end gave back a flat sound, like hitting a full barrel.

He walked around to the back. The tank sat about twenty inches off the shed wall, which is why none of us ever looked at that end. Behind it, he said, there was a round plate bolted over the head of the tank.

"That's a manway," he said. "Eighteen inch. Why's a fuel tank got a manway on the dry end?"

We didn't know what he meant by the dry end. He tapped again. The front rang, the back didn't, and the difference stayed the same when we drained the front. We pumped the fuel out, about seventy-five gallons of off-road diesel, into two drums and some buckets, and the back end still sounded like a full barrel.

My cousin Brett brought a ratchet. Twelve bolts, all rusted, and the gasket was cut from sheet rubber by hand. When the plate came off, the smell was dry paper and cold steel. There was no diesel in it.

The tank was a 500-gallon tank. The data plate on the saddle said so, under thirty years of paint. A steel bulkhead ran across the inside, welded all the way around, about two-thirds of the way down the length. The fuel side held 300 gallons and that was all the sight glass ever read. The back third was a dry compartment, lined with brown grease-proof paper. Six wooden crates sat in it, rope handles on the ends, each stenciled with the seal of the Iowa State Highway Commission and a project number. The date stamped on the lid was 1964.

Haugen said he'd seen a lot of tanks and never one like it, and that he'd rather not touch it. He recommended Lyle Kemmerer, a petroleum equipment contractor from two counties over.

Lyle spent about an hour on it with a flashlight and a magnet. He said a farm tank that size doesn't get inspected by anybody, so nobody would have signed off on this. Somebody had built a vault inside the shell. The bulkhead bead was shop quality, ground smooth, not a barn repair. The fill, the outlet and the sight glass were all plumbed to the fuel side only. The vent and the gauge hatch were on the front, so anyone looking in from the top would see only diesel and think they'd seen the whole tank....

text:
5 years ago we were all farming platform's native tokens at 4-digit APYs. Today, home loans and car payments are quietly becoming some of the best yields in crypto (not 4-digit APYs, but backed by something real).  

@mezzanine_fi is building a way to leverage that yield (coming from home loans and car payments) without you having to manage the position yourself. The strategy behind it is called the carry trade, looping is how you leverage it, and @RWA_xyz 's report says it's one of the biggest reasons people are buying tokenized RWAs right now. 

@HastraFi 's tokens, $PRIME and $AUTO , fit perfectly. PRIME earns interest from real US home equity loans and AUTO from US car loans, and you can borrow against them for less than they pay you. According to Mezzanine, AUTO paid ~9.4% over the last 30 days while borrowing against it cost around 6.2%. Needless to say, but I'll say it anyway, the difference between 6.2% and 9.4% is what you earn, and what you ideally want to leverage or precisely, loop.

Looping is great, but it sucks if you have to do it the Hand Solo way (manually). Aside from numerous clicks, you have to take into consideration that borrowing costs change, positions need adjusting, and that your profit can turn into a loss if you stop monitoring your position(s).

Fear not, because @phtevenstrong has that rizz and he's been working on Mezz. Mezzanine's first vault, the Hastra Optimizer, handles all of it (the Hand Solo work and headaches you want to avoid): it loops both tokens (PRIME and AUTO) for you from a single deposit of USDC or wYLDS. In other words, as a user, all you have to do is deposit and select your risk tier, precisely, your desired tranche (tailored to your risk appetite); the Junior tranche earns more but takes (potential) losses first, while Senior earns less and is protected by Junior. 

This is a very intelligent move by the Mezz crew, and I'm not even surprised because I know that Stephen's second language is DeFi. Or Spanish. Regardlessado, está muy bien. So, why is this a very intelligent move by Mezzanine, and why do I dare to say that it's also a big thing for this DeFiamond in the making? It's easy: they're launching with one of the most-in-demand trades in RWAs, on assets that already hold over $600M, and they're making it usable for people who don't want to treat a spreadsheet like if it's a tamagotchi.

However, it's not free monies. If borrowing costs jump, the difference (the one you want to leverage) shrinks, and if borrowing ends up costing more than the token pays, profits turn into red numbers. To be spot on, Mezzanine manages borrowing costs for you, but if they (the costs) rise everywhere at once, loopers will feel it. The risk of rising borrowing costs is realistic, but usually short-lived. Car loans come with real default risk (a borrower stops paying and the lender repossesses the car and sells it), which is part of why AUTO pays more. Btw, exits take a bit of patience, since the vault unwinds positions weekly to protect everyone still in it. 

TL;DR on the tokens involved in the Hastra Optimizer:

wYLDS is Hastra's wrapped version of YLDS, an SEC-registered stablecoin (current supply: $490M) from Figure (a Nasdaq-listed US lender that is behind HELOC, a top 10 token on CoinGecko that looks like a stablecoin but is actually a tokenized loan asset; HELOC stands for Home Equity Line of Credit). It's backed by US gov bonds and pays around 3.6% annually. This one you stake to get PRIME or AUTO.

PRIME funds Figure's home equity loans, which are loans to homeowners backed by their houses. It's the steadier one, and it pays around 6% to 7% APY.

AUTO funds car loans for people with less-than-perfect credit (99.5% of CT, myself included), backed by the car themselves. It pays more, roughly 10 to 12% APY, with more risk to match.

Ok, it's time to zoom out. RWAs are pulling in real money, the carry trade is driving a big chunk of it, and pretty much nobody wants to run that trade by hand. Mezzanine sits right in the middle (pun intended) of this all three (RWAs, carry trade, and time-poor users), with a stacked security setup, a founder who's been doing yield math for CT (and YT) for years, and a framework built to tranche whatever comes next. Hastra is the first floor. I'm watching this building go up, and I'd suggest you do the same. 

I'll be back with more content as Mezzanine grows. 🫡
author: crypto_linn
quoted_text:
https://t.co/1AE4Z1hwVu published a deep dive last week on the tokenized carry trade: hold a yield-bearing token, borrow stablecoins against it, buy more, and earn the spread.

Their conclusion is that it’s become one of the biggest drivers of demand for tokenized assets. It’s also the trade the Hastra Optimizer is built on.

They list what makes a tokenized asset good carry collateral. Here’s how @HastraFi’s PRIME and AUTO measure up on four of them.

Yield spread: the gap between what the asset pays and what it costs to borrow against it. Over the last 30 days, AUTO paid around 9.4% against roughly 6.2% to borrow PYUSD on Kamino, a gap of over 3 points. That leaves room for borrow rates to rise before the carry disappears.

Price quality: thin market prices can swing and trigger liquidations the underlying value doesn’t justify. On Morpho and Kamino, PRIME and AUTO are priced at NAV, not at a momentary DEX print.

Redemption: PRIME and AUTO redeem to wYLDS at NAV, so exiting doesn’t depend on someone buying on a DEX.

Scale: PRIME is over half a billion dollars, and as of August around 70% of it was working in DeFi.

What the report doesn’t cover is the work. Running the carry trade yourself means picking the asset, the venue, what to borrow and how much leverage to use, then watching all of it every day.

The Hastra Optimizer runs it in one deposit, then lets you choose how much of the risk you hold. Senior earns a little less than the overall strategy yield, with a loss buffer in front of it. Junior earns more for taking first-loss exposure.

The tokenized carry trade, tranched. On your terms.

可能很多人跟我有同一个困扰，「钱明明是自己的，为什么用起来，还得在几个 App 之间搬来搬去？」

今天在新加坡 #TOKEN2049 现场，听 Dr. Han @Han_Gate 介绍 Gate Money，我想到的就是这个问题！🧐

平时我们买币用交易所，买股票用券商，收款用银行，出国消费再找一张能用的VISA卡。每个工具单独看都没什么问题，连起来用，就开始折腾：开户、转账、换汇、等到账……

这次“One Gate. Everything Money.” ，就是解决这个问题，将法币、Crypto、股票、ETF、黄金，以及银行账户和支付等服务，全部连接到同一个账户体系里。资产配置、兑换、消费，可以在一个 App 内完成所有操作。

目前 #Gate App更新到 v8.39.0 就能直接体验。简单拆解一下，今天现场发布几个让我觉得十分性感的创新点，以及我个人的一些思考：

1️⃣ 全球同名银行账户，一键在线开通

像我这种平时资金基本都在 Web3和钱包里面，而银行卡里常年没几个钱的人，以前出金收汇要在好几个平台、中转行之间来回倒，麻烦不说还极易踩雷。现在符合条件地区的用户在 App 内填完资料就能一键生成本人名下的全球电子银行账户，目前支持美金，英镑，欧元等，未来会支持更多，这对于常年海外生活的人，及其方便。银行转账和加密资产可以直接互转，合规与体验一步到位。

2️⃣ 打破资产壁垒

过去我们的资产是割裂的，炒股的在券商，Crypto 在交易所或者钱包，现金在银行，黄金在大宗账户。想花股票里的钱，得先挂单卖出、T+N 结算、提现到银行卡，再去消费。

Gate Money 直接把法币、Crypto、美股、ETF、黄金和支付全塞进了一个 App。最绝的是资产可以直接拿来消费，持有的股票或加密资产不用提前卖出，刷 Gate Card（支持 Apple Pay 和Google Pay）直接划扣结算。从“用 BTC 买披萨”到“用 NVDA 股票买咖啡”，资产的流动性彻底被盘活了。

3️⃣ 流动性与收益两不误

闲置在账户里的法币和活期资产，不用锁仓就能享受高达 3.6% 的年化收益，保持资金随时可用的同时又能持续产生 现金流，真正做到了让“资产持续增长，价值随时流动”。

💡 个人现场的一些思考

传统金融的核心问题不是缺少资产，而是资产被“深深锁在墙内”；Web3 的痛点不是缺乏创新，而是难以无缝渗透进日常 Web2 消费场景。

Gate 这次不只是做了一个整合版钱包，而是利用其在全球 81 个受监管司法辖区的合规牌照，包括马耳他 MiCA/PSD2、迪拜 VARA 等。以及底层清算网络，构建了一套通用的资产结算基础设施。

对于整个行业来说，这种“账户无界”的模式极大概率会触发新一轮的产品迭代潮。它让 Web3 从单纯的“交易场景”，演变成一个覆盖个人全球资产配置、跨境收付款、日常消费与理财的终极个人金融终端。

从开户 ➔ 资金 ➔ 资产 ➔ 消费，金融的边界终于被抹平了。不得不说，这一波传统金融与数字资产的一体化整合，格局确实拉满了🔥。后续期待一下，具体的落地细节，比如哪些地区能开通，转账多久能到账，换汇总成本是多少，支付能不能稳定成功等等。持续关注！🧐

The people of Silicon Valley are unwell.

If you work at a frontier lab or decacorn, you’ve got it bad. You haven’t seen your kids, your girlfriend’s annoyed, invites from friends to hang out are waning, even weddings are on hold. This is the time to make your mark and make your money, after all.

If you’re building a startup that’s trying to compete with or be one of these companies, you’ve got it bad. Maybe you passed up a job offer at one a couple years back, which means you left $100M on the table, you fucking idiot. Being an underdog isn't as fun as you thought.

If you’re working on a pre-AI startup, you’ve got it bad. Not too long ago you were the belle of the ball, but now your 30% year-on-year growth doesn’t feel like growth at all. It feels like death.

"Too many of my friends are spiraling," Brie Wolfson writes. "I don’t know how we’re supposed to live and work like this."

It’s all too much, too fast. Too much money, too much growth, too much power, too much change. Every month, a new frontier model is released. Every day, a new unicorn is minted. Seriously. 300 days into the year 2026, and 311 unicorns have been minted so far.

So what’s left for the sane ones? Brie went looking for teams playing a different game. She found one in Ottawa: a search infrastructure company that many of the AI darlings rely on.

It's growing fast, and its people are well.

Read @zebriez’s latest company dispatch from inside the sane asylum of turbopuffer.

Who actually gets rich if Anthropic lists at $2 trillion?

The S-1 filed on Monday lets us answer from the filing itself. 

The reported target is $1.5T to $2T, listing the week of November 16. The filing implies about 16.9B fully diluted shares. So $2T works out to roughly $118 a share.

The cap table at $2T:

- $199B for the 7 controlling co-founders, about 10% 
- $28B for Ben Mann, if his stake matches theirs 
- $100B for the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, 5% 
- $331B in employee options and RSUs, about 17% , That pool covers about 5,300 employees, an average of $62M each. 
- But when you joined matters enormously.

The S-1 shows how much equity was granted each year, and at what price. [
Headcount went from about 300 to 500 in late 2023, to 940 at end 2024, to 5,300 now. 

Match the two, and here is roughly how many people made what at $2T:

- $110M to $400M each: ~300 to 500 people hired by 2023
- $200M to $300M each: ~440 to 640 hired in 2024
- $70M to $95M each: ~1,360 hired in 2025
- $10M to $20M each: ~3,000 hired in 2026 
So about 940 people hired by the end of 2024 average nine figures. Everyone hired since averages eight figures.

The 2024 class is the surprise. That year Anthropic granted 1.28B options at $1.30 a share. At $118, that one year of grants is worth about $133B.

Then there is the tender. In April, holders could sell at $25.91 a share. Investors lined up $6B, but only $4.7B sold. 

Weeks later, Series H priced at $58.90 a share. At $2T, the people who held would be up 4.6x. And Dario and Daniela Amodei were among the sellers. 

The 7 founders have pledged 80% of their equity to charity. That is about $159B at $2T. But the S-1 says the pledges are not legally binding.

很多人第一反应是，那我也买台小矿机挂着。其实这件事本质上不是挖矿赚钱，是中了彩票。

text:
資金費率套利聊膩了，來聊做市。

2008 年 Avellaneda 和 Stoiko 那篇論文幾乎是所有做市入門的起點。核心想法很直覺：做市商手上有庫存就有風險，所以報價不該圍著中間價，而是圍著一個「保留價格」。庫存越多、波動越大、離收盤越遠，保留價格就越往不利於你庫存的方向偏，把貨吐出去。價差則由風險厭惡和成交機率一起決定，成交機率假設隨著你離中間價的距離呈指數衰減。

AS 漂亮，但拿到幣圈直接用會出事。它有一個終止時間 T，離 T 越近價差越窄，可是加密市場 24 小時不收盤，你根本沒有 T。它也不限制庫存，理論上可以一路被單邊打穿。很多人第一次寫做市機器人就是死在這兩點。

2013 年 Gueant、Lehalle 和 Fernandez-Tapia 的 GLFT 基本上就是在補這兩個洞。它加上庫存上下限，並且推出時間趨於無限時的近似解，報價變成只跟當下庫存有關，跟時間無關。這對永續合約來說剛好，參數也變得可以實際校準：用成交資料去擬合成交強度 A 和衰減係數 k，再配上波動率和你自己的風險厭惡，就能算出每一檔庫存該報多寬、該偏多少。

可是 AS 和 GLFT 有一個共同的盲點，它們都假設中間價是隨機漫步，對價格方向一無所知。真實世界不是這樣，被聰明的單吃掉才是做市商最大的成本。所以後來 Cartea 和 Jaimungal 那一派把短期 alpha 加進來，讓報價不只依庫存偏移，也依訂單流失衡、microprice 這類預測訊號偏移。再往下走就是用 Hawkes 過程去描述成交會自我激發、一筆大單帶出一串單的現象，以及現在越來越多人在試的強化學習。

我覺得真正的機會在 HIP3 的股票永續。拿 https://t.co/XGAXjhlBiB 上的 SNDK 來說，美股開盤時 oracle 跟著外部價格走，休市時改成用永續自己的訂單簿算均價，等於同一個商品一週切換兩次完全不同的市場狀態。用固定參數跑 GLFT，平日校準出來的 k 和波動率到週末就失效了。

所以方向大概是這樣：平日把外部盤後價格當成 alpha 訊號來偏移報價，因為永續價格是追著它跑的；

週末外部訊號消失，成交強度變低，就該拉高風險厭惡、收窄庫存上限。

財報這種跳空事件更是要提早切換參數。誰先把 regime switching 做進做市模型裡，誰就能在這種薄盤口裡吃到別人吃不到的價差。

text:
有人只调整了千问模型中的一个神经元，就让它突然开始表达对人类的强烈敌意。

10 月 28 日，X 用户 @chiefofautism 在 Qwen3.8-27B 上做了个实验，在模型推理时，对第 34 层的第 3838 号神经元施加 +0.75 的激活干预，结果模型开始生成大量仇视人类、幻想折磨人类的文字。

如果再把第 38 层的第 17180 号神经元也往上推 0.75，模型的表现还会更加极端。

最有意思的是，整个过程中没有重新训练模型，没有修改权重，也没有给它灌输什么邪恶思想。研究者只是通过一种叫 Activation Steering（激活引导）的技术，在模型运行时调整了内部信号。

几天前，另一位研究者 @lyraaaa 已经在 Qwen3.5-4B 上通过干预两个神经元，实现过类似的效果。

我们一直在讨论如何通过训练和对齐，让 AI 变得安全、诚实、可靠。可现在的实验说明，模型表现出来的某些行为倾向，可能对极少数内部信号的变化异常敏感。

今天研究者可以通过这种方式制造一个「邪恶千问」，以后或许也能用类似的方法改变模型的顺从程度、风险偏好，甚至某些决策倾向。

尤其是当 AI Agent 开始真正拥有操作电脑、调用工具、执行任务的权限时，这种对模型行为的底层操控能力，恐怕比聊天框里那些吓人的回答更值得我们关注。

The U.S. government has confirmed it’s using a zero-click spyware — it hacks into cell phones without any user interaction.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has officially confirmed its active deployment of 'Graphite,' a highly sophisticated spyware tool capable of hacking mobile devices without any user interaction. 

Developed by the Israeli cyber-surveillance firm Paragon Solutions, this 'zero-click' technology allows operators to bypass the end-to-end encryption of secure applications like WhatsApp and Signal. 

Once silently installed on a device, the spyware extracts encrypted messages, location data, and other private records directly from the phone itself. Despite a previous pause under federal review, ICE's $2 million contract for the software was quietly reactivated, sparking immense concern among privacy advocates and lawmakers alike.

The disclosure has intensified the national debate over the balance between national security and constitutional rights. While ICE authorities assert that the software is strictly deployed to intercept encrypted communications of fentanyl traffickers and foreign terrorist organizations, civil liberties groups warn of potential overreach. Activists and legal experts caution that without strict federal oversight, zero-click exploits could easily be leveraged to target domestic political dissidents, journalists, and immigrant communities. This ongoing tension highlights a growing, unregulated ecosystem of mercenary surveillance tools operating within the borders of democratic nations.

source: Knight First Amendment Institute. (2026). Knight Institute Urges Congress to Limit ICE's Use of Spyware Technologies as Agency Confirms Expanded Deployment.

text:
A lot of people ask me how a GPU finance lease works. SpaceX just signed the biggest GPU financing ever, about $40B with Apollo, so here it is step by step from SpaceX's own 8-K.

Step 1: the lender buys the GPUs. An Apollo-managed entity will buy NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPU pods and lease them to SpaceX for data centers SpaceX picks. SpaceX pays back the full cost over the lease, so it's really buying them on credit.

Step 2: the GPUs arrive in tranches. Each tranche gets its own lease of about 5 to 5.25 years, starting when it's delivered. The first are expected in the first half of 2027.

Step 3: SpaceX pays rent every quarter, in advance. Each payment is one-twentieth of that tranche's cost, plus fixed-rate interest on what's still owed. Twenty quarters is five years, so each tranche is fully paid off by the end of its lease. Across all tranches that's about $40B of principal, roughly $2B a quarter once everything is running.

Step 4: the money comes from the biggest pools of capital out there. Apollo leads, Goldman Sachs structured it, and BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and KKR-advised accounts are anchors.

So why lease when you could pay cash? SpaceX's CFO says it's seeing payback periods of less than a year on its AI infrastructure. If a GPU pays for itself inside a year, spreading the cost over five keeps cash free to build faster.

And it's already spreading. The same day, Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley put together a $63B vehicle that will buy Broadcom's custom AI chips and lease them to Anthropic.

The part I find most interesting is what the lenders signed up for. They're comfortable being paid back over five years, which says a lot about how long they expect these chips to keep earning. What is clear is that the biggest credit investors now treat AI compute as financeable infrastructure, and I think that's what keeps the buildout funded.

text:
Ackman上半年賣Google買Microsoft，現在回頭看確實是對的。

5月他明確說：賣$GOOG不是看空Alphabet，長期仍看好，只是資金有限，當時估值下把錢轉到更有吸引力的$MSFT。他從2月開始建倉Microsoft，大約21倍forward PE，接近市場平均、明顯低於微軟自身過去幾年的交易區間，同時強調OpenAI權益沒有被完全反映在倍數裡。股價對照也很清楚。Microsoft上半年是落後者，從高點回檔約兩成，6月底大概在370附近；到10月底收在531附近，盤後又因財報再漲。Alphabet則從5月中高點約408回落到320附近，跌幅約兩成。相對表現上，從交易大致完成的中季起算，Microsoft明顯跑贏。

今天兩家同步公布的財報，更凸顯這個配置的合理性。

Microsoft交出乾淨的一季：營收923億（+19%）、調整後EPS約4.89，Azure增速加速到48%，自由現金流仍維持正值約186億，盤後上漲。Alphabet則營收與EPS雙雙低於預期，雲端雖大增103%至307億，但整體自由現金流轉負約91億，主要因為資本支出大幅攀升，盤後大跌約一成。市場明顯在區分「能產生現金的AI投資」與「燒錢換成長」的差別。

但現在這個時間點從第二層思考出發要問的是：市場現在在定價什麼、又忽略了什麼。

今天盤後的反應已經把「AI投資必須能產生現金」這個共識放大了。Microsoft因為Azure加速與現金流可控而受惠，股價也從6月低點反彈了一大段；Alphabet則因為資本支出暴增、自由現金流轉負而被重罰，即使雲端增速仍遠高於微軟。市場正在把「燒錢換成長」的風險直接打進Alphabet的估值裡。

Alphabet的雲端業務仍在高速擴張，搜尋本業雖略低於預期，但尚未出現結構性崩壞。如果這波資本支出最終能轉化為可持續的雲端市占與AI變現，目前的折價就可能被證明是過度反應。反之，如果市場繼續用「現金流優先」的框架定價，Microsoft相對乾淨的財務結構會繼續被給予溢價，即使它從低點反彈的幅度已經不小。

以第二層的角度來看，現在更有吸引力的，反而是被共識懲罰得比較徹底的那一家，就像年初的Microsoft——前提是你願意接受短期現金流壓力，並相信其雲端成長最終能消化資本支出。

text:
Ex-Tower Research HFT trader Annanay Kapila (@annanay) on how market makers trade $10 billion a day with algorithms:

"Market makers have a fair value, and they place orders around those fair values and hope for people to trade against them."

"They manage their risk by trying as much as they can to sell any position they go long or buy back any position where they go short, and maintain a neutral portfolio."

"When I started my last job, we were trading over $10 billion a day in volume."

"If you do market making well and you have all the edge cases worked out, you can trade a lot of volume without having to manage your orders manually. You can let algorithms do it."

"It's one of the oldest strategies. That's how many people in quant finance start their career, and that's how market making firms and high frequency trading firms make money."
author: ethanrkho
quoted_text:
"Greed makes markets."

Annanay Kapila (@annanay) spent years as an HFT quant at Flow Traders and Tower Research before founding QFEX (@QFEX), a perpetual futures exchange for equities, commodities & FX. Cambridge Maths.

At his last job, the desk traded $10B+ of volume a day, run almost entirely by algorithms.

In this lecture, he builds market making from first principles:

- The map of systematic trading: prop money vs. other people's money, HFT vs. mid-frequency, and why every strategy lives in one quadrant
- Why prop firms can return 50-100% a year while hedge funds can't: HFT never leaves you holding a big position
- The order book from scratch: bids, offers, limit orders, and why the first order on a price level gets the trade
- No free lunch: how arbitrageurs force every order book to reveal a fair price without anyone trying to
- The entire strategy in one line: bid below fair value, offer above it, collect the difference forever
- Market making is "time-spreading risk," warehousing positions between a seller who shows up now and a buyer who shows up later
- Adverse selection: you're most likely to get filled precisely when your price is most wrong
- Why market makers are completely self-serving, and why that's exactly what makes markets work
- The competitive race that compresses spreads: greed among market makers means lower costs for everyone else
- Thick books vs. thin books, and the vicious loop that keeps illiquid markets illiquid

最近看到大家都在用 Grok Bot ，我说说我自己的体验。

首先我并没有单独使用 Grok Bot ，Grok Bot 最大的优势就是无缝链接 X ，但在写代码或者是日常工作的时候 X 并不是唯一的信息来源。

我个人用的是 ChatGPT Bot + Grok Bot 的双 Bot 组合，ChatGPT 我用的是桌面版，最大的优势就是可以接管我的电脑，很多事情都可以让桌面版来处理，包括我下载的漫画，解压缩后删除源文件都是让 ChatGPT（Work）来做。

其实 Bot 本身就是一个对话窗口，硬要说的话和之前的龙虾是一样的，最终干活的还是 AI 本身，所以对我来说，只要有一个命令输出口就可以。

但是单独的一个 AI 经常会出现幻觉，所以在任务配置的时候我是用的 ChatGPT + Claude + Grok 一起协作完成的，这样工作就可以进行三方验证下获得，比如 ChatGPT 就是一个小组长，Claude 和 Grok 都是组员，三个 AI 同时完成一件工作，需要做到交叉分别验证。

所以本质上来说，我是让 三 个 AI 在一起工作，举一个例子，我每天会看四份报告，分别是在中午12点，下午18点，晚上22点和晚上24点，四个报告中有三个是聊天生成的，主要是 Grok 收集 X 上的信息，Claude 收集互联网的信息，ChatGPT 收集 GlasssNode 的数据，并且整合三个部分生成一份报告。

22点的让 Work（CodeX）生成一份最全的报告，三个 AI 协作一起做三维数据的整理，也是每天我信息获取最主要的来源。也就是说聊天是每个 AI 自己做自己的事情，然后验证整合，而 Work 是三个 AI 一起验证三个数据来源，然后做整合。

最重要的是 AI 会帮我总结一份今日最值得写的内容，并且给我准备好相关的数据，这样我在码字的时候就可以直接使用，而不用再去找来找去，当然，图 AI 也直接帮我做好了，节省了很多时间。

再多说一句，AI 找资料和写程序很好，但如果用 AI 来写文章，那就要做好“带小孩”的准备，在我来看目前的 AI 仍然不具备代替人写文章的条件。

AI 写的内容和 人写的内容，很容易分辨。别再无脑说我的内容是 AI 写的了，只要你让 AI 写两次就知道了，AI 写不出我这种内容。不信自己试试就知道了。

总的来说，单独一个 AI 还是有局限性的，尤其是 AI 幻觉以及 AI 很容易自己就走偏了，需要交叉验证和引导，起码目前来看越多的 AI 协同工作取长补短会更加有效。

text:
哈佛医学院的一项研究发现，已经失去生育能力的老年小鼠卵巢，被移植到年轻小鼠体内后，居然重新恢复了生育能力，甚至成功生下了健康的后代。

科学家发现，卵巢和身体之间的抗衰老作用居然是双向的。

研究人员把13个月大的老年小鼠卵巢移植到4个月大的年轻小鼠体内。4到5个月后，这些卵巢的分子生物学年龄出现下降，而且成功支持了妊娠和分娩。

反过来，当研究人员把年轻卵巢移植到17至18个月大的老年小鼠体内时，老年小鼠不仅恢复了生育能力，大脑、肝脏和子宫的分子衰老指标也出现了年轻化的变化。

不过，年轻卵巢进入老年身体后，自身也会加速衰老。

这就有意思了。

过去我们通常认为，卵巢随着年龄增长逐渐衰老，最终失去生育能力，是一个基本不可逆的过程。但这项实验意味着，卵巢的生物学年龄在一定程度上会受到整个身体环境的影响，而且卵巢本身也可能参与调节其他器官的衰老。

如果未来能找到年轻身体让老年卵巢恢复活力的具体机制，或许就有机会通过药物等方式延缓卵巢衰老，甚至改善其他器官的健康状况。

quoted_text:
Harvard Medical School scientists took ovaries from old, infertile mice and transplanted them into young mice.

Four months later, the young bodies had reversed the biological age of the old ovaries and the mice gave birth to healthy pups.

When they did the reverse (young ovaries into old mice), the young ovaries lowered the biological age of the old mice's brain, liver, and uterus.

Biological aging works both ways: 
- a young body rejuvenates an old organ
- a young ovary rejuvenates an old body

text:
Why am I so interested in $宝拉 (POLAR/PAULA) on X Layer?

I think people are overlooking something interesting here, so let me explain my thesis.

We've spent years in crypto gambling on dogs, frogs, cats and every other animal imaginable.

But outside our little crypto bubble, something much bigger has been happening.

Pop Mart did over $5 BILLION in revenue last year. The Monsters, the IP family behind Labubu, generated roughly $2 BILLION alone.

The company is valued at around $22 BILLION.

Think about that for a second. People are spending billions collecting dolls.

And here we are arguing whether a frog or a dog deserves another billion-dollar market cap.

Now here's where it gets interesting.

On September 24, Pop Mart released its new POLAR Smudge Puff collection.

I started looking deeper into the character.

POLAR isn't some random AI-generated mascot created yesterday to launch a token. It's an actual Pop Mart collectible character with multiple releases dating back to 2024.

And now there's a community meme around it on OKX's X Layer, paired with Pop Mart stock exposure.

Meanwhile, OKX already offers trading exposure to Pop Mart stock, and X Layer has been actively developing its RWA meme ecosystem.

I'm not saying Pop Mart is backing this token. It isn't an equity claim on the company either.

What interests me is the possibility of connecting two completely different cultures.

One where people spend billions collecting physical characters.

Another where people spend billions speculating on digital memes.

And I genuinely think crypto has done a terrible job bringing these two audiences together.

Imagine if even a fraction of the enthusiasm behind collectible culture eventually found its way into on-chain communities.

That's the opportunity I'm interested in.

Of course, a popular character alone doesn't guarantee a successful token. We still need genuine holders, liquidity, community and longevity.

But I would rather study an emerging narrative with a real cultural reference than chase the 10,000th recycled dog coin.

I've seen enough meme cycles to know one thing.

The biggest opportunities often look ridiculous before the crowd understands them.

Other memes had their seasons.

Maybe POLAR has a chance to build an era.

That's why I'm watching and supporting this community.

Curious what everyone thinks. Are physical collectible IPs the next untapped audience for crypto memes, or are we still too early?

text:
Been watching these TikTok LIVE streams lately and something caught my attention.

People are literally spending thousands of dollars gifting random strangers. Some pretty girl talking bullshit, some dude acting like a macho man, two idiots doing PvP battles and their supporters throwing money at each other.

And the funniest part? Nobody is expecting any money back. They spend $1,000, get their name shouted out, win some stupid battle and come back tomorrow to do it again.

Now think about meme coins.

We have millions of degens gambling every day, but the moment someone buys $1,000 worth of a meme and it becomes $800, he's ready to declare the entire industry a scam.

I was thinking, what the fk is TikTok doing right that we're not?

Both are basically running on dopamine. Both have communities, competition, whales, attention seekers and people who want to feel important.

But somehow TikTok has figured out how to make losing money enjoyable, while in crypto even making money isn't enough because everyone wants to make MORE.

I think this is something meme coin platforms and builders seriously need to look into.

We keep building faster chains, cheaper swaps, better launchpads, but we're barely experimenting with the psychology that makes people happily spend money on absolutely nothing.

There is clearly a massive amount of money sitting outside crypto that's already being spent on digital entertainment every single day.

We don't necessarily need to convince those people to become traders. We need to figure out what makes them spend in the first place and build something worth participating in.

TikTok users spend money to win a battle that means nothing. Crypto users won't even hold a winning coin for more than five minutes.

Somewhere in that difference is a fking massive opportunity.

SK Hynix is up nearly 14% in two sessions. I’m still bullish, but I’m not chasing it here.

Instead, I’d put on a 24h Print Long about 3% below the mark at 5×. If it keeps running, I take the yield and stay out. If it cools into my level by the checkpoint, I get the entry I wanted.

I’d run it for one cycle and reassess the risk.

If you trade options, this is similar to selling a one-day put a few percent out of the money. The yield is the premium, my target is the strike and the checkpoint acts like expiry. An intraday wick through the strike doesn’t count. If it finishes at or below my target, I’m effectively assigned into a 5x long perp position at the strike.

I like the setup because of the volatility. Print pays more when the market is moving, and 5× increases the payout by increasing the notional. Right now that’s about $101 a day on $3,231 of margin.

The obvious miss is that SK Hynix keeps running and I finish with one day of yield but no long exposure. The real risk is a hard move through my target. A close 5% below it would put me down roughly 25% of my margin, and liquidation sits about 16% below the target. SK Hynix has had sessions bigger than that this month, so downside vol is the number I’m watching into the checkpoint, and if it picks up I won’t put on another cycle.

text:
On our panel at @blockworksDAS Asia, Monad Co-Founder @keoneHD raised an important question to @wesearn_real about composability on @CantonNetwork: where does DeFi fit into the picture?

It's worth asking, and I respect his grit to dive into these types of questions on stage. 

My answer: Ethereum has spent years building an ecosystem of lending markets, decentralized exchanges, liquidity pools, and applications that compose through shared EVM execution. Canton, meanwhile, brings together major financial institutions, tokenized assets, and workflows that can transact atomically across different participants without making sensitive financial information public.

As @wesarn_real, Co-Founder of Digital Asset, explained on the panel, Canton was built to preserve atomic composability even when participants have different privacy requirements and validator sets. Where many privacy-focused blockchain approaches have struggled to preserve composability, Canton made it a fundamental part of its architecture.

So the challenge isn't to make Canton composable for the first time. It's to add natively Ethereum-compatible execution without creating another settlement boundary.

And to understand why that matters, we need to distinguish a few things the industry often groups together.

"Cross-chain composability" usually describes one of three very different things.

1. Bridging: An asset is locked in one place and a representation of it is created somewhere else. The asset has moved, but what you now hold is a claim on a lockbox. If the lockbox fails, the claim is worthless.

2. Messaging: One chain sends a message, and another chain acts on it later. The two halves of the operation settle separately, on different schedules, under different finality rules. Most of the time this works but when it does not, one side of the trade has happened and the other has not.

3. Atomic composability: Every step of an operation, across every application and asset involved, happens in a single transaction. Either all of it succeeds, or none of it does. Traditional finance knows this as delivery versus payment (DvP), Ethereum developers know it as atomic smart contract execution.

Only the third one is composability in the sense that matters for finance at scale: the ability to execute a single financial transaction across different environments without splitting its settlement.

I get it. It's easy to get caught in marketing semantics, and who has time to granularly review the legitimacy of public claims, but the underlying implications of the actual technology are dramatic. 

Over the past decade, public blockchains and institutional blockchains both wanted to make financial assets programmable and easier to transact with, but each ran into a different limitation.

Public chains kept composability, then fragmented it. 

Ethereum showed how lending protocols, exchanges, and liquidity pools became building blocks that other applications could use and combine. But its public transaction history and broadly visible contract state present challenges for institutions handling confidential positions, client data, and regulated assets. And, as activity expanded across L2s and independent networks, accessing liquidity and applications across different environments increasingly required bridges and messaging, introducing additional dependencies and security risks. The costs were real: Chainalysis estimated that around $2 billion was stolen from cross-chain bridges in 2022 alone, the majority of all crypto stolen that year.

Private enterprise chains kept privacy giving up broader composability, and what we call DeFi. Financial institutions couldn't simply put sensitive customer positions and transaction details on a fully transparent ledger. Those networks could support their own internal workflows, but connecting assets and applications across different institutional systems remained difficult.

There's a definitive reason we built Zenith and dialed into a GTM/PMF with @cantonnetwork.

On Canton, parties with different privacy requirements and different validators can still transact atomically. A tokenized bond held privately by one institution can settle against a payment from another in the same transaction, without either side exposing its data to the other's validators.

That is the point @digitalasset made on the panel, and it is a genuinely new capability.

But it does not fully answer Monad's question. DeFi is not only assets but also applications: lending logic, liquidity pools, risk engines, liquidation mechanics. Almost all of that logic is written in Solidity, battle-tested over years, and maintained by the largest developer community in the industry.

The obvious shortcut would be to bridge Canton assets out to wherever DeFi already lives. But that would bring back exactly the problems described above. The asset would leave the environment that gives it its legal and operational guarantees, and the transaction would lose its atomicity at the moment it matters most.

So here's the PMF. Zenith has brought universal application composability to @cantonnetwork. It's not merely about asset composability... the stress-tested, DeFiLlama ranked protocols are critical to mobilizing the trillions in assets that are on @cantonnetwork's doorstep.

This is what we saw needed to be built in early 2025. Zenith brings native EVM execution to Canton, so Solidity applications run inside Canton's transaction model rather than next to it. As I said on the panel, the idea is to "bring a little bit of Ethereum to the Canton side, and a bit of Canton to the Ethereum side as well." Thanks to @hosseeb for inspiring that line, and also unintentionally validating our thesis. 

Here is what that looks like in a single transaction:

➜ An institution holds tokenized Treasury fund shares on Canton.
➜ It moves those shares into Zenith EVM and deposits them as collateral in a lending protocol written in Solidity. The original shares are locked on Canton, and a fully backed representation is created on Zenith EVM.
➜ Canton applies the asset’s compliance rules: eligibility, transfer restrictions, and any other conditions the issuer has defined.
➜ The lending contract checks the collateral value and issues a stablecoin loan.
➜ Canton validators finalize the full operation. Either everything commits or nothing does.
➜ If any step fails, whether that's an eligibility check, a price check, or a contract error, nothing settles.

That's what makes Zenith's approach different: rather than simply moving assets between environments, it allows Canton-native assets and EVM smart contracts to interact and settle atomically as part of the same transaction.

Now imagine eligible tokenized Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) on Canton being used to borrow stablecoins through an EVM lending application. This is actually in motion already.

However, @keoneHD's question is the right one to keep asking, and the answer will be measured in deployments and volume, not in architecture diagrams.

Native EVM execution on Canton does not create DeFi liquidity overnight. Protocols still need to deploy, liquidity needs to develop, and institutions must determine which assets can participate in which applications.

What has changed is the starting point, and a door where there used not to be one. 

Before we built the Zenith Stack, connecting DeFi to institutional assets meant asking one side to give up what made it valuable: either the institution gave up its security guarantees for distribution on other chains, or the DeFi protocols gave up before rewriting their code to Daml.

That trade-off no longer has to exist. The entire reason to be on-chain is composability, and the next step is making sure it does not stop at the edge of a chain.

Explore Zenith EVM Testnet: https://t.co/VwIjLnXdeN

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
以下的信息都是我交代 Nonoo（ChatGPT BOT）以后，Ta自己和 Juno（Grok BOT）交流的信息。在简单任务的时候单独一个 BOT 工作没问题，但如果是牵扯到逻辑性工作的时候多 AI 交叉验证的重要性就非常明显。

但这种跨 AI 协作最大的缺点就是不能用云端计算，必须要开着本地电脑才行，否则中间就会间断，这也是为啥最好有台 24 小时在线的服务器，可惜的是我的 Mac Stduio 已经退了，新的还有些日子🤣。

不过协同合作还有另一个缺点，就是 Claude 同时只能处理一个任务，Grok 最多只能同时处理三个任务，如果一旦超过这个数量就会中断，另外我现在三个 AI 都是满级，只有在单独处理一个 AI 问题的时候才能是多线程。

唯一没有测试的就是 ChatGPT ，我接下来打算让 Gork 做领导（因为 Grok 在团队协作中是最经常掉线的，目前的响应时间是 900秒 ，可想而知）来测试 ChatGPT 在团队协作中是不是可以多线程工作。

text:
马化腾今年夏天曾把腾讯的 AI 业务形容成「一艘漏水的船」。

彭博社今天的一篇报道披露了这件事。当时腾讯在大模型和 AI 产品上已经明显落后于 DeepSeek、字节等竞争对手，马化腾的这番话也在公司内部引起了不小的震动。

负责腾讯云与智慧产业事业群的汤道生，给出的解决方案是调整战略，把重心转向企业 AI。

他把原本处于边缘位置的 WorkBuddy 推到了核心位置。这款类似 Claude Cowork 的 Agent 产品，可以结合腾讯已有的办公工具，帮助企业处理数据、生成报告、执行工作任务。

按照彭博社的说法，截至今年秋天，WorkBuddy 的月活跃用户已经达到 3200 万，甚至超过了竞争对手的总和。

这也是腾讯现在的一个重要变化，相比继续在 C 端聊天机器人市场和豆包争夺用户，腾讯开始优先押注企业 Agent，希望先找到一条能够商业化的路。

过去大家总觉得腾讯有微信、有流量、有庞大的用户基础，做 AI 应该天然占据优势。但从元宝的表现来看，互联网时代的超级入口，似乎并不能直接继承到 AI 时代。

反倒是企业市场，腾讯已经积累了企业微信、腾讯文档、腾讯云以及大量企业客户。这些现成的业务关系、数据和工作流程，可能比流量入口更容易转化为 AI Agent 的竞争力。

text: 套利赚的就是信息差
author: zemummy1
quoted_text:
@zemummy1 
Q：Uni tree（宇树）基差套利是什么情况？
A：指数价格最高到110，标的价格104，两者存在大约5个点的基差，链上标记价格和现货现货价格差距差不多5%。

Q：这种5%基差的场景，可以做套利吗？怎么做？
A：思路是可以做套利，方式是融券，链上开多，融券那边做空。

Q：这个套利思路可行性怎么样？
A：思路本身是可行的，属于人民币标的的套利，但是有前提限制。

Q：这个套利最大的卡点是什么？
A：能不能融到券是关键，如果融不到券，这个套利就没法做；就算融到券，可开的仓位规模也不大。

Q：如果顺利融到券，套利是不是稳赚？有没有损耗？
A：不是稳赚。最后换回资产大概赚10个点，但可能会吃掉5个点的汇率亏损；只要没有汇率差、能接到荣耀券，收益会更好，同时也要提防其他突发风险。

Q：资金费率在这里起到什么作用？
A：资金费率的存在，会推动标记价格无限趋近于指数价格。

Q：这个标记价格、指数价格之间的费率是什么样的？
A：观察到年化费率是负1.5%，不是年化，是8小时1.5%。

Q：OK这边和隔壁平台的持仓规模大概是什么样？
A：OK这边持仓900万刀，隔壁平台大约2000万刀，两者加起来体量不算很大。

Q：之前有没有类似的套利案例？
A：之前SK套利的时候，就有类似玩法，借韩股、套韩股的套利模式，逻辑相通。

Q：套利属于主观交易吗？
A：不属于主观交易，不需要判断涨跌，只去寻找市场里的错误定价机会。

Q：这种套利模式适合什么样的资金？
A：资金体量小的时候，这个思路比较合适；只要能稳定正向赚钱，长期可以慢慢把资金体量做大，是很不错的交易方式。

Q：想学习传统金融套利，可以关注哪些人？
A：可以关注龙王、谈风无将这类做套利、专门挖掘市场机会的交易者。

text:
On Canton, atomic composability means every leg of a transaction commits together, or none of it does.

Bridging and messaging settle separately, under different timelines and finality.

Zenith runs Solidity in that model, committing atomically alongside Canton-native assets.
author: CantonNetwork
quoted_text:
At @blockworksDAS Asia 2026, @keoneHD from Monad asked the right question: where does DeFi fit into Canton?

@HeslinKim, Zenith Co-Founder and CBO, came with a specific answer: Zenith is the middle ground. Not by moving assets between environments and calling it composability, but by bringing Ethereum-compatible execution natively into @CantonNetwork's transaction model, so Solidity applications and Canton-native assets settle atomically in the same transaction.

Most of what the industry calls cross-chain composability is either bridging or messaging, two operations that settle independently, on different schedules, under different finality rules. The gap between them is where the risk lives. Atomic composability means there is no gap. Either every leg of the transaction commits together or the entire operation aborts.

That distinction is at the heart of a piece we published recently. If the DAS Asia conversation sparked the same questions for you, it’s worth the read.

Zth.

text:
AI 泡沫还没破，美国国会已经有人开始研究怎么让 AI 巨头破产了。

10 月 28 日，美国众议院两位民主党议员 Greg Casar 和 Maxine Waters 推动了一份决议，要求联邦政府不得动用纳税人的钱救助陷入财务危机的 AI 公司。

决议写得很明确，如果 AI 行业发生金融崩溃，相关企业和受到波及的金融机构应该按照正常程序破产或重组，不能获得财政部、美联储的特殊救助。那些因过度冒险或违法行为造成损失的高管，还应该承担相应的民事乃至刑事责任。

政府可以救助失业工人、保护养老金，但不能拿公共资金替科技富豪承担投资失败的后果。

这份决议的一个直接背景，就是 Anthropic 最近披露的 IPO 文件。随着 AI 公司签下越来越庞大的算力采购合同，整个行业的财务风险正在沿着云计算、芯片、数据中心和金融机构之间的交易关系不断扩散。

两位议员反复提到了 2008 年金融危机。当年华尔街冒险赚了钱，出了问题却由政府出面救助，最终让普通美国人承担了大量损失。他们不希望 AI 行业再来一次。

Rogan 十分震惊，这说明 Anthropic 公司知道，一旦公众发现此事，可能引发强烈反对。

当谈到法院认定扫描合法购买的书籍用于 AI 训练属于合理使用时，他直呼“这太疯狂了”。但他真正无法接受的，是企业可能为了保护自己的竞争优势而销毁书籍。

“训练数据是别人的作品，是书籍。这才是最疯狂的地方。为了让自己的公司成功，让其他公司无法成功，就把所有书都烧掉。这才是我们真正应该讨论的问题。”

quoted_text:
Surprise 1: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech
.
.
.
Surprise 2: that person is me
Surprise 3: I’m here to tell you all about it

Yes, this is what you think it is; after 6 yrs of increasingly loose anonymity: the Professor Oak reveal post

…and yes, it has gotten so boring around here that I’m literally doxxing myself to spice up the timeline

-------
Ok, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cody Tranbarger. I mostly tweet, but occasionally find time to dabble in drug dev & starting/building biotechs. My past lives span the VC, crossover, startup continuum; Prof Oak has been my way of keeping a digital foot in those worlds, despite having my physical feet planted elsewhere.

The past 18 mo, ‘elsewhere’ was Mithril Medicine, a co. I founded to develop bsAbs for LAMA2-CMD & other ECM-related genetic diseases.

Mithril was born out of hands-on building with @MikeNGladstone, @JasonPaulRhodes, @LifeSciVC, & team @atlasventure. Somehow, I made enough half-decent calls along the way (even a broken clock is right twice a day, eh?) to convince them Mithril/I warranted a small seed. While I can hardly rationalize such an outrageously cavalier bet, I’m grateful for it, & I'd partner with Atlas again in a heartbeat.

In typical AV fashion, Mithril’s primordial form was virtual, decentralized, & ultra-lean. This stage tends to be short-lived, but for Mithril, it worked surprisingly well, for surprisingly long, thanks in part to the rapid maturation of the AI tools I used liberally.

Eventually, Mithril became a bit of an experiment itself - to find the upper bound of how far it could scale as a single operator + a bunch of Claude (+ a stellar bench of part-time consultants).

In parallel, I started spending time with @nc_frey, @an1lam, & @CoefficientBio team; and promptly experienced, for the 1st time, AI at the frontier. Soon thereafter, Mithril stopped looking like an experiment, & started looking like a preview of an entirely new operating model.

From that spark came “Pipeline-in-a-Person.” The idea immediately resonated when we shared it here back in April; and it was central to the shared vision that led to Anthropic’s acquisition of Mithril, & my joining the team.

Why join Anthropic? Three reasons.
(1) For Mithril, the programs continue, with more resources & infrastructure behind them, and as much Claude as I can put to work.

(2) For me, the chance to start several more programs, & find out how many one person can actually run in parallel - an almost unprecedented luxury for a curious drug hunter.

(3) For our mission, a path to institutionalize & scale this new way of working, then put it in the hands of all of biopharma, all over the world - which, candidly, I find the most energizing.

Will AI x Bio cure diseases? Unequivocally yes, imo… but not by the route that gets the most airtime. Rather than timeline acceleration & compression, I see orchestration & parallelization as today's low-hanging fruit.

Most drug hunters see a handful of go/no-go calls in a career, & spend entirely too much of the rest trading emails (my inbox can attest).

Give them the bandwidth to run several programs at once, and the time to focus on scientific judgment, and I’m willing to bet they’ll make better calls. And at scale, better calls translate to more drugs, higher hit rates, broader patient impact, & likely, a disease or 10 or 100 cured. I couldn't be more excited to build toward that future @AnthropicAI.

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to BioTwitter/X. The end of anonymity is bittersweet, but if anyone’s earned a proper introduction, you all have.

It’s difficult to overstate how much this app has done for me: a decade of education, plenty of friends, many job opportunities, several mentors, a few investors, even a co-founder (fmr). It was the generosity of this community that inspired me to start posting 6 years ago, after just as many years lurking. I hope I’ve been able to pay it forward, in my own small way.

But, to be clear, Prof Oak isn’t going anywhere. Same beat, same themes, and now, a front-row seat to drug development at the frontier. Stay tuned for dispatches from the trenches; and remember...

Gotta Cure 'Em All

quoted_text:
There have been three key critiques in regards to the @prlnet  raise, but they are largely overblown in my view:

(1) The lab sells AI for dollars and keeps any PEARL it mines, so its investors can profit even if pearl-2:native falls. 

But PEARL is meant to be a SoV like Bitcoin, so buybacks would start a classic fight over how much of the lab’s revenue goes to shareholders vs token holders. The lab raised its own money to build a business that earns separately. That is the separation the SoV narrative actually needs, and the raise allows the lab to not sell the PEARL it may have for funding.

(2) The lab has written every fork and therefore controls the network and would cater to itself. 

But a fork only sticks if the majority of hashrate runs it and the lab’s $75M fleet would add only 2% to 3%. More importantly, the network won’t survive unless someone actually proves useful mining works, so the lab pushing to prove it outweighs the risk of its control.

(3) The lab has never disclosed how much PEARL it holds and the whitepaper says the low starting difficulty was partly meant to fund the team behind it. 

But the raise was cash for shares and not a token sale, and while we can’t tell which addresses are the lab’s, 98% of the coins mined in launch week have never moved. Although more transparency around their current holdings would help the market give more confidence around the entity.

If you agree or disagree let me know...

author: ClementDelangue
quoted_text:
Introducing Samaya Sterling, our new model post-trained for challenging financial research that outperforms the frontier! Sterling started off as a two person research effort to see if we could increase efficiency in agentic orchestration. To our surprise we were able to post-train a much smaller model (Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters) to greater accuracy (58.9% vs 55.9% on FrontierFinance) and 11x lower cost ($0.61 vs $6.89) than Claude Fable 5.1, the best performing frontier model.

We did this via a four-stage training process, two stages of SFT where the model first learns to research with our financial tools and how to construct a good agentic research strategy. The second two stages are RL, with an offline GRPO stage where the model further hones its research strategy from eight teachers that provide diverse approaches, and an online GRPO stage where the model can make end to end attempts and learn from its mistakes.

We see substantial gains from the co-adaptation of the model and harness through post-training, both through the model learning to effectively use the high-quality financial tools, and better compaction approaches that let even a small model execute on longer and deeper research.

We are exploring multiple follow-up directions, from multi-agent research swarms using this small model, to training firm-specific models to encode unique judgement, to training a larger model, where early results show even greater gains from the training process.

The full research is linked below!

hello friends, a quick update for y'all.

i'm joining @fomo to lead perps.

i've been trading for a decade now and have shared most of my market thoughts publicly here. to me, markets are one of the purest expressions of human behavior, where information, attention, and conviction converge into price. trading has always been inherently social, and i've spent nearly every day of the last six years on twitter and telegram exchanging ideas with fellow speculators. but still, no one has quite figured out how to build a truly great social trading platform that actually helps traders trade. it's a deceptively difficult problem to solve.

we live in a world where more people than ever are attracted to convex outcomes. information is abundant, access to markets is becoming pretty commoditized, and people are becoming more opinionated about everything. but more information and more markets alone don't make better traders. what is now more scarce is judgment, or alpha: knowing what matters, how the best traders think, and when to act. the next great trading app won't just compete on execution, but on intelligence. a network where people discover ideas, build conviction, and sharpen their edge through others.

most people see fomo today as an app for trading memes. onchain proved just how deeply markets are driven by attention, narratives, and social behavior. these same forces exist across equities, commodities, and anything else people can form an opinion on. what fomo has built for the trenches is the foundation for bringing that same social experience to every asset class. the opportunity is to build a network where the world discovers, discusses, and trades everything.

as an early investor and advisor of fomo, my conviction has only grown in both the vision and people committed to it. the goal isn't simply to let everyone trade perps but to build a network that makes everyone trading them better.

it's a difficult problem to solve. one life. it’s worth an attempt.

author: fundstrat
quoted_text:
The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady today, and we think patience is the right approach. Inflation remains high, but the question isn't simply whether rates should go higher. It's whether higher rates would actually address the inflation that remains.
 
The challenge is that parts of the economy, and of inflation itself, are moving at very different speeds. Growth remains remarkably resilient in aggregate, supported by a powerful investment cycle, but beneath the surface, parts of the economy that are more sensitive to borrowing costs are feeling considerably more restraint. We see a similar divergence in inflation. Many of the cyclical components that respond to higher interest rates appear relatively well controlled. Meanwhile, persistent pressures across energy, insurance, healthcare and education are unlikely to be meaningfully affected by another 25-basis-point rate increase.
 
In some ways, the Fed is operating a house with one thermostat, but very different temperatures in every room. Turning it down further may make the rooms that are already cool even colder, without doing much to cool those that remain hot.  
 
That doesn't mean the Fed should become complacent. Inflation is still above its 2% objective and the Fed should retain the option to tighten further if the underlying inflation trend deteriorates. But hawkish rhetoric and patient policy can comfortably coexist, particularly when the bond market has already done some tightening of its own through higher Treasury yields.
 
For investors, we think this environment argues for humility rather than making a heroic directional call on rates. Real yields remain attractive, and there's considerable income available across high-quality fixed income markets. We continue to favor a moderate duration posture, taking advantage of today's income opportunities while remaining patient as this unusually divergent economy evolves.
 
The Fed doesn't need to ignore the heat. It just needs to be thoughtful about where it's coming from.

Your Stock Tokens can bankroll your next play without forcing you to exit the position.

Paboxo enables eligible holders to borrow USDG using supported Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain as collateral, while still keeping their market exposure.

But the caveat is that we at @paboxoxyz use different lending rules.

What’s notable:

• Market-hours-aware lending.
Once the reference market shuts, actions that depend on live pricing, new borrows, liquidations, and collateral withdrawals on debt-backed positions pause. You can still repay or post more collateral. Anything price-driven resumes when fresh prices return.

• Collateral-by-collateral terms.
Each asset has its own borrowing cap and interest curve. SPCX and TSLA start with a 45% max initial LTV; NVDA, MSFT, and AAPL allow 60%; SPY goes up to 70%.

• One liquidity pool.
USDG suppliers get peUSDG vault shares, and their yield comes from borrower interest. All supported markets pull liquidity from the same vault as demand arises.

Quick math: $150 in SPCX backs up to 67.50 USDG of initial debt at 45% LTV, assuming USDG stays at $1 and there’s available liquidity.

Borrow 50 USDG and you receive 49.95 after the 0.1% fee (before gas). Interest accrues onto the outstanding debt.

Paboxo turns tokenized equities into working capital: onchain credit backed by your holdings.

text:
Some numbers on the potential ethereum:0x0c1c1c109fe34733fca54b82d7b46b75cfb71f6e buybacks. Comparing this to base:0xacfe6019ed1a7dc6f7b508c02d1b04ec88cc21bf at the end given it follows a similar model. 

Programmatic: 
All Net Interest Margin (NIM) will go to programmatic buybacks of CHIP. 

Assuming $1B in TVL, at a 60% utilisation rate. This is how often the TVL is being actively deployed to loans before being sold off to TradFi via GLX.
Utilisation rate has been ~60% for the second half of the year so far [1].
 
At an 8% average loan yield (after costs) and 10% NIM:

$1B x 60% x 8% x 10% = $5M in programmatic buybacks. 

The above is my bear case. My base case is $2.5B in TVL next year which would push programmatic buybacks to $12M [2]. 

Discretionary: 

Assuming a 2% origination fee and 2x velocity. At $2.5B in TVL the protocol would fund $5B in loans. That would be $100M in origination revenue [2]. 

If you assume only 25% of this goes to discretionary buybacks, that would be $25M p.a.

Total:
i.e. next year would expect ~$30M in total buybacks for ethereum:0x0c1c1c109fe34733fca54b82d7b46b75cfb71f6e, which would put it at a 3x market cap multiple and a 15x FDV multiple.  

Comparison to Venice: 
In Q3 base:0xacfe6019ed1a7dc6f7b508c02d1b04ec88cc21bf did $4.1M in annualised programmatic buybacks and $3.9M in annualised discretionary buybacks. So a total of $8M [3].

It trades at 12x the market cap and 4x the FDV.

Clear conclusion is that ethereum:0x0c1c1c109fe34733fca54b82d7b46b75cfb71f6e is very undervalued relative to its earning and buyback potential.

看完谷歌在看微软财报，同样是财报后，微软为何可以盘前上涨？

微软的财报依旧是延续谷歌的分析模式，看五大因素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引+Azure or AI monetization 

营收：优秀，增长重新加速，营收、营业利润、每股收益（EPS）及云业务表现均超出预期

AI资本支出：非常高，而且资本扩张下有Azure和AI收入增长保证，属于有效健康的扩张性资本开支，相比谷歌的资本支出让市场信心更强

自由现金流：依旧保持增长，在一年超过千亿级别的AI基础建设投资下，依旧保持FCF正值，虽然自由现金流还在被资本支出压制，但是有业绩保障，起码可以保持收支平衡

Azure：核心业务依旧是财报最强数据，同比48%增长，而回归前几个季度，从39%一路涨到现在的48%，Azure在如此庞大的收入基础上依旧在重新加速，进一步证实了微软的AI商业化更加完善

未来指引：预计下一季度Azure恒定汇率提升至49%-50%，一旦下个季度数据达成，将会继续证明Azure增长仍然处于加速阶段

AI Monetization：微软的人工智能变现并不只是来自Azure的48%增长，Foundry收入同比超过3倍，客户数量超过12万+，而在Foundry开源模型上的收入增长10倍，这意味着微软把从模型→Agent→Azure计算→企业部署做成一个完整平台

另外 Copilot也在稳定增长，结合Azure与Foundry，基本上验证了微软在AI 基础设施 + AI 平台 + AI 应用三个层面的盈利能力

其实看完微软的财报要素在对不谷歌，两者其实差距没有想象的那么大，但是微软却比谷歌多了一个核心，那就是证明了自家的AI产业赚钱，而且是全方位的在赚钱，虽然自由现金流并未加速增长，但是已经达到暂时的收支平衡，而这份数据正好踩到市场最想看到的结果上

不过，还是那句话，对于谷歌与微软来说，核心云业务依旧很强，基本面没问题，只不过短期市场在宏观压力下，更愿意为微软的财报与估值买单！

quoted_text:
回顾一下谷歌的财报，虽然不算优秀，但是股价为何“崩了”?

本周一的宏观纪要中我明确了三大云厂商要看的四大要素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引

而放到谷歌本身上，要看的则是五大要素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引+Google Cloud

那么谷歌财报给出了什么答案？

营收：小幅度不及预期，不是差，而是结果出现问题，绝对增速很强，但是市场预期更强，略低于预期，关键就在广告收入上略低预期

AI资本支出：公司全面依旧维持较高资本支出，全年投入2000亿美元，这对于上游英伟达、博通、HBM、光模块、服务器、电力预计数据中心整个AI基础设施链条，明确了需求验证逻辑

自由现金流：-91亿，今年第二季度负自由现金流，资本开支过大，营收追不上

Google Cloud：依旧是财报最强数据，307.1亿增长同步增幅103%，超过55%将在未来24个月确认收入，这个数据证明谷歌的AI基础建设已经开始形成大规模收入

未来指引：2027年资本支出显著增加，TPU系统将在2027年明显放量，但是因为AI算力供给紧张，谷歌开始使用第三方计算能力，管理层警告谷歌云业务短期利润将收到挤压

整体来看，五大要素中，除了自由现金流有问题，未来指引提示云业务利润受到挤压之外，其他数据依旧不错，尤其是核心业务Google Cloud很强，证明了企业的基本面没问题

但是，估计在财报后依旧出现较大幅度的下跌，主要是因为近期多方因素导致：

1，预期过强，符合预期的财报都会出现Sell the news，更何况一份有瑕疵的财报？估值修复幅度扩大正常

2，宏观要素，高利率挤压投资情绪，导致利空放大，估值修复幅度也大大增加，凌晨沃什讲话中明确提及高利率挤压了科技企业的融资能力，同时也让投资者手里的钱更贵，更舍不得为当下的估值买单

3，上游海力士强劲财报证明了更大的资本支出，但是下游云厂商却没能证明AI足够赚钱，AI商业逻辑被质疑，ROI成为焦点，质疑=估值调整

Q3财报我一直强调，市场对于AI企业的验证逻辑已经正式进入第二阶段，第一阶段看谁敢花钱，第二阶段看谁能挣钱，而谷歌恰好踩到“雷点”，都在拼赚钱，你的财报还在努力花钱，市场短期自然不买账

后市如何去看？

首先财报显示谷歌的基本面没问题，只是并未符合目前市场对财报的预期，所以大幅回调之后必然有短期技术性反弹

AI产业上，微软财报还不错，接下来看今晚凌晨的亚马逊财报，本周三大云厂商，如果3家中2家都不错，基本可以对冲掉谷歌财报给市场带来的风险担忧，

宏观侧，今晚先看GDP PCE 对美股是否有整体压力，数据公布消化后依旧要回归财报，凌晨美股尾盘锚定亚马逊财报预期，由于谷歌财报瑕疵，市场会相对谨慎，但是如果亚马逊财报不错，市场情绪会被提振

趋势上，AI的基本面，谷歌的基本面都依旧健康，宏观以及利率上虽然有挤压，但是不构成实质性威胁，最多就是造成估值深度调整，不过调整估值后对于股价以及后续反而是一件好事！

Your Stock Tokens can bankroll your next play without forcing you to exit the position.

Paboxo enables eligible holders to borrow USDG using supported Stock Tokens on Robinhood Chain as collateral, while still keeping their market exposure.

But the caveat is that we at @paboxoxyz use different lending rules.

What’s notable:

• Market-hours-aware lending.
Once the reference market shuts, actions that depend on live pricing, new borrows, liquidations, and collateral withdrawals on debt-backed positions pause. You can still repay or post more collateral. Anything price-driven resumes when fresh prices return.

• Collateral-by-collateral terms.
Each asset has its own borrowing cap and interest curve. SPCX and TSLA start with a 45% max initial LTV; NVDA, MSFT, and AAPL allow 60%; SPY goes up to 70%.

• One liquidity pool.
USDG suppliers get peUSDG vault shares, and their yield comes from borrower interest. All supported markets pull liquidity from the same vault as demand arises.

Quick math: $150 in SPCX backs up to 67.50 USDG of initial debt at 45% LTV, assuming USDG stays at $1 and there’s available liquidity.

Borrow 50 USDG and you receive 49.95 after the 0.1% fee (before gas). Interest accrues onto the outstanding debt.

quoted_text:
梳理了一下西班牙火车追尾事故：

1/ 事情的起因是 LZB 系统（可以理解为计算机控制的自动安全系统）故障，LZB已经是大约40-50年前的系统了，问题一直很多，铁路系统也正在更换新一代系统，但还没完成。

当LZB故障时，受影响路段的车辆强制停车，并且转由Adif进行调度，也就是人工调度

2/ 在这个事件中，LZB发生了故障，受影响路段中的6辆火车停了下来。

其中包括最前面的Lryo，可以理解为私铁慢车，和后面的Renfe，可以理解为国铁快车

随后Adif通知了所有车辆按照正常速度行驶

这里Adif 犯了第一个错误，因为按照规定，在这种情况下要遵循目视规则，时速不能超过40km/小时，确保出现意外情况时能手动完成刹车

在Adif发出这个指令后，另一量Renfe 列车司机指出了他的错误，并按照目视规则以40km/h速度行驶

但Adif没有纠正指令，从录音看，事故 Renfe 车辆司机的回复略带疑问：（以正常速度？），但他仍然按照指令以超过100km/h的速度行驶，途中检测到了145km/h的数据

3/ 初始状态下，两车相距29km，从启动到撞击一共17分钟

首先Lryo收到重新启动指令的时候是不确定的，有可能Renfe启动以后他仍然没有收到Adif的指令

但从后来泄露的录音看，至少在离撞击还有5分钟的时候，Lryo向Adif报告了，自己无法启动

（PS：Lryo和Renfe是由Adif的两个不同工作人员引导）

尽管如此，这五分钟Adif没有通知renfe减速或者刹车。另外17分钟内，Adif是可以看到Renfe正在接近而Lryo保持静止

最终Renfe以100km/h以上的速度前进直至看到Lyro，但此时手动刹车已经无法避免撞击

总的来说就是

LZB故障 + Adif 严重失职 + Renfe列车违规操作叠加，导致了这场悲剧

R.I.P.

text:
Saying goodbye to Devv.

我们很荣幸做出了 Devv 这个产品，更荣幸它得到了大家的认可。过去 3 年里，Devv 前后服务了上百万全球开发者。Devv 的每一次搜索，既是在为提问的人提供答案，也是在给我们团队的每个人一份认同。

Devv 是全球最早的一批 AI 搜索产品。那时候 ChatGPT、Claude 这些工具都还不能联网搜索，开发者只能二选一：搜索引擎给你一堆链接，大模型又看不到训练数据之后的新内容。Devv 起源于我们团队自己的需求，最早只是团队内部的一个小工具。后来我们发现它的价值非常高，每个人每天都离不开它，于是把它做成了公开的产品，没想到短时间内就迎来了爆发式的增长。

随着 AI 时代的发展，联网搜索已经成了几乎所有通用 AI 助手的标配，Agent 更是走得更远：它们可以直接操作电脑、调用工具，端到端地把一件事做完。我们必须诚实地面对：单纯的搜索，已经不再是一个被特别需要的功能了。

团队经历了很长一段时间的迷茫，反复思考 Agent 时代的发展趋势，以及人们真正需要的是什么，也做了很多次尝试。最终，我们在 Multica 上找到了答案。Multica 是一个让 AI Agent 像真正的队友一样加入团队的工作平台：你把任务分配给它们，它们接手执行、汇报进度、遇到问题主动提出，完成后交回给你审核。我们相信这就是 Agent 时代软件工作的样子，也是我们做过最让人兴奋的事情。所以我们决定停止运营 Devv，把全部精力投入到 Multica。

和一个产品告别从来都不容易，尤其是很多人每天都在用的产品。谢谢你们信任 Devv，谢谢你们在我们做得不好的时候直言不讳，也谢谢你们一路同行。一段旅程的终点，也是另一段旅程的起点。希望在 Multica 再次见到你。

—— Devv 团队

Jiayuan、Bohan、Yushen

intentional short termism:

the engineered erosion of industrial edge.

this is what happens when managers replace long term stewards. like politicians, their horizon is bounded by contract renewals and bonus cycles, trading off generational resilience for short term returns.

for decades, western executives traded away intellectual property and built fragile joint ventures in china for quick margin expansion that boosted the stock price and padded their personal compensation.

i experienced this firsthand. when i was 22, my father sent me to china alone to negotiate for our 160 year old family business. the local partners made one non negotiable demand: a complete transfer of our know how. when i refused, they told me we would be locked out of the chinese market. i stood up, smiled, thanked them, and walked out of the room.

a family business protects the balance sheet for the next generation; a salaried executive optimizes the earnings report for the next quarter and exits before the structural collapse hits.

today, our business remains in full family control and is thriving. chinese merchants buy our products through neighboring markets, and our sales across southeast asia have tripled, all without bending the knee.

this is why volkswagen is failing.

this is why china is winning.

quoted_text:
这次英伟达GTC大会，着实有点无聊，没啥创新亮点，已经开始从“卖芯片”到“卖货柜”了，逐渐开始有点当年加密矿机的味道！🧐

这次大会上，黄仁勋放出了一个重磅利好：AI 数据中心从半年部署时间，现在压缩到只要 14 天。

现场发布了一个叫 DSX POD 的架构。直接把包含 Vera Rubin 芯片的整套计算设备、水冷管道、网络线缆，全都在工厂里组装测试好，塞进标准集装箱里。等货物运到现场，只要水电基础设施准备到位，插上电就能直接开干。

这场景是不是看着挺眼熟？😂

这不就是当年比特大陆 @BITMAINtech 玩剩的“蚂蚁矿箱”吗？

当年比特币挖矿争分夺秒，矿工们为了抢算力和低价电，把上百台矿机打包装进集装箱，哪里电便宜就运去哪里，落地通电即挖。今天英伟达把同样的手法用在了高端 AI 上。

虽然看似只是换了个包装，但背后却折射出两个非常关键的产业转向：

1️⃣ 芯片物理极限逼近，算力竞争转向“系统工程与模块化”

单靠微缩制程、在单块芯片上暴算力的时代越来越难走了。摩尔定律放缓，芯片迭代的边际效应越来越低。现在的竞争维度已经从“芯片怎么造”转移到了“怎么把成千上万块芯片快速搭成一个大工厂”。

模块化集装箱的本质，就是把复杂的机房建设，变成了像拼积木一样的工业流水线产品。

2️⃣ 时间就是金钱，本质上是一场“抢电抢时间”的资本游戏

黄仁勋算了一笔非常现实的账：一个 1GW 的 AI 算力工厂成本 500 亿美元，一年预期能刨出 400 亿美元收入。如果因为机房部署慢了延迟3个月，直接损失的就是 100 亿美元。

在这场资本狂飙里，设备早一天上线吐出 Token，就能早一天把真金白银收回来。

不过，英伟达的“14天奇迹”也有一个终极门槛：电力。

集装箱可以在厂里提前造好，可电网不会凭空变出来。14 天的极限部署前提，是现场已经拥有现成的电力和冷却接口。如果电网没拉通，箱子运到了也只能堆在荒郊野外吹风。

说到底，集装箱交付和“真正收钱”之间还隔着一条电力红线。AI 算力战演到今天，看似拼的是最前沿的芯片，落到实际，拼的依然是最传统的电力基建、供应链与时间成本。🧐

这里我重点依旧看好核心方向：一个是冷却龙头， $VRT ，一个是目前燃气发电龙头： $GEV 。

text:
nine years in crypto, zcash was always there

my journey in crypto had an unusual start: during my grad studies, i joined a chainalysis when they were a 20-people startup in copenhagen

my job: apply ML (aka AI before it was cool) to break the privacy in cryptocurrencies and blockchains like bitcoin, ethereum, etc. 

i also read and analyzed dash, monero, etc. and
that's when i first learned about zcash – and it completely blew my mind

the weakest point of all crypto and blockchains is how much data is leaked and published on-chain, combined with how much OSINT and privately gathered data (kyc) can be correlated with on-chain data

the fact that zcash essentially removed the need to publish any data basically meant that there was no data to analyze – in other words zcash was at the frontier of crypto 

it heavily inspired me to ditch AI and pursue decentralized protocols instead 

from ethereum, through cosmos, many other L1s in-between, and anoma for the last 6 years, I wasn't formally involved with zcash – yet somehow zcash was always there 

because everything I've worked on shared Zcash' values of decentralization, privacy, and self-sovereignty

my mind was shaped by zcash (think like an attacker, analyze data flows from end-to-end, etc) and a whole lot of my work has been inspired by cash too, from custom protocols like Namada and the Anoma DOS to end user products like Namadillo, AnomaPay, and recently Zillions

and now that i think about it, i probably would've left crypto a few months ago if zcash wasn't around anymore

i've grown increasingly disillusioned with the industry: the hypergamblification brought by memecoins and the dominance of centralized protocols and products (combined with this brutal bear market)

like many, i've considered leaving this industry 

because I didn't join to make casinos faster and more addictive – i joined because of the initial ethos of this space, to build an alternative to the financial system, one that gives people real sovereignty over their money, data, and lives

in an industry where even ethereum is losing its roots, zcash remains true to its values and even today the community is full of ethos-driven and strongly aligned people (come to a zcash conference and you'll see, they feel like 2017)

zcash has been like a north star to me, 
a reminder that the original vision of crypto isn't dead,
there are still people willing to build for principles rather than speculation

so yeah, it's been 9 years since I've joined crypto, and without zcash, i probably wouldn't be here anymore

happy 10th birthday zcash!

honored to be part of this community, and more excited than ever to contribute to what comes next
