author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Onchain lending vaults went from $1.5B to $10B in two years.

Meanwhile, actively managed onchain trading vaults are at roughly zero.

Not for lack of demand. You just couldn't run a real hedge fund book on one onchain venue. Hyperliquid fixed that this year, and @Infinit_Labs is the first team I've seen build the actual fund wrapper around it.

So I pulled the full trading wallet of their first vault and rebuilt it day by day, across 340 fills, incl. every funding payment and the daily marks.

Here's what I found:

Why HL, why now?

CTA momentum is the oldest strategy in managed futures. Rank markets by relative strength, long the top, short the bottom, across stocks, commodities and crypto. Dollar neutral, so the return comes from selection, not direction.

It only works if all three asset classes sit on one margin account tho. Until HIP-3 came to Hyperliquid, that didn't exist onchain.

Today 23 HL markets clear INFINIT's $100M open interest floor. 10 are crypto. 13 are stocks, indices and commodities (S&P 500, Nasdaq 100, Gold, Silver, Brent, WTI, SK Hynix, MU, SPCX, GOOGL, META and a few more).

That means: One venue, 24/7, one margin system, and this universe is why a cross-asset vault can exist now and couldn't 12 months ago.

Simultaneously, the rapid advances in AI play a similarly crucial role.

Not for the signals tho. Relative-strength ranking with systematic entries and exits is quant, not some sort of agentic magic, and Apex says so themselves.

Yet, AI is the ops layer, and that's another crucial part worth paying attention to:

- Trading credentials can open and close positions but can't withdraw. Deposits sit behind a 3-of-4 multisig and the manager holds none of the signing keys, so a manager's key can never block withdrawals.

- A trade gateway sits in front of the exchange. Any order outside the eligible list or the declared limits gets blocked before it lands.

- Monitoring agents check live trading against the manager's published mandate. Breaches go to a human risk team, unresolved ones pause trading access.

- Share accounting and investor reporting run on the same stack.

That's pretty much the middle office of a fund, running almost fully autonomously, and it's the reason a $500K vault can be run with institutional process at all, and the reason MS2 can take more capital without hiring ten people.

So, what does the wallet (and onchain data) say?

APEX MS1, operated by Apex Quant Capital had $506K deposited on the 3rd of August and its first fill on the 10th of August.

The overall return is about 40% annualized as of today, +8.4% actual over 78 days, before vault fees. The peak was +8.5% on the 23rd of October, and Apex reports roughly 40% annualized after fees through September, which lines up.

A few more stats:

- The worst drawdown was (only) 3.7%, all of it in the first week.

- Dollar neutral in practice, not just on paper. Net exposure averaged 1% of gross across 70 active days, with 7.5% on the worst day. Right now it's $143K long vs $131K short.

- 1x isolated on every position, every day. Gross exposure peaked at 1.04x capital.

- Ten equal position slots of about $45K at launch, roughly 9% of capital per market.

- The book went fully to cash twice when the signal had nothing. "Holds cash when conditions aren't right" is actually part of the strategy, not just marketing.

- 20 markets traded with $12M volume, $2.2K fees paid, and $3.1K funding received.

Current book, in case you're curious (on the 26th of October): long S&P 500 against short ETH, SOL, XRP, HYPE and ZEC.

So what does that mean?

Eleven weeks in, neutrality, leverage, market eligibility and cash discipline all check out onchain, and the two numbers Apex publishes match the wallet.

The PnL split is what you’d expect from a momentum book in this tape. Crypto had the trends and made the money, SOL, ZEC and HYPE about $57K net. Single stocks chopped and the stops gave back about $25K. Indices flat, commodities about +$13K in October on Brent, Gold and WTI.

Losers cut, winners left to run. And the trend is now moving into commodities, with the book flipped long the S&P. That’s the whole point of a cross-asset book. MS1 got a first taste in October, MS2 is where it gets tested properly.

Wen MS2?

Deposits open on the 28th of October until the 11th of November, and I'm looking to deposit too.

Why?

Bc a fund-structured vault with public fills, trade-only keys and a manager putting up first-loss capital for APEX 1 and 2 is the first version of this I'd actually put money in.

This is likely the model the next wave of onchain asset management gets built on, and it's live on HL right now.

What I'll be watching?

- Fee terms and the size of Apex's first-loss commitment
- Whether the stock and commodity legs keep contributing
- How the strategy behaves at size ($500K is a pilot and the real capacity test is more capital in the same 23 markets)

NFA tho ofc.

text:
I want to give my opinion on Ember herself, because I think the person people have come to appreciate is getting lost in this controversy.

From what I’ve seen of Ember, she is a warm, lovable, caring person. I’ve appreciated her personality, her advocacy for mental health and women’s rights, and her willingness to speak up for others. I’ve generally found her open and sincere, and those are meaningful reasons why I respect her.

Finding out something about the person behind her avatar does not suddenly erase those qualities. The kindness people appreciated, the conversations that helped them, and the enjoyment they found in her content still matter. I don’t think those things should be discarded as though none of them meant anything.

Personally, whether the creator behind Ember is male or female does not change why I enjoy her content or appreciate her as a person. I still support her.

That doesn’t mean I’m dismissing everybody who feels hurt or uncomfortable. People are entitled to their boundaries, and nobody has to continue a friendship or collaboration they no longer feel comfortable with. But feeling uncomfortable does not justify harassment, dog-piling, or using someone’s private life as ammunition for drama.

Honesty and personal boundaries matter to me. I wasn’t part of the private conversations being discussed, so I’m not going to present allegations or assumptions as established facts. Any specific concern should be considered with evidence and context. An avatar, a voice changer, or an undisclosed offline identity does not, by itself, establish that somebody exploited another person’s trust.

VTubing is built around avatars, performance, and privacy. No one is automatically entitled to deeply personal details simply because they assumed something about the person behind the screen. Keeping personal information private is not, by itself, proof of dishonesty.

That’s also where I disagree with the Side Scrollers discussion. Trust matters, absolutely. But I don’t believe viewers or occasional collaborators are automatically owed somebody’s offline identity as the baseline of honesty. The question is whether someone deliberately misled another person in a way that affected their relationship or boundaries. Privacy alone does not answer that question.

As for Strawb, I disagree with how this was handled publicly. Her statement says she contacted Celestium privately, and I acknowledge that. But I still think approaching Ember directly would have been a more considerate way to clarify these concerns before bringing them before an audience. Believing somebody would lie is still an assumption about a conversation that never happened.

I understand that Strawb did not feel comfortable having that conversation. That does not, by itself, explain why bringing the matter before an audience was the more responsible choice. I would have preferred a private attempt to clarify the concern, with room for Ember to respond. Any public criticism should focus on specific conduct and avoid exposing more personal information than necessary.

Whatever the intention, I think this needed more care. Someone’s private information should not be treated casually when exposing it can bring a wave of scrutiny and harassment. Public humiliation does not resolve questions about trust or help people establish what actually happened.

That is why BananaJuju’s response resonates with me. She describes people approaching her to dig for unrelated information about Ember and build a narrative. I agree with her objection to that. If there is a specific concern about someone’s behavior, address that concern honestly. Searching through their personal life for anything that might make them look worse does not help establish the truth.

Lord Intellectual’s response adds another important point. In his comic, the supposed dramatic revelation that Ember is a guy is met with the question: “Is it really relevant?”

Relevant to the kindness she has shown? The help she has given people? Her personality, her content, or the reasons people appreciated her? For me, that revelation does not erase any of those things.

He says he already knew, or at least strongly suspected, and he described how Ember had helped him. That support did not suddenly become meaningless because of who was behind her avatar. I think that matters when we’re discussing somebody’s character.

He also made clear that he would condemn genuine wrongdoing and cut ties if necessary. His support wasn’t unconditional, and neither is mine. But someone’s private identity alone is not enough for me to disregard the care and good nature I’ve seen from them.

That’s why his statement, “Ember Paradox remains my friend,” carries weight for me. Alongside BananaJuju’s refusal to participate in digging for dirt, it reflects the approach I support: respect people’s privacy, take specific concerns seriously, and judge their character through their actions.

As a Christian, I believe honesty, compassion, and dignity should guide how we handle this. That applies to Ember, Strawb, Rev, and everyone involved. I don’t support harassment of any of them. Disagreeing with how someone handled a situation does not justify turning around and treating them cruelly.

What matters most to me is Ember’s character, values, and how she treats people. My appreciation includes the kindness, advocacy, warmth, and good nature I’ve seen from her. I’m willing to listen to substantiated concerns and acknowledge mistakes, but I’m not going to let this revelation erase everything I appreciated about her.

I still support Ember, and I hope everyone involved can move forward with honesty and compassion.

This is my personal opinion, based on what I’ve seen and read. I don’t claim to know every private detail or have the complete picture. Everyone is entitled to their own thoughts and conclusions, and these are mine.

We should all take what we hear on the internet with a grain of salt, examine the evidence in context, and avoid jumping on bandwagons or participating in harassment on either side.

text:
As someone who has personally spent $500k / mo+ on Google Ads for years, I can tell you with certainty: 

This revenue growth in Search is artificial & extremely unhealthy for Google’s business long term

Search volumes are declining as legacy search is being increasingly cannibalized by non-monetized LLM queries

Google’s response? 

Manufacture revenue growth via short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics. I.e. charge advertisers more for lower quality clicks, including clicks they do not want and explicitly did not approve Google to charge them for

A few examples to illustrate: 

For all of its history until recently, Google operated on a 2nd price auction model

I.e. if you bid $5 CPC and the next highest bidder bids $1 CPC, Google charged you $1.01 for the click (one penny more than the 2nd highest bidder) rather than the $5 you bid

This was a genius move by Google early on as it incentivizes advertisers to input their true maximum willingness to pay rather than trying to play the game of bidding low and constantly adjusting to try to stay just ahead of the next highest bidder while still not paying too much

However recently, Google silently deprecated the 2nd price auction and began charging advertisers as much as their bid and budget caps allow, regardless of what anyone else is bidding

It’s a short-sighted cash grab at the expense of the long term health of the  advertiser ecosystem

Making thing worse, Google also recently nerfed keyword targeting precision

Google previously had precise keyword targeting settings that allowed advertisers pick individual search phrases to bid on, defined down to the character w/ exact match or phrase match targeting 

This was one of the core features that made search advertising magic, enabling advertisers to run extremely precise campaigns based on exactly what their target customer typed 

But now, even if you bid on a specific term or phrase using the strictest exact 
-match targeting settings, Google will show your ad across 1000’s of unrelated keywords, labeling them as as “exact match (close variant)” 

The definition of “close variant” means whatever they want it to and changes constantly. The result is advertisers get billed for clicks that are totally irrelevant to their business and that their targeting settings explicitly forbid Google from targeting. Google does it anyway and there’s no ability to turn this off

So now exact match is broad match, and broad match is just meaningless spam

This is all very bad for advertisers, but for Google, it allows them to show your ad and bill you for clicks across 1000x more searches that were previously going unmonetized (mainly because they’re garbage queries no one wants) 

This is how you grow revenue atop declining search volumes 

Lastly, and perhaps most egregiously, Google quietly stopped respecting budget caps by a factor of 2x. For example campaigns we’ve been running for years with $1000 daily budget caps suddenly began spending $2000+ per day 

And the extra spend is entirely on the garbage keywords Google arbitrarily throws in as “exact match (close variants)” which have no value to our business, but can’t be turned off

Google offers no refunds nor any recourse for overspend or spend on keywords you explicitly did not target

These are not the actions of a healthy business. These are the actions of company whose core business is in decline but desperately needs to pump quarterly earnings so Wall Street will continue to fund insane capex while hopefully looking through their rapidly deteriorating negative free cash flow 

Google operated a benevolent monopoly for the better part of 25 yrs

Meaning the value Google captured from Search was but a small fraction of the value it created, and that spread produced a potential energy that justified expectations of high earnings growth far, far into the future 

This is now no longer the case

At the alter of AI capex, Google is sacrificing the golden goose

quoted_text:
Surprise 1: Anthropic acquired a one-person biotech
.
.
.
Surprise 2: that person is me
Surprise 3: I’m here to tell you all about it

Yes, this is what you think it is; after 6 yrs of increasingly loose anonymity: the Professor Oak reveal post

…and yes, it has gotten so boring around here that I’m literally doxxing myself to spice up the timeline

-------
Ok, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Cody Tranbarger. I mostly tweet, but occasionally find time to dabble in drug dev & starting/building biotechs. My past lives span the VC, crossover, startup continuum; Prof Oak has been my way of keeping a digital foot in those worlds, despite having my physical feet planted elsewhere.

The past 18 mo, ‘elsewhere’ was Mithril Medicine, a co. I founded to develop bsAbs for LAMA2-CMD & other ECM-related genetic diseases.

Mithril was born out of hands-on building with @MikeNGladstone, @JasonPaulRhodes, @LifeSciVC, & team @atlasventure. Somehow, I made enough half-decent calls along the way (even a broken clock is right twice a day, eh?) to convince them Mithril/I warranted a small seed. While I can hardly rationalize such an outrageously cavalier bet, I’m grateful for it, & I'd partner with Atlas again in a heartbeat.

In typical AV fashion, Mithril’s primordial form was virtual, decentralized, & ultra-lean. This stage tends to be short-lived, but for Mithril, it worked surprisingly well, for surprisingly long, thanks in part to the rapid maturation of the AI tools I used liberally.

Eventually, Mithril became a bit of an experiment itself - to find the upper bound of how far it could scale as a single operator + a bunch of Claude (+ a stellar bench of part-time consultants).

In parallel, I started spending time with @nc_frey, @an1lam, & @CoefficientBio team; and promptly experienced, for the 1st time, AI at the frontier. Soon thereafter, Mithril stopped looking like an experiment, & started looking like a preview of an entirely new operating model.

From that spark came “Pipeline-in-a-Person.” The idea immediately resonated when we shared it here back in April; and it was central to the shared vision that led to Anthropic’s acquisition of Mithril, & my joining the team.

Why join Anthropic? Three reasons.
(1) For Mithril, the programs continue, with more resources & infrastructure behind them, and as much Claude as I can put to work.

(2) For me, the chance to start several more programs, & find out how many one person can actually run in parallel - an almost unprecedented luxury for a curious drug hunter.

(3) For our mission, a path to institutionalize & scale this new way of working, then put it in the hands of all of biopharma, all over the world - which, candidly, I find the most energizing.

Will AI x Bio cure diseases? Unequivocally yes, imo… but not by the route that gets the most airtime. Rather than timeline acceleration & compression, I see orchestration & parallelization as today's low-hanging fruit.

Most drug hunters see a handful of go/no-go calls in a career, & spend entirely too much of the rest trading emails (my inbox can attest).

Give them the bandwidth to run several programs at once, and the time to focus on scientific judgment, and I’m willing to bet they’ll make better calls. And at scale, better calls translate to more drugs, higher hit rates, broader patient impact, & likely, a disease or 10 or 100 cured. I couldn't be more excited to build toward that future @AnthropicAI.

Finally, a heartfelt thank you to BioTwitter/X. The end of anonymity is bittersweet, but if anyone’s earned a proper introduction, you all have.

It’s difficult to overstate how much this app has done for me: a decade of education, plenty of friends, many job opportunities, several mentors, a few investors, even a co-founder (fmr). It was the generosity of this community that inspired me to start posting 6 years ago, after just as many years lurking. I hope I’ve been able to pay it forward, in my own small way.

But, to be clear, Prof Oak isn’t going anywhere. Same beat, same themes, and now, a front-row seat to drug development at the frontier. Stay tuned for dispatches from the trenches; and remember...

Gotta Cure 'Em All

text:
Sometimes it helps to think of trading like a business. Every business that lasts makes money because it provides something of value to someone who is willing to pay for it. In markets, that someone might be a hedger who needs to offload risk, a fund that is forced to rebalance or an impatient buyer who pays a spread for immediacy.

Most traders run this logic in reverse. It’s like opening a coffee shop because you love a particular street, then standing outside wondering why nobody comes in, instead of first finding where people actually want coffee and setting up there.

A business starts with the customer and the need and the location follows. Trading can work the same way, with the market chosen based on where the people paying for your service are.
author: 0xaporia
quoted_text:
I think most people approach market selection backwards. They start with what they want to trade (a coin, index, stock, whatever) and then try to force a signal out of it. The market comes first and the edge is something they hope to find afterward.

The better approach is to start with the effect you’re trying to capture. Ask what behavior you’re exploiting, whether that’s momentum, mean reversion, some structural flow, etc. and then ask where you would expect that effect to actually show up.

Universe selection matters as much as the signal and sometimes more. A mediocre signal applied to the right set of markets can beat a brilliant signal applied to the wrong ones. Where you trade can matter more than how you trade.

author: OfficialSUNio
quoted_text:
𝗦𝗨𝗡 𝗕𝘂𝘆𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸 & 𝗕𝘂𝗿𝗻: 𝟲𝟴𝟱.𝟳𝟴𝗠+ 𝗧𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗹𝘆 𝗕𝘂𝗿𝗻𝗲𝗱 🔥

A token burn is one thing. Building a business model that keeps funding it is another.

@OfficialSUNio has completed another SUN buyback and burn round, removing 7,232,977.17 SUN between July 25 and October 25, 2026.

That brings cumulative burns to 685,780,165.49 SUN, according to the reported figures.

The bigger story isn't just the number burned. It's how revenue from multiple TRON ecosystem businesses feeds into SUN's long-term supply-reduction mechanism. 🧵👇

🔹 1️⃣ The Latest Burn: Another Round Completed

▪️ Latest round: 7.23M SUN burned
▪️ Cumulative burns: 685.78M SUN

The burned tokens were sent to the designated burn address, with transactions publicly verifiable on-chain.

This matters because the mechanism has moved beyond a one-off announcement into a recurring process with records that anyone can independently check.

🔹 2️⃣ Three Revenue Engines, One Burn Mechanism

The reported cumulative contributions are:

▪️ SunSwap V2: 388,023,868.41 SUN
▪️ SunPump: 285,879,914.81 SUN
▪️ SunX: 11,876,382.27 SUN

Together, these figures account for the reported 685.78M SUN burned through the ecosystem's revenue-funded mechanism.

Each product operates in a different market, but all three contribute to the same broader token-economics framework.

🔹 3️⃣ How the Buyback & Burn Model Works

The mechanism connects product activity to SUN's token supply.

▪️ SunSwap V2: 0.05% of each transaction amount is allocated to buying back and burning SUN.

▪️ SunSwap V3: A portion of fees from the specified TRX/USDT 0.05% fee-tier pool supports buybacks and burns.

▪️ SunPump: 100% of protocol revenue is allocated to the mechanism.

▪️ SunX: 50% of net revenue after operating costs is allocated to buybacks and burns.

Revenue is used to acquire SUN, which is then sent to a designated burn address.

The important distinction is that the burn mechanism is linked to activity across products rather than depending on a single source of revenue.

🔹 4️⃣ What 685.78M SUN Means for Supply

Token burns permanently remove tokens from circulation, reducing the amount that can remain available in the market.

Against a circulating supply of approximately 19.22 billion SUN, cumulative burns of 685.78 million are equivalent to around 3.6% of that circulating-supply benchmark.

That comparison helps put the number into perspective, but it should not be confused with the percentage of SUN's original supply that has been burned.

The long-term impact depends on continued execution, revenue generation, demand, and the wider token economy.

🔹 5️⃣ Product Growth Is the Key Variable

The sustainability of this model depends on more than announcing another burn.

▪️ SunSwap needs trading activity and liquidity.

▪️ SunPump depends on continued platform usage and protocol revenue.

▪️ SunX needs sustainable trading activity and net revenue after costs.

If these products generate more eligible revenue, the mechanism has a larger potential funding base. If activity slows, the amount available for buybacks may also decline.

That makes product adoption and revenue quality important metrics to watch alongside the burn total.

🔹 6️⃣ What About SUN's Market Performance?

Around October 27, 2026, SUN was trading near $0.0162, with roughly $10 million in reported 24-hour trading volume. Its price had also drifted lower over the preceding week.

This is a useful reminder: a token burn does not guarantee an immediate price increase.

Market price also reflects demand, liquidity, broader crypto conditions, investor expectations, and selling pressure.

The burn mechanism can reduce supply over time, but it cannot independently determine short-term price action.

🔹 7️⃣ The Bigger Picture: Revenue-Linked Value Capture

The more important question is whether SUN's ecosystem can keep generating meaningful revenue and consistently direct a portion of it toward buybacks and burns.

That creates a framework connecting product usage with token supply reduction.

For holders and ecosystem observers, the metrics worth tracking are:

▪️ SUN burned in each round
▪️ Cumulative tokens burned
▪️ Revenue generated by each contributing product
▪️ Trading activity and liquidity
▪️ Circulating supply and market demand

The takeaway: 685.78M SUN burned is a significant cumulative milestone. But the long-term case rests on whether SunSwap, SunPump, and SunX can sustain the activity and revenue that power the mechanism.

Track the revenue. Verify the burns on-chain. And judge the model by consistent execution—not just the headline number.

quoted_text:
Who actually gets rich if Anthropic lists at $2 trillion?

The S-1 filed on Monday lets us answer from the filing itself. 

The reported target is $1.5T to $2T, listing the week of November 16. The filing implies about 16.9B fully diluted shares. So $2T works out to roughly $118 a share.

The cap table at $2T:

- $199B for the 7 controlling co-founders, about 10% 
- $28B for Ben Mann, if his stake matches theirs 
- $100B for the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, 5% 
- $331B in employee options and RSUs, about 17% , That pool covers about 5,300 employees, an average of $62M each. 
- But when you joined matters enormously.

The S-1 shows how much equity was granted each year, and at what price. [
Headcount went from about 300 to 500 in late 2023, to 940 at end 2024, to 5,300 now. 

Match the two, and here is roughly how many people made what at $2T:

- $110M to $400M each: ~300 to 500 people hired by 2023
- $200M to $300M each: ~440 to 640 hired in 2024
- $70M to $95M each: ~1,360 hired in 2025
- $10M to $20M each: ~3,000 hired in 2026 
So about 940 people hired by the end of 2024 average nine figures. Everyone hired since averages eight figures.

The 2024 class is the surprise. That year Anthropic granted 1.28B options at $1.30 a share. At $118, that one year of grants is worth about $133B.

Then there is the tender. In April, holders could sell at $25.91 a share. Investors lined up $6B, but only $4.7B sold. 

Weeks later, Series H priced at $58.90 a share. At $2T, the people who held would be up 4.6x. And Dario and Daniela Amodei were among the sellers. 

The 7 founders have pledged 80% of their equity to charity. That is about $159B at $2T. But the S-1 says the pledges are not legally binding.

the noise first:

the domain is verified with Google. this is a paid Workspace account, not a gmail alias.

4. who did it
these records sit in the same Cloudflare account that runs the site. only the domain owner can add them. 

this is the team.

what it tells you: agents don't need inboxes.

teams talking to partners, exchanges, lawyers, auditors and institutions do. every one of those conversations starts with "send it to your company email."

this is the boring setup you do before you have a public face.

quiet onchain.

busy behind the domain.

author: mdudas
quoted_text:
It's been a long time coming... But it's finally time

Part of evolving as a business is recognising where your focus should be while remembering who your users are. 

The reality is that we spent an incredible amount of time purpose-building a network that is specifically designed to cater to HFT and everything that it encompasses. 

Execution needed to be faster and limitations to throughput hindered our ability to run real time risk checks as we think about scaling to 100,000 to 1,000,000 users and beyond. 

For those who have been following along, its no secret that there has been friction between how we execute and what the preference is from Solana leadership. 

I understand and respect their stance, however to continue to frame BULK a solana dex would be reductive to the actual offering, so we’re officially putting this on the record. 

The stronger case is that multichain access expands BULK’s distribution and usable capital while bringing more activity into the same market.

Distribution follows where users hold their money.

As more people enter crypto through neobanks, wallets and payment applications, their first chain may simply be whichever network their provider uses. Their choice of trading venue will depend on execution quality, liquidity and convenience.

Requiring those users to move to a particular chain before they can trade creates an acquisition barrier: another transaction, another fee, another interface and another opportunity to abandon onboarding. It also asks wallets and neobanks to move customers away from their existing infrastructure to integrate BULK.

Multichain access lets BULK meet that distribution where it already exists. A wallet or neobank could offer its customers BULK markets through the rails they already use.

The lesson from multicurrency products like Wise is that a single financial relationship can span across several underlying currencies and payment systems. We expect users to increasingly demand the same convenience across chains.

A unified clearing layer can make capital more productive and markets more liquid.

The strongest clearinghouse analogy is capital efficiency. Traditional clearing infrastructure brings eligible collateral and positions into a common risk framework, allowing qualifying exposures to offset and reducing the capital required to support them. 

This today belongs to CME Group.

For BULK, the opportunity is to connect capital held across supported chains to a common margin system and shared order book. A trader’s access to liquidity should not depend on which chain funded their account. A market maker should be able to serve that combined demand through the same BULK markets.

This creates an economic advantage: more sources of capital and order flow can support deeper books; deeper books can improve execution; better execution can attract more traders and integrations.

That advantage depends on keeping liquidity concentrated. Multichain access should bring users into the same markets, with eligible collateral recognized under a consistent risk framework. It should also let users withdraw available capital through supported destination chains, making BULK useful within their wider financial activity.

BULK’s specialised execution layer gives it a natural role connecting these rails.

BULK is a purpose-built trading L1 rolled into an order book, matching engine and risk engine. Its value comes from how efficiently it executes trades and manages risk. That specialization gives it a reason to serve capital from multiple ecosystems.

Today, collateral lives on Solana, and BULK’s ledger tracks the corresponding balances, positions and margin. Extending that model to supported networks such as Arc, Tempo, Arbitrum and HyperEVM would allow more funding and withdrawal routes to connect to the same execution system.

The architectural principle is to handle each chain’s confirmation and settlement requirements at the funding boundary. Once collateral is securely recognised, trading should run through BULK’s own execution and risk process. This allows BULK to preserve its performance while broadening access.

The intended experience is straightforward: fund from a supported chain, trade against BULK’s shared liquidity, and withdraw available balances to a supported destination. A user could enter from Solana and exit on HyperEVM, with BULK coordinating the accounting, settlement and destination liquidity required.

For wallets and neobanks, that would make BULK an exchange and clearing integration they can use across their supported networks. Each additional rail would expand access to the same venue, and strengthen the market already serving everyone else.

我最近和不少做CS的人聊了才知道不同行的认知区别有多大。由于数学和CS本身是闭合系统，大部分的问题都是Math-like的，即验证是几乎免费的，困难在于极大的解空间。这种问题AI/SI极其擅长，N-S Clay问题的解决就代表了在类似的问题上SI的能力已经超越了任何活着的人类的加和。

然而这个世界上大部分的问题其实是没有办法自验证的，换言之，验证本身是在Agent存在的闭合环境之外的。比如物理实验，虽然有正确答案，但是这个正确答案本身是不能被Agent本身验证的，Agent只能通过数学建模对问题做模拟验证，真正的正确答案是在系统之外的。这个问题最好的例子就是制药，验证本身是受到客观世界的限制的，几乎没有试错机会，而且时间极其长。

然而这种问题往往可以做成某种形式的优化问题，即人类可以制定一个好/坏评判标准。而对AI真正的挑战是在这种问题上，让SI能做到比人类更好，甚至好几个数量级的判断力。这正是科学Benchmark比如TB Sci的价值。恰恰是因为科学本身是极为长尾分布的，在这些问题上面的表现才能凸显AI本身的对现实世界的理解。所以看到Kimi 3.1 Pro在科学问题上的表现的时候，说实话还挺失望的，因为这些问题才是真正考验AI是否能被SI的场合。

text:
既然讲完了谷歌与微软的财报，顺便前瞻下凌晨亚马逊的财报！

亚马逊在本周三大云厂商所处的位置非常关键——二次验证，恰好谷歌财报有瑕疵，那么亚马逊的财报就有点重要了，能否提振云厂商企业的信心，就要看亚马逊了！

亚马逊的财报验证逻辑同样看五大要素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引+AWS

而验证逻辑可以是：AWS 增长 → AI CapEx → AWS 利润率 → FCF → Q4/2027 指引，而且相比微软与谷歌，亚马逊的压力更加直接，市场直接要通过财报得出一个结论——AI投入能不能快速转化为现金流

营收：＞203B优秀，201-203B及格符合预期，199-201B偏弱，＜199B明显差，不过营收在今晚的财报中比重较低，因为核心AWS才能决定估值

AWS：今晚第一核心，Q2 AWS 42.2B，同比增长37%，AWS营业利润达到16.6B，也就是说AWS是亚马逊承担AI增长故事+利润故事的核心，目前主流预期45.4B，对应同比应该是40%，所以AWS要关注增速能否达到40%。＞40%非常优秀，41%就大超预期，37%-40%符合预期，34%-37%及格但是偏弱，＜34%则意味着很差，尤其是如果今晚财报显示资本支出继续扩大，但是核心AWS业务增速不及格，就又是跟谷歌一样。

AI资本支出：Q3验证逻辑改变，并不是数字越大越好，Q2 亚马逊已经将资本开支扩大到220B，所以今晚如果资本开支保持增长趋势220B-230B，那必须要搭配AWS ＞40%的增速+backlog增长+AWS利润率稳定，才能支撑利好，否则反而是利空。

自由现金流：亚马逊最大的隐患，Q2财报中显示过去十二个月的经营现金流161.4B，同比增长33%，但是自由现金流为负7.6B，这意味着Q2面对高速增长的经营现金流依旧在挤压FCF，那么Q3想要让FCF 转为正值难度很大。所以今晚对于亚马逊的自由现金流要做预期降级，不能希望直接转为正值，而是看数字是否继续恶化，如果相比Q2数字不在恶化，算是好事。

AWS利润率：这是很容易被市场忽略的指标，AWS作为亚马逊的核心业务，在业务增长的前提下如果无法保证利润率，将会削弱业务增长带来的利好，Q2的利润率39.3%左右，那么今晚对应38-40%就算不错，如果搭配AWS业务增长40%，算是一个优秀组合。

未来指引：如果说财报是给过去一个答案，未来指引就是引导未来预期，目前主流分析营收指引约在239B-246B，中值242.5B，营业率利润29B-34B左右，今晚的管理层指引关键看三个关键词：AWS 容量、AI需求、2027年资本开支，如果AWS需求仍然超过可用算力，属于利好，这意味着未来AWS增速是受到算力供给限制而并非市场需求限制。

简单总结：

其实谷歌财报瞎吃对于亚马逊反而是一件好事，才本周三大原厂商财报公布前，对于三家企业的预期都非常强，加上上游海力士强劲财报压力，其实给三大云厂商的带来更多的压力溢价，而谷歌财报瑕疵导致AI企业估值调整，反而算是给后续亚马逊的解除了一定的预期压力

接下来，三家原厂商，如果亚马逊可以拿出一个及格线以上的财报，那么美股的信心也会逐渐回归，本周美股表现如何，就要看亚马逊能否给出一个满意的答卷了，否则面对目前的宏观压力，美股周五可能会表现不佳！

quoted_text:
看完谷歌在看微软财报，同样是财报后，微软为何可以盘前上涨？

微软的财报依旧是延续谷歌的分析模式，看五大因素：营收+AI资本支出+自由现金流+未来指引+Azure or AI monetization 

营收：优秀，增长重新加速，营收、营业利润、每股收益（EPS）及云业务表现均超出预期

AI资本支出：非常高，而且资本扩张下有Azure和AI收入增长保证，属于有效健康的扩张性资本开支，相比谷歌的资本支出让市场信心更强

自由现金流：依旧保持增长，在一年超过千亿级别的AI基础建设投资下，依旧保持FCF正值，虽然自由现金流还在被资本支出压制，但是有业绩保障，起码可以保持收支平衡

Azure：核心业务依旧是财报最强数据，同比48%增长，而回归前几个季度，从39%一路涨到现在的48%，Azure在如此庞大的收入基础上依旧在重新加速，进一步证实了微软的AI商业化更加完善

未来指引：预计下一季度Azure恒定汇率提升至49%-50%，一旦下个季度数据达成，将会继续证明Azure增长仍然处于加速阶段

AI Monetization：微软的人工智能变现并不只是来自Azure的48%增长，Foundry收入同比超过3倍，客户数量超过12万+，而在Foundry开源模型上的收入增长10倍，这意味着微软把从模型→Agent→Azure计算→企业部署做成一个完整平台

另外 Copilot也在稳定增长，结合Azure与Foundry，基本上验证了微软在AI 基础设施 + AI 平台 + AI 应用三个层面的盈利能力

其实看完微软的财报要素在对不谷歌，两者其实差距没有想象的那么大，但是微软却比谷歌多了一个核心，那就是证明了自家的AI产业赚钱，而且是全方位的在赚钱，虽然自由现金流并未加速增长，但是已经达到暂时的收支平衡，而这份数据正好踩到市场最想看到的结果上

不过，还是那句话，对于谷歌与微软来说，核心云业务依旧很强，基本面没问题，只不过短期市场在宏观压力下，更愿意为微软的财报与估值买单！

めちゃくちゃ良い。クレジット市場からAntのIPOを眺めると全く別の景色が見えてくる

- 信用市場は、ハイパースケーラーのBSからどれだけ離れているかによって業界を序列化している。信用スプレッドはCoreWeaveが約1,066bp、Oracleが年初144bpから約308bp、SpaceXが過去最高の226bp、Metaが108bp、NVIDIAが101bpとなっている

- Anthropicの報道ベースの1,000億ドル、Metaが10月26日に開始した350億ドル、さらに計画中の600億ドルなどを合わせると、AI企業は1年以内に株式市場へ約3,400億ドルを求めることになる。しかもFRBは利上げ中だ。まだ開いているのが株式市場という窓であり、多くの企業が同時にそこを通ろうとしている

- 9月30日までの6カ月間に公開されたモデルがQ3売上高の80%超を生み、9月の新モデルでは、タスク当たりコストがFable 5.1で約25%、Opus 5.5で約40%低下した。40%の値下げに売上を維持するだけでも、利用量を約3分の2増やす必要がある

売上はモデル公開と値下げに連動して段階的に増える。その増加幅が小さくなった時期に、長期契約の請求が届き始める

Anthropicにとっては賢い設計だが、リスクを負担する余力が最も乏しい供給企業にリスクを移している。柔軟な契約の層にいるのが、ネオクラウドだ

- Anthropicが計上した転換証券の公正価値変動による724億ドルの費用は、同じ再評価を反対側からAmazonとAlphabetが行うANT株が取引されるようになれば、その株価は四半期ごとにAmazonとAlphabetの営業外利益へ反映され、ANT株の不振は指数構成比率の大きい2社の利益未達につながる。両社にはIPOの需要を強く保つ直接的な利害がある

quoted_text:
今天又有幸和 @otzgary 大佬聊天，聊到了一个很有意思，也有点可怕的话题。

以前我们总说，基因编辑、胚胎筛选这些技术存在巨大的伦理问题。

因为它可能让富人的后代变成“超级人类”，更聪明、更健康、更强大，最终与普通人形成一道难以跨越的鸿沟。

但今天突然意识到，这件事好像已经在发生了。

只不过不是通过生物技术，而是通过计算机技术。

有钱的人可以买到更贵、更新、更强大，甚至近乎无限的 AI 算力和模型服务。他们可以借助 AI 获得远超普通人的认知能力、信息处理能力和决策能力。

而站在更顶端的模型厂商，甚至拥有大众根本接触不到的内部模型、更高的算力预算，以及处理复杂任务的能力。

过去我们担心的是，财富会决定下一代的智商上限。

现在我们面对的是，财富正在决定这一代人的智能上限。

以前有钱可以买时间、买资源、买教育。

现在，有钱甚至可以直接买“智能”。

更可怕的是，这种优势可能会不断自我强化：更强的智能创造更多财富，更多财富又可以买到更强的智能。

这和我们曾经担心的基因技术造成的阶层固化，本质上又有多大区别？

未来怎么办呢？

当智能开始成为一种可以用钱购买的资源，人类社会真正的分水岭已经变成了是谁能负担得起更聪明的 AI。或者说谁有资源能拿到更聪明的AI

text:
trade[XYZ] launched its first market on Hyperliquid 381 days ago. Today, we are joining forces with ICE, parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, to bring perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to U.S. regulated markets.

I don’t usually write long posts, but today merits reflection.

For years, builders across this industry have worked to show that open, onchain markets could support price discovery, manage risk, and withstand stress to the standards of traditional market infrastructure, all while staying open when and where those markets aren’t. 

Our achievements stand on the shoulders of those builders. And today, the company that owns the New York Stock Exchange has chosen to build upon the work of every developer, trader, market maker, and user who took a chance on us and our markets. We share this moment with all of you.

Markets are shaped by their participants. A new generation of investors trades from their phones, across asset classes, at any hour of any day. Until Hyperliquid, the right infrastructure for those markets didn’t exist.

Building these markets was hard. It took novel approaches to pricing, funding, and risk, refined with real capital at stake, in markets that don’t close. It also meant earning the trust of the people trading on them. We’re honored that the community recognized that effort and responded in kind.

That trust is what allowed us to grow our volumes to a ~$1 trillion annualized run rate in just over a year, to help pioneer new instruments like pre-IPO perps, and to earn the confidence of storied institutions like S&P Dow Jones Indices. That’s why ICE has chosen trade[XYZ] as its exclusive partner to bring 24/7 perps to the U.S.

Shifts in technology have pushed markets toward greater transparency, better price discovery, and broader access: from the coffee house to the curb exchange, ticker tape to the telephone, the trading floor to digital exchanges.

ICE helped write that last chapter. In 1997, Jeff Sprecher bought a small power-trading technology business for $1. ICE launched as an electronic energy marketplace in 2000, helped digitize major commodity markets, and acquired the NYSE in 2013. It has grown exponentially because of this appetite for innovation. That’s the partner we wanted: a partner that looks forward and embraces progress.

Americans deserve access to the most innovative markets in the world, and the protections of U.S. regulation. With trade[XYZ] and ICE, subject to regulatory approvals, they’ll have both.

The difference isn’t just access. Perps don’t expire, so traders never have to roll positions, and liquidity concentrates in a single deep market for each asset. Cross-margining enhances capital efficiency by letting one pool of collateral back positions across stocks, commodities, and crypto. Underpinning it all are atomic clearing and settlement, real-time risk management that enables continuous markets, and universally applied rules that anyone can verify. This is the next chapter we’ll write together.

My responsibility, our responsibility, is to now build markets worthy of the confidence our partners and our users have placed in us. Our commitments will not waver: to fair and transparent markets, to diverse markets, to low costs of execution, and above all, to market integrity.

All of this in pursuit of one thing:

A universal exchange, open around the clock, coming to the United States.

We’re proud to have deployed more than 100 markets on trade[XYZ]. But measured against the opportunity ahead, we’ve barely started. There is an enormous universe of assets we haven’t reached, alongside things people want to trade that have no established market at all. Wherever there is demand to trade an asset, we want trade[XYZ] to be where its price is discovered.
Global stocks, commodities, bonds, pre-IPO companies, compute, new indices, digital assets, interest rates, equity baskets, volatility products, alt assets… Anything. Anytime. Anywhere.

Ultimately, everything you own should work with everything you trade. Picture a headline breaking on Saturday night. You should be able to post tokenized shares as collateral, hedge your portfolio with an index perp, add exposure to oil, and take a view on a company that has not yet gone public. All in one account, all on one risk engine, before any traditional market opens. trade[XYZ] and Hyperliquid were built for this.

I hope someone opens their first investment account years from now to find that trivial, and to wonder why their predecessors needed so many separate financial relationships. Getting there will take liquidity, reliability, trust, and prices people have reason to believe. It will take years. I’m prepared to spend them.

Finally, a few thank yous.

First to the XYZ team: For the tireless nights and for committing to this vision before it was obvious.

To Jeff Sprecher and ICE, with special thanks to Michael Blaugrund and Trabue Bland who championed us throughout: You’re a world-class, technology-embracing team that proves innovation and scale are in fact not at odds.

To Stan Druckenmiller: For your partnership and helping us turn the next page.

To Hyperliquid Labs: For being the best partners we could ask for. You set an impossible standard, one we continually strive to meet. @chameleon_jeff, @iliensinc, @xulian_hl

And most importantly, to our users: You traded these markets when no one thought it mattered.

Guess what? It did.

quoted_text:
trade[XYZ] and ICE, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, are joining forces to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States.

In just over a year, our markets on Hyperliquid have surpassed $650 billion in volume. They provide continuous price discovery for stocks, indices, and commodities, and have become trusted reference points for retail and institutions alike when traditional markets are closed. Much of the world trades them. Until now, Americans could only watch.

We intend to change that. Subject to CFTC approval, trade[XYZ] and ICE plan to establish a new, dedicated U.S. market, with novel exchange and clearing infrastructure built on Hyperliquid. Planned contracts span equities, indices, commodities, FX, and crypto, with access through participating brokers and platforms. We’ll share more on products, eligibility, and timing as approvals progress.

ICE brings more than 25 years of experience operating regulated markets, clearing, and managing risk. trade[XYZ] brings the product development, market design, and technology behind the most liquid and robust markets on Hyperliquid. 

Innovation and the protections of U.S. regulation shouldn’t be a trade-off. Together, we plan to prove it.

ICE is making a strategic investment in trade[XYZ] and joins us in building towards the future of Hyperliquid. A small group of market luminaries is joining as well, beginning with Stan Druckenmiller. For more than four decades, few investors have anticipated the great turns in markets as often as Stan. We’re proud to have him with us for the next one.

We’re building the U.S. market in parallel with our existing HIP-3 markets, which we’ll continue to expand and innovate on. We expect both to flourish. They each have a long road map ahead, from new asset classes to new ways to trade them.

To the Hyperliquid community, whether you were here before us or came because of us, thank you. You took a chance on new markets and you made them matter. You’ll forever be a part of this story.

Anything. Anytime. On ICE[XYZ].

🚨 BREAKING: Hackers are hitting banks in 7 countries at the same time.

This is what Covid looked like in week 1. A few countries. Small numbers. Nobody called it a crisis.

1/ South Korea: hackers used a Chinese AI tool to break into at least 7 financial firms. 68,000 people's data stolen. 16 firms breached by mid-October. This week Daishin Securities reported 38,490 customers' data leaked, bank account numbers included.

2/ Latin America: one gang ran AI agents built on Claude, Grok and Kimi against 400+ targets, banks and payment firms included. They stole passwords and got into customer bank accounts.

3/ Italy: a fake WhatsApp from "the CEO" and an AI-cloned voice got Intesa Sanpaolo's private bank to send out €95 million. €36 million is still MISSING, turned into crypto.

4/ India: small lenders lost ₹300 crore (about $31 million) in 2 months. 150 cases. Hackers copied bank logins and sent the money out as fake loans. One firm was hit twice.

5/ Crypto: $351 million drained from Bitget's hot wallets. North Korean hackers are suspected.

6/ Japan: hackers hit GMO Internet's currency trading service and demanded $50 million in crypto. The prime minister promised an emergency anti-cyberattack package.

7/ Australia: the regulator warns AI attacks put more than A$4.5 trillion in retirement savings in the firing line. Government cyber alerts jumped 80% in a year.

Now zoom out.

AI hacking tools are now easy to get. Smaller firms have weak security. The money moves in minutes. It jumps across banks, through rented accounts, out as cash or crypto. The bosses are often abroad.

Covid locked the streets. Nobody is calling this a crisis yet. But the central banks already plan for the day the hackers get in.

The G7 agreed to run drills that simulate AI attacks on banks. The ECB reportedly gave eurozone banks 4 months to hand in their defence plans.

If your savings sit in a bank, hit follow. I'm tracking where the hackers strike next and how much they take.

text:
继被标普 500 拒之门外后，Strategy 的资本飞轮正迎来传统金融体系最严峻的一次审查。

国际指数编制巨头 MSCI 定于 11 月 11 日公布成分股筛选结果。由于新规重点排查“缺乏实质运营资产”的投资载体，Strategy 以及日股 Metaplanet 等比特币金库概念股，均被列入潜在剔除名单。

最直接的冲击是抛压。

据摩根大通测算，若被剔除出 MSCI，跟踪该指数的被动基金将带来约 28 亿美元的卖盘；若其他主流指数跟进，抛售总额恐攀升至 88 亿美元。

（不过需明确，这是二级市场对美股的被动调仓减持，并不等于公司被强制抛售比特币储备。）

但真正致命的其实是融资生命线。Strategy 过去能够持续大规模加仓比特币，高度依赖在美股溢价增发股票、优先股以及可转债。

指数被动配置资金此前是其重要的买盘底仓，一旦失去这层支撑，加上市场对股权稀释的担忧，未来继续通过“发债发股买币”的资本飞轮将急剧承压。

Michael Saylor 虽然指责 MSCI 搞“带有偏见的价值判断”，但在传统资管的框架下，当一家上市公司的主营业务几乎等同于囤币，它与华尔街基准规则的正面交锋，终究还是到来了。

text:
谷歌盘后大跌超9%，市场用脚投票：搜索广告低于预期、自由现金流转负91亿，AI似乎在蚕食核心业务现金流。

电话会上，Sundar Pichai把当前阶段直接对标十年前移动端转型：「就像十年前我们转向移动端一样，我们专注于先打造最佳搜索用户体验，然后再实现变现。」

首席商务官Philipp Schindler则坦承结构性问题：「AI模式搜索量的强劲增长带来了影响，因为我们在AI模式下看到了较低的变现率。」但他补充，多数AI查询是增量，平均长度是传统搜索的三倍，广告实验已显示积极信号，正在扩大覆盖。

自由现金流的黑洞，CFO Anat Ashkenazi解释得更直白——TPU系统的时间差：

「当我们与客户签订销售TPU系统的协议后，你首先会看到这些在我们的积压订单中体现。然后我们开始建立库存——从现金角度，我们先把现金花出去建立库存，之后才获得收入流。」

她明确指引：部分TPU收入已开始确认，但更大规模将在2027年到来。云积压已达5610亿美元。

Pichai把2027年称为「生产力黄金年」。内部部署Gemini 4 Argon后，他说这已成为「见过的最有意义的内部软件工程生产力杠杆之一」，代码产出和质量出现明显拐点。

但Ashkenazi同时警告：2027年资本开支将「显著增加」，Q4搜索和云利润率仍将承压。

故事讲完了。市场接下来要验证的是两件事：AI带来的增量查询，最终能否转化为与传统搜索相当甚至更高的广告价值；以及TPU从自用芯片变成对外平台后，那5610亿美元的积压，能不能在2027年真正变成现金流。

text:
英特尔明天凌晨公布三季报，服务器业务有机会带来一份略好于预期的成绩单，但财报后能否继续上修盈利预期，要看四季度的交付能力，以及新增收入能留下多少利润。

这家公司现在有一个很有意思的反差。PC市场仍在承压，市场对英特尔的收入预期却在向上走。AI带来的CPU需求，正在给它争取修复经营的时间。与此同时，先进制程和新工厂还要持续花钱

回到具体数字，我对三季度的判断是：收入164亿至168亿美元，中心大约166亿美元；调整后EPS 0.40至0.45美元，中心大约0.42美元；调整后毛利率42%至43%。这是我的推演，略偏向市场预期的上方。支撑主要来自服务器交付和产品组合改善，同时给PC端压力留出了一些余地。几个区间需要结合起来看，收入和毛利率都落在下沿时，不能再单独取EPS的上沿。

四季度方面，市场预期大约是171亿美元收入、0.44美元调整后EPS。我倾向于公司给出的收入指引中点在171亿至175亿美元，调整后EPS中点在0.44至0.50美元，调整后毛利率指引约42.5%至44%。这里说的是我对未来指引的预测。

如果三季度收入超过168亿美元、调整后EPS超过0.45美元，同时四季度收入指引中点达到176亿美元以上，毛利率向44%靠近，我会认为上调后续盈利预期的理由比较充分。这些是我用来区分结果强弱的参考线，股价反应还会受到此前预期和市场环境影响。

如果三季度只报到160亿至163亿美元，则要看四季度能否补回来。交付延后和需求变弱，对后续判断的影响差别很大。

目前，我对服务器需求兑现的信心，高于对代工投资迅速产生回报的信心。英特尔确实得到了一个修复窗口，能用多长时间、修复到什么程度，要看这几季的执行。

亚马逊Q3前瞻:AWS这次增速得多高市场才能满意？个人基准判断三季度营收约2035亿美元，营业利润约270亿美元，AWS增速在40%左右。关于亚马逊财报核心的几点：
1、AWS增速卖方参考大致处在高30%的增速区间，但已经有机构看得更高。如果AWS增长40%，说明业务继续加速，成绩很好。部分资金在财报前已经按照更高的增长率做了准备，公布后可能还要再多看一步：四季度能否再快一点，明年的收入预测能否继续上调？

2、更关键的还是是普通企业开始花多少钱？
这也是看微软和谷歌财报要看的核心点，我会特别关注非前沿大模型客户。原因在于，少数模型公司的算力采购，可以在短时间内把订单数字推得很高。如果企业软件、传统行业和互联网应用也开始稳定增加消费，AWS未来增长的客户基础就会更广。这方面已经有一些实证。

3、自由现金流为负也是大概率的，当然市场更关心明年资本开支是什么情况，以及预期营收增速如何？

不认为资本开支一上调，就应该直接转向悲观。只要新产能能够较快投入使用，客户持续付费，较高投入可以有合理回报。所以市场需要更具体的证据：比如，新增收入是否跟得上投入速度；新一批服务器投入服务后，利用率和利润表现怎样。

text:
为什么比特币在8万美元附近，币圈的情绪却这么冷？因为比特币的价格，早已不能代表大多数散户的账户余额。

最核心的原因是很多人的主要仓位根本不在比特币，而在山寨币，跌了90%还能再跌90%。反复暴跌、解锁和追热点的亏损，消耗掉的不只是信心，还有继续参与的本金。有些人不是不想玩，是真的没钱再玩了。

留下来的人也没那么容易买单了。项目一上线就给出几十亿美元的完全稀释估值，产品和收入还没证明自己，未来几年的预期已经提前卖给散户。新叙事缺乏突破，旧概念换个包装继续发币，Meme又成了拼手速、拼信息差的存量博弈。经历过几轮收割，大家自然不愿意再轻易抬轿子。

而且资金也有了更多选择。币安10月15日公布代币化美股产品bStocks累计交易量已超过400亿美元，资产管理规模突破10亿美元。这不能直接证明山寨资金都去了美股，却说明美股资产正在争夺同一批用户的钱和注意力。当参与美股也能像买币一样方便，币圈项目凭什么让投资者继续为一个尚未兑现的故事付钱？

再叠加宏观不确定性，资金更难持续承担高风险。市场并非完全没有流动性，而是愿意流向山寨的增量资金不足，有限的资金还被越来越多的代币分散。

币圈缺的不只是一个新叙事，更是散户本金的修复、合理的入场估值，以及能持续兑现的真实需求。只有发币和解锁，没有让普通参与者赚到钱和留下来的理由，再热闹的故事也很难撑起下一轮行情。

text:
Sometimes it helps to think of trading like a business. Every business that lasts makes money because it provides something of value to someone who is willing to pay for it. In markets, that someone might be a hedger who needs to offload risk, a fund that is forced to rebalance or an impatient buyer who pays a spread for immediacy.

Most traders run this logic in reverse. It’s like opening a coffee shop because you love a particular street, then standing outside wondering why nobody comes in, instead of first finding where people actually want coffee and setting up there.

A business starts with the customer and the need and the location follows. Trading can work the same way, with the market chosen based on where the people paying for your service are.
author: AltcoinSherpa
quoted_text:
I think most people approach market selection backwards. They start with what they want to trade (a coin, index, stock, whatever) and then try to force a signal out of it. The market comes first and the edge is something they hope to find afterward.

The better approach is to start with the effect you’re trying to capture. Ask what behavior you’re exploiting, whether that’s momentum, mean reversion, some structural flow, etc. and then ask where you would expect that effect to actually show up.

Universe selection matters as much as the signal and sometimes more. A mediocre signal applied to the right set of markets can beat a brilliant signal applied to the wrong ones. Where you trade can matter more than how you trade.

> a reply, a quote or a DM share: 7.6x
> a follow from the post: 6x
> a repost: 1.5x
> a like: 1x
> a bookmark: 0

the negative actions weigh far more, a report is -355x a like, a mute -89x, "not interested" -79x and a block -47x

if X predicts someone is likely to mute or report your post, it ranks lower in their feed

reports get a big weight because they are rare, a report is over 1,000x less likely than a like

these rules decide how far a post can reach:

> if you have 50,000 followers or fewer, X can boost a new original post up to about 16th place in someone's feed
> the boost only works in the post's first 2 hours, and stops once the post has 200 views in the Home feed
> X boosts one post each time a feed loads, and it prefers posts that got the most likes per view from their first viewers
> after 48 hours, X stops putting your post in people's feeds
> your replies and reposts only show up in the feeds of people who follow you
> original posts can also reach people who don't follow you, X scores them 25% lower for those people
> when several of your posts compete for one person's feed, the 2nd keeps 62.5% of its score and the 3rd keeps 43.75%
> replies, quotes, DM shares and copied links only count when people find your post in their feed, so engagement from a group chat link adds nothing
> if X labels your post low quality, it shows a notice on it and people can't like, reply, repost, bookmark or share it, misinformation labels can limit it too

what I'd do with it (my read of the weights):

> post when you can reply in the first 2 hours
> write posts people want to quote, reply to or send in a DM
> reply back to accounts that follow you
> post originals when you want to reach new people

People ask me why I decided to make Galileo Club accessible to everyone rather than keeping it exclusive.

The answer is simple.

When I was starting out, my biggest limitation wasn’t ambition or willingness to work. It was access. I didn’t have the network, or experienced people around me to learn from.

I want to remove that barrier for others.

I also believe talent is incredibly difficult to identify through applications, follower counts, or public profiles.

Someone can be an exceptional growth operator and a terrible content creator. Someone else might have incredible market knowledge but absolutely no network.

Both bring different forms of value.

Over the coming weeks, we’ll start segmenting Galileo Club based on members’ backgrounds, skills, experience, and ambitions. This means more specialised channels, curated introductions, targeted webinars, private sessions, and eventually smaller circles built around specific opportunities.

The idea isn’t to give everyone the same experience. It’s to create an environment where people can find the right people and opportunities for their particular stage.

I’d rather discover talent through participation and contribution than reject it because someone doesn’t look impressive on paper.

Exclusivity should be a consequence of demonstrated value, not a barrier to discovering it.

That’s the philosophy behind Galileo Club.

Today, in collaboration with Anthropic, we’re excited to share rapid initial progress towards an antibody treatment for food allergy, which affects over 200 million people worldwide, discovered with the help of Claude.

At Divergence Labs, we believe that AI can unlock the next generation of antibody therapeutics with more effective mechanisms than before. Such mechanisms are urgently needed in food allergy, which involve overcoming one of the tightest affinity protein pairs in immunology, IgE and its receptor FcεRI, on mast cells.

Treatment with Xolair—the only approved antibody for food allergy—sequesters circulating IgE, but mast cells remain sensitized for weeks to months due to the extraordinarily slow dissociation of IgE from FcεRI.

We envision a treatment that actively pulls IgE off of FcεRI, without waiting for natural dissociation. Like picking a lock, this requires the right combination of geometry and force.

Our research team, working with Claude, ideated on mechanisms to accomplish this disruption, and converged on an antibody format with two arms with different functions and epitopes. Within one month, we designed, synthesized, and experimentally confirmed the biophysical function of the two arms, which we are now assembling into full therapeutic formats.

text:
Same AI wave, so why is Meta's ad business surging while Google's is stalling?

Google's Q3 results are out, and the core miss was advertising (I flagged this in my subscriber channel yesterday). Search ads came in at $63.3B, up 12% YoY, below the ~$65B consensus. The stock fell 10% after hours.
What's striking is that a week earlier Meta reported ad revenue of $63.1B, up 26% YoY, with impressions up 10% and price per ad up 14%: volume and price rising together. Two ad machines of similar size, both front-runners of the AI era, so why is one growing more than twice as fast as the other?

1. The core reason: AI pushes the two businesses in opposite directions

For Meta, AI works directly on the auction. Better conversion prediction, Advantage+ automated campaigns and generative creative all make the same impression more valuable to advertisers, so they bid more. That's where the 14% price increase comes from. AI hasn't changed what Meta's product is; it just makes recommendations and targeting more accurate. It's a pure tailwind.

For Google, AI first changes the product itself. AI Overviews and AI Mode turn ten blue links into a direct answer. Users click out less, each query has fewer ad slots, and monetization comes under pressure.

It's not that Google can't use AI to optimize ads. Schindler talked on the call about Gemini improving ad quality and AI Max. But those gains are being offset by the drag of the product transition. Put simply, Meta is using AI to upgrade the engine, while Google is using AI to replace the chassis, and it's normal not to go fast while you're swapping the chassis.

2. Ad inventory has completely different elasticity

Meta sells attention. Its unit of inventory is an impression in Feed and Reels, and that inventory can expand: algorithms increase time spent on recommended content, ad load can rise, and new surfaces open up (Reels, Threads, WhatsApp business messaging). That's how Meta grew impressions 10% and price 14% this quarter.

Google search ads sell intent. Its unit of inventory is a query with commercial intent, and Google doesn't create that inventory; it depends on whether the user wants to buy something right now. Ad slots on the traditional results page have long been full, so growth can only come from more commercial queries. That's exactly where this quarter's problem lies: query growth was the fastest in five years, but much of the incremental volume landed in AI Mode, and management admits AI Mode monetizes at a lower level. In other words, Google's inventory is growing, but the new inventory isn't on the shelves yet.

3. The data feedback loops differ in depth

Many of Meta's advertisers are e-commerce and DTC brands. Their conversion events flow back to Meta through the Pixel and the Conversions API, and Advantage+ shopping ads close the loop from impression to purchase inside the app. Meta's view of whether an ad actually drove an order keeps getting more direct.

Google's search signal is the query itself. It's a strong signal but a one-off one: Google sees less than Meta of what happens after the user clicks out. And as AI answers absorb some clicks, the traffic Google sends to advertisers' landing pages is still shrinking, which further weakens its ability to prove ROI to advertisers.

4. AI Mode monetization is still early, but its ceiling may be higher

In traditional search, one query is one ad opportunity; the user looks at the results page and leaves.
AI Mode is a multi-turn conversation. A user goes from "I want a laptop" to "under $1,000" to "which has the best battery life," and each turn is a new expression of intent. Multi-turn ads essentially split one session into multiple auctions. Google says AI Mode queries are on average three times as long as traditional searches, one in five includes voice, images or documents, and most AI Mode queries are incremental. These queries carry far richer intent than keywords, so in theory each query's ad value should be higher, not lower.

AI Mode conversations naturally move users from the top of the funnel to the bottom.

Traditional search is good at catching people who've already decided to buy. AI Mode can catch people who are still comparing and deliberating, a part of the decision process that used to belong to Xiaohongshu, Reddit and YouTube reviews. Google now has a chance to take it back.

The obstacles are obvious, of course. A generative answer naturally has room for fewer ad slots than a page of ten blue links. And user trust is where Google is more fragile than Meta: people are used to ads in a feed, but inserting ads into an AI answer that looks like neutral advice damages the credibility of search itself.

There's also self-cannibalization. As AI Mode monetization catches up, traditional search is being replaced at the same time. The net gain depends on whether the first curve's slope can outrun the second.

text:
Deepseek V4.1 flash 1017版本更新里提到了基于自反馈的强化学习（RL）训练技术。

自反馈强化学习（Reinforcement Learning with Self-Feedback）指的是：在强化学习训练过程中，不完全依赖外部“标准答案”或人工标注的奖励，而是让模型自己对自己的输出进行评估、批判或验证，把这些自我评价当作奖励信号（或奖励的重要组成部分），用来优化模型行为。

官方说明是：通过基于自反馈的强化学习，提升了模型从零开始构建完整项目的能力（游戏开发、3D 建模等“许愿式编程”场景）。

这类任务往往没有非常明确的“标准答案”（不像数学题有唯一解），很难只靠外部测试完全覆盖。自反馈机制让模型学会：在生成过程中自我检查、自我纠错对中间结果和最终效果做质量评估在较少提示和参考素材的情况下，通过短轮次交互直接交付相对完整的项目。

传统只靠外部结果奖励的 RL，在这种场景下信号太稀疏，模型很难学到“怎么把一个项目从头做完”。“许愿式编程”就是用户只给一个高层描述（“做一个故宫3D展示”或“做个网页赛车游戏”），模型需要自己规划、写多文件代码、调视觉/交互、处理各种隐性要求。这种任务：没有明确的 ground-truth 答案，中间步骤很多（长程Agent典型场景），早期错误会累积
最终质量难以用简单规则自动打分。

Reinforcement Learning with Self-Feedback提供更密集的中间奖励，减少对外部标注和人工偏好的依赖。

25-26 年社区有不少这个领域的论文，之前也看过一些，最新26年近期也有不少：

1/Post-Training Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning from Self-Feedback
用模型自身对答案的置信度作为内在奖励，生成偏好数据后做偏好优化（RLSF）
https://t.co/eeAN1um2wG

2/RLSR: Reinforcement Learning from Self Reward
模型自己当裁判（self-judging），无需标准答案就能提供奖励信号，实现自我改进
https://t.co/RJ2fnFraff

3/Reflect, Retry, Reward
模型答错后生成自我反思，再用第二次尝试成功与否来奖励反思过程（用了 GRPO）
https://t.co/CxTcLfxYBb

4/Self-Rewarding Language Models
模型既生成回答，又用 LLM-as-a-Judge 给自己打分，迭代训练
https://t.co/8vrUreTe7C

5/Self-Evolved Reward Learning for LLMs
奖励模型用自己生成的反馈迭代改进自己
https://t.co/DZzcvXjmfv

6/ReflexiCoder: Teaching LLMs to Self-Reflect on Generated Code and Self-Correct It via RL
用 RL 把“生成 → 反思 → 自我修正”的完整轨迹内化进模型权重，推理时不需要外部执行环境也能自我纠错
https://t.co/qmxcEHqRxm

7/ICRL: Learning to Internalize Self-Critique with Reinforcement Learning
联合训练 solver 和 critic，让模型把批判带来的提升真正内化成自己的能力，在 agent 任务上有明显增益
https://t.co/D9nVzzH74j

8/Self-Credit: Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Agentic RL via Intra-group Rescaling
针对长程 agent 任务中稀疏奖励的信用分配问题，用模型自己生成的 citation 做密集信用分配
https://t.co/WhZFPEKMZk

9/Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
系统性训练 agent 的主动反思能力，结合环境反馈和 RL
https://t.co/gbvjIvAcPy

10/ReVeal: Self-Evolving Code Agents via Iterative Generation-Verification
多轮生成-自我验证闭环的 RL，让生成和验证能力共同进化
https://t.co/BL2fv4byzW

text:
做空机构 Culper Research 宣布做空 AI 芯片公司 Cerebras（CBRS），指控其晶圆级芯片实际寿命可能只有两年左右，远短于上市文件采用的设备折旧年限。

问题出在热胀冷缩。Cerebras 把整片硅晶圆做成一颗巨型芯片，但晶圆与连接板受热膨胀的程度不同，反复升温降温可能损坏连接点。

CEO Andrew Feldman 此前宣称，公司发明了新型连接材料，解决了这个困扰半导体行业数十年的难题。Culper 却称，这种材料实际来自外部供应商 Paricon，相关产品早在 1980 年代就已出现。

按照 Culper 的调查，Cerebras 可能并未从硬件上彻底解决问题，而是靠软件减少温度波动：让晶圆部分闲置区域持续执行无效计算，避免温度骤降。

报告援引一名现任 Cerebras 解决方案架构师的公开讲话，称不执行这些计算可能损坏芯片；还称在软件中发现了「dummy tokens」字段，作为这一机制的佐证。

这也带来了高耗电问题。哈佛与 Meta 研究人员实测，Cerebras CS-3 闲置时的功耗仍相当于自身热设计功耗（TDP）的约 80%，而测试中的英伟达和 AMD GPU 约为 20%。

Culper 还采访了多名客户。一名客户称，设备运行约一年后就有一个区域发生故障，最终不得不更换整套系统；另一名客户称，其系统曾被更换两次。Culper 进一步根据芯片老化模型估算，Cerebras 晶圆的老化速度可能是 GPU 的 3–3.5 倍，使用寿命仅约 1.4–2.3 年。

Cerebras 在 2025 年 12 月的上市草稿中，将计算机设备预计使用年限列为 1.5–3 年；到了今年 4 月，招股书中的「数据中心及计算机设备」变成了 3–5 年。虽然两份文件的设备分类不同，但新的折旧年限更长，意味着每年分摊的成本可能更低，账面毛利率更高。Culper 按 2.25 年重新估算，认为公司今年上半年毛利率会从披露的 29.9% 降至 24%。

Cerebras 还与 OpenAI 签下了超过 200 亿美元的算力合作。按照招股文件，已承诺交付的每批算力服务期为 3–4 年，还可以延长至最多 5 年。如果芯片真只能使用两年左右，Cerebras 就可能需要在合同期内提前更换设备，增加资本开支。

text:
Bloomberg: "Early signs suggest that the credit market is approaching the limits of how much more debt it can absorb. One after another, yields are soaring into the double digits on bonds and loans funding the AI infrastructure buildout. Bankers are finding it more difficult to offload risk to insurers and other investors...With those jitters growing louder each week — and spurring, in turn, angst about the potential economic fallout — Citadel Securities is cautioning clients that even the biggest names in tech could get ensnared as they put their balance sheets behind scores of projects critical to their AI ambitions."

Years ago, I was debating the implications of the COVID outbreak with a client at 13D and I was expressed concerns about debt sustainability when he told me: "Never underestimate how much money there is in the world." That's stuck with me since and puts into perspective the extraordinary scale of AI buildout ambitions, which are running into the limits of what capital markets can provide. As I warned in my September report on "The AI Trade" (https://t.co/wQQNniS2kj):

"In the first five months of this year, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle borrowed as much as they had in the five years prior. Morgan Stanely expects AI-related debt issuance to top $570 billion this year, more than double any previous record. Just for a bit more context about the scale of the borrowing binge, here’s an FT recap of Goldman analysis:

'The numbers are just bonkers. Goldman Sachs said in a note earlier this month that US dollar investment-grade issuance had already exceeded $1.5 trillion so far this year, which put 2026 on track to beat the previous record-breaking blowout from the pandemic era. The bank had previously penciled in a total of $2.1 trillion for the whole of this year but now it thinks that may be looking too cautious. The average deal size is $1.7 billion, the biggest in the post-crisis era. This includes at least 20 deals at $10 billion or more at announcement—a size it describes as “jumbo”. (I’m old enough to remember when “jumbo” transactions were $1 billion or more, so thank you Goldman for making me feel ancient.) In the whole of 2025, there were just 12 deals on this scale and from 2022 to 2024, there were 15 in total.'

Market participants remain complacent about tech giants continuing to borrow at the rate they’re borrowing if borrowing costs keep rising. And if tech giants begin to pull back from the debt binge, it’ll ripple far beyond the bond market, through to everything from equities to consumer spending."

trade[XYZ] launched its first market on Hyperliquid 381 days ago. Today, we are joining forces with ICE, parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, to bring perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to U.S. regulated markets.

I don’t usually write long posts, but today merits reflection.

For years, builders across this industry have worked to show that open, onchain markets could support price discovery, manage risk, and withstand stress to the standards of traditional market infrastructure, all while staying open when and where those markets aren’t. 

Our achievements stand on the shoulders of those builders. And today, the company that owns the New York Stock Exchange has chosen to build upon the work of every developer, trader, market maker, and user who took a chance on us and our markets. We share this moment with all of you.

Markets are shaped by their participants. A new generation of investors trades from their phones, across asset classes, at any hour of any day. Until Hyperliquid, the right infrastructure for those markets didn’t exist.

Building these markets was hard. It took novel approaches to pricing, funding, and risk, refined with real capital at stake, in markets that don’t close. It also meant earning the trust of the people trading on them. We’re honored that the community recognized that effort and responded in kind.

That trust is what allowed us to grow our volumes to a ~$1 trillion annualized run rate in just over a year, to help pioneer new instruments like pre-IPO perps, and to earn the confidence of storied institutions like S&P Dow Jones Indices. That’s why ICE has chosen trade[XYZ] as its exclusive partner to bring 24/7 perps to the U.S.

Shifts in technology have pushed markets toward greater transparency, better price discovery, and broader access: from the coffee house to the curb exchange, ticker tape to the telephone, the trading floor to digital exchanges.

ICE helped write that last chapter. In 1997, Jeff Sprecher bought a small power-trading technology business for $1. ICE launched as an electronic energy marketplace in 2000, helped digitize major commodity markets, and acquired the NYSE in 2013. It has grown exponentially because of this appetite for innovation. That’s the partner we wanted: a partner that looks forward and embraces progress.

Americans deserve access to the most innovative markets in the world, and the protections of U.S. regulation. With trade[XYZ] and ICE, subject to regulatory approvals, they’ll have both.

The difference isn’t just access. Perps don’t expire, so traders never have to roll positions, and liquidity concentrates in a single deep market for each asset. Cross-margining enhances capital efficiency by letting one pool of collateral back positions across stocks, commodities, and crypto. Underpinning it all are atomic clearing and settlement, real-time risk management that enables continuous markets, and universally applied rules that anyone can verify. This is the next chapter we’ll write together.

My responsibility, our responsibility, is to now build markets worthy of the confidence our partners and our users have placed in us. Our commitments will not waver: to fair and transparent markets, to diverse markets, to low costs of execution, and above all, to market integrity.

All of this in pursuit of one thing:

A universal exchange, open around the clock, coming to the United States.

We’re proud to have deployed more than 100 markets on trade[XYZ]. But measured against the opportunity ahead, we’ve barely started. There is an enormous universe of assets we haven’t reached, alongside things people want to trade that have no established market at all. Wherever there is demand to trade an asset, we want trade[XYZ] to be where its price is discovered.
Global stocks, commodities, bonds, pre-IPO companies, compute, new indices, digital assets, interest rates, equity baskets, volatility products, alt assets… Anything. Anytime. Anywhere.

Ultimately, everything you own should work with everything you trade. Picture a headline breaking on Saturday night. You should be able to post tokenized shares as collateral, hedge your portfolio with an index perp, add exposure to oil, and take a view on a company that has not yet gone public. All in one account, all on one risk engine, before any traditional market opens. trade[XYZ] and Hyperliquid were built for this.

I hope someone opens their first investment account years from now to find that trivial, and to wonder why their predecessors needed so many separate financial relationships. Getting there will take liquidity, reliability, trust, and prices people have reason to believe. It will take years. I’m prepared to spend them.

Finally, a few thank yous.

First to the XYZ team: For the tireless nights and for committing to this vision before it was obvious.

To Jeff Sprecher and ICE, with special thanks to Michael Blaugrund and Trabue Bland who championed us throughout: You’re a world-class, technology-embracing team that proves innovation and scale are in fact not at odds.

To Stan Druckenmiller: For your partnership and helping us turn the next page.

To Hyperliquid Labs: For being the best partners we could ask for. You set an impossible standard, one we continually strive to meet. @chameleon_jeff, @iliensinc, @xulian_hl

And most importantly, to our users: You traded these markets when no one thought it mattered.

Guess what? It did.

quoted_text:
trade[XYZ] launched its first market on Hyperliquid 381 days ago. Today, we are joining forces with ICE, parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, to bring perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to U.S. regulated markets.

I don’t usually write long posts, but today merits reflection.

For years, builders across this industry have worked to show that open, onchain markets could support price discovery, manage risk, and withstand stress to the standards of traditional market infrastructure, all while staying open when and where those markets aren’t. 

Our achievements stand on the shoulders of those builders. And today, the company that owns the New York Stock Exchange has chosen to build upon the work of every developer, trader, market maker, and user who took a chance on us and our markets. We share this moment with all of you.

Markets are shaped by their participants. A new generation of investors trades from their phones, across asset classes, at any hour of any day. Until Hyperliquid, the right infrastructure for those markets didn’t exist.

Building these markets was hard. It took novel approaches to pricing, funding, and risk, refined with real capital at stake, in markets that don’t close. It also meant earning the trust of the people trading on them. We’re honored that the community recognized that effort and responded in kind.

That trust is what allowed us to grow our volumes to a ~$1 trillion annualized run rate in just over a year, to help pioneer new instruments like pre-IPO perps, and to earn the confidence of storied institutions like S&P Dow Jones Indices. That’s why ICE has chosen trade[XYZ] as its exclusive partner to bring 24/7 perps to the U.S.

Shifts in technology have pushed markets toward greater transparency, better price discovery, and broader access: from the coffee house to the curb exchange, ticker tape to the telephone, the trading floor to digital exchanges.

ICE helped write that last chapter. In 1997, Jeff Sprecher bought a small power-trading technology business for $1. ICE launched as an electronic energy marketplace in 2000, helped digitize major commodity markets, and acquired the NYSE in 2013. It has grown exponentially because of this appetite for innovation. That’s the partner we wanted: a partner that looks forward and embraces progress.

Americans deserve access to the most innovative markets in the world, and the protections of U.S. regulation. With trade[XYZ] and ICE, subject to regulatory approvals, they’ll have both.

The difference isn’t just access. Perps don’t expire, so traders never have to roll positions, and liquidity concentrates in a single deep market for each asset. Cross-margining enhances capital efficiency by letting one pool of collateral back positions across stocks, commodities, and crypto. Underpinning it all are atomic clearing and settlement, real-time risk management that enables continuous markets, and universally applied rules that anyone can verify. This is the next chapter we’ll write together.

My responsibility, our responsibility, is to now build markets worthy of the confidence our partners and our users have placed in us. Our commitments will not waver: to fair and transparent markets, to diverse markets, to low costs of execution, and above all, to market integrity.

All of this in pursuit of one thing:

A universal exchange, open around the clock, coming to the United States.

We’re proud to have deployed more than 100 markets on trade[XYZ]. But measured against the opportunity ahead, we’ve barely started. There is an enormous universe of assets we haven’t reached, alongside things people want to trade that have no established market at all. Wherever there is demand to trade an asset, we want trade[XYZ] to be where its price is discovered.
Global stocks, commodities, bonds, pre-IPO companies, compute, new indices, digital assets, interest rates, equity baskets, volatility products, alt assets… Anything. Anytime. Anywhere.

Ultimately, everything you own should work with everything you trade. Picture a headline breaking on Saturday night. You should be able to post tokenized shares as collateral, hedge your portfolio with an index perp, add exposure to oil, and take a view on a company that has not yet gone public. All in one account, all on one risk engine, before any traditional market opens. trade[XYZ] and Hyperliquid were built for this.

I hope someone opens their first investment account years from now to find that trivial, and to wonder why their predecessors needed so many separate financial relationships. Getting there will take liquidity, reliability, trust, and prices people have reason to believe. It will take years. I’m prepared to spend them.

Finally, a few thank yous.

First to the XYZ team: For the tireless nights and for committing to this vision before it was obvious.

To Jeff Sprecher and ICE, with special thanks to Michael Blaugrund and Trabue Bland who championed us throughout: You’re a world-class, technology-embracing team that proves innovation and scale are in fact not at odds.

To Stan Druckenmiller: For your partnership and helping us turn the next page.

To Hyperliquid Labs: For being the best partners we could ask for. You set an impossible standard, one we continually strive to meet. @chameleon_jeff, @iliensinc, @xulian_hl

And most importantly, to our users: You traded these markets when no one thought it mattered.

Guess what? It did.

There is an enormous universe of assets we haven’t reached, alongside things people want to trade that have no established market at all. Wherever there is demand to trade an asset, we want trade[XYZ] to be where its price is discovered.
Global stocks, commodities, bonds, pre-IPO companies, compute, new indices, digital assets, interest rates, equity baskets, volatility products, alt assets… Anything. Anytime. Anywhere.

Ultimately, everything you own should work with everything you trade. Picture a headline breaking on Saturday night. You should be able to post tokenized shares as collateral, hedge your portfolio with an index perp, add exposure to oil, and take a view on a company that has not yet gone public. All in one account, all on one risk engine, before any traditional market opens. trade[XYZ] and Hyperliquid were built for this.

I hope someone opens their first investment account years from now to find that trivial, and to wonder why their predecessors needed so many separate financial relationships. Getting there will take liquidity, reliability, trust, and prices people have reason to believe. It will take years. I’m prepared to spend them.

Finally, a few thank yous.

First to the XYZ team: For the tireless nights and for committing to this vision before it was obvious.

To Jeff Sprecher and ICE, with special thanks to Michael Blaugrund and Trabue Bland who championed us throughout: You’re a world-class, technology-embracing team that proves innovation and scale are in fact not at odds.

To Stan Druckenmiller: For your partnership and helping us turn the next page.

To Hyperliquid Labs: For being the best partners we could ask for. You set an impossible standard, one we continually strive to meet. @chameleon_jeff, @iliensinc, @xulian_hl

And most importantly, to our users: You traded these markets when no one thought it mattered.

Guess what? It did.
