如何定位 Hyperliquid，以及如何看到 $240 的 hyperliquid:native

这两天看到新闻，智谱在招聘一个全新的岗位叫 Brand Narrative Manager，加密闭口不提的词汇「叙事」现在被 AI 拿去用了。不过我始终认为对于前沿领域的科技公司而言，叙事是最重要的战略能力之一——叙事可以扭曲现实力场，叙事可以编程目标受众的心智

回过头看 Hyperliquid 的叙事历史：从最早的公平发射的 Dex，到 APP L1，再到 Blockchain to House All Finance，最近升级为「Infra to House All Finance（金融领域的 AWS）」

规律肉眼可见：脱离应用层，迈向协议层；HL 不再是交易所，而是基础设施。把合规成本外包给 builders，把 Dex 的身份给 builders，保持自身定位的纯粹和干净，隔离合规风险，也是顶级阳谋了

至此，Hyperliquid 头上悬着的达摩利斯之剑很可能彻底消失了，之前社区还担心 Jeff 被抓怎么办，现在 HL 已经摇身一变成为下一代金融的正统新基建了

目前 Kraken 已经在测试 HIP-3 的白名单地址功能，xyz 也在针对美国市场（疑似）做新的产品，而 Hyperliquid 在产品上仅仅只做了一个白名单功能

我觉得很多人还没意识到，Hyperliquid+HIP 可能是进入美国市场的低成本最优路线——更透明的市场、天然资金自托管、审查友好的白名单功能...意味着更低的合规成本，意味着更少的证明

我们可以朴素预测未来的两种繁荣场景，一是更多 HIP-3 部署者，针对美国市场提供更多 dex 供给；二是美国机构、合格投资者的资金涌入 HL。这是 10x、100x 数量级的资金

one more thing，「金融领域的 AWS」定位还透露着巨大的野心和可能性，纳斯达克想实现资产上链、7*24 全球交易，基建供应商的 list 里，那个绿色葫芦很大概率成为首选

聊一下对 hyperliquid:native 的价格判断逻辑：最好的商业模式、最强的代币经济机制、最顶级的品牌定位与叙事，BTC 从 12w 下跌到 6w 反弹到 8w 这一次下跌里，HYPE 从 50 涨到了 80，韧性很强

判断逻辑一：

从盘感的角度看，当前 HYPE 有上轮牛初 $80 的 solana:So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 的即视感，而后者牛市高点涨到 $240

判断逻辑二：

从 AF 的 buying power 角度，把 HYPE 的年度回购能力，类比成一家公司的年度盈利，给 Hyperliquid 赋予基本面——「市回率 buyback multiple」，流通市值除以年化回购力：

- buyback multiple = HYPE 流动市值/年化 buyback power
- 回购收益率 = 年化 buyback power/HYPE 流动市值 = 1/buyback multiple

YTD 的年化回购能力在 $597M/年，市回率 29.85x，回购收益率 3.35%

buyback power 这个指标不仅反应了 Hyperliquid 的业务发展（收入和市占率），还代表着整个 crypto 的交易市场热度，如果以 buyback power 指标刻舟求剑的话，我做了一个 HL 价格预测模型：

统一控制变量
- 要求回购收益率：3.35%
- 对应 buyback multiple：29.85×，保守假设市回率保持不变，共识没有增强
- HL市占率：4.811% → 5.790%，保守假设 线性增长，没有加速度，一年线性增加约0.98个百分点
- 综合回购费率：2.1588 bps，包含 Core 与HIP-3
- HIP-3 收入结构不变，没有关掉 growth mode
- 业务保守扩张，没有推出新的收入机制
- 忽略质押、解质押、EVM 繁荣度影响
- 流通量：2.2245亿枚
- 不给予社区共识增强或估值倍数扩张
- 不计 BTC Beta 对市场价格的额外影响

统一控制变量的情况下，$HYPE 的理论价值粗略跟市场交易量、交易热度正相关

结论是：
- 全市场月交易量每增加 $1T
- 年化 Buyback Power 增加约 $150M
- HYPE 理论价值增加约 $20.13

预设三种市场交易热度阶梯，当前牛熊转化阶段、上轮牛市年度月平均、全样本趋势，分别对应 $6.7T、$7.74T、$9.48T 的月平均全网合约交易量，分别对应着 HL $1.005B、$1.161B、$1.42B 的一年后年化 buyback power

一年后 HYPE 理论价格分别是 $134.87、$155.83、$190.79

以上变量控制地非常保守，如果考虑 HL 市占率增长遵循当前加速度、更多利好出现、社区共识增强、BTC beta 牛市、宏观经济利好催化等因素，价格会比预期更高

判断三：

HYPE 达到 SOL 和 BNB 的当前市值，分别是 500 和 1000 亿，对应着 $ 250 和 $430 的价格

没什么逻辑，纯预测，坏消息是不太确定 crypto 还能否达到上一轮周期的热钱浓度，好消息是 90% 赛道证伪了，钱和共识会涌向头部项目

当然 hyperliquid:native 的走势颇有特色，必须回踩再上新台阶，要承受 30%-50% 的健康回调，换句话说，对于看好 HYPE 的人来说，回调 30% 就可以开始抄底加仓

text:
A FIELD GUIDE TO HEARTBREAK
Part 5 — Depression: When the Silence Finally Gets a Word In

Congratulations. You've survived denial, anger, and bargaining. Unfortunately, your reward is depression.

Grief operates like a particularly sadistic video game: every level unlocks a more unpleasant one.

Except this time, there's no boss to fight, no argument to win, and nobody left to negotiate with.

Just you. And a disturbing amount of silence.

At first, you almost welcome it. After weeks of emotional warfare, the absence of noise feels suspiciously like peace.

For approximately eleven seconds.

Then you discover that silence has an extraordinary talent for making everything you've been avoiding considerably louder.

Memories arrive uninvited, ordinary objects become historical artifacts, and a familiar song or perfume takes you somewhere you never meant to revisit.

Meanwhile, life demands your participation, oblivious to the catastrophe.

The refrigerator needs groceries, the laundry has established an independent government, and people still expect you to socialize. Frankly, the administrative burden of being alive seems excessive.

But you manage, at least from the outside. You work, answer questions, laugh at jokes, and appear functional, despite spending ten minutes staring at a wall.

You haven't listened to your favorite music in weeks. Hobbies that once filled afternoons seem like activities performed by someone you vaguely remember.

You want company until someone offers it. You want to talk until you consider explaining yourself. Even your emotional needs have stopped communicating with one another.

And then comes an unsettling discovery: you don't just miss the person who left. You miss yourself.

You miss the version of you who made plans, looked forward to things, and enjoyed an ordinary afternoon without feeling that happiness required an explanation.

You search for that person in familiar routines, only to discover that recognition isn't the same as connection.

It's a peculiar experience, becoming homesick for someone you've never actually stopped being.

Then comes the thought you've been avoiding.

What if this is just who I am now?

That's when depression becomes especially persuasive. It doesn't merely describe how miserable you feel today; it starts making predictions about tomorrow, next month, and every year you haven't lived yet.

Your brain, which recently tried negotiating with the universe, has promoted itself to Head of Long-Term Forecasting. Its qualifications remain questionable, but exhaustion can make even a terrible prediction sound convincing.

That's the cruelest part: pain can make it difficult to imagine anything beyond itself.

I wish I knew when that changes. I can't promise tomorrow will be wonderful or that what you've lost will return.

But a feeling, however overwhelming, is not a prophecy.

The person you miss being hasn't necessarily disappeared. You may be struggling to reach them, and you don't have to manage that today.

You don't have to turn suffering into wisdom or demonstrate impressive personal growth. If all you've managed today is to get through it, that counts. If even that feels impossible, please tell someone. You deserve support, not another impossible standard.

I'd like you to stay. Not because I can promise a spectacular ending, but because there are still pages you haven't read, conversations you haven't had, and possibilities you can't imagine from where you're standing.

You don't have to believe in a beautiful future today. Just don't let your worst moments write the entire story.

And if you'll stay with me, there's one uncomfortable conversation ahead. We've spent four chapters with the person left behind.

Next time, we're giving the person who walked away a chance to speak.

I expect this decision to be poorly received.

Next: The One Who Walked Away — And the One Who Came Back

my unfiltered thoughts on the data industry right now:

there are too many brokers in the data space. in the last 4 months this industry has become the new equivalent to dropshipping.

i have no issue with that. but if your entire moat is spam calling smb owners all day and begging them to license their data for a micro1 referral fee, you are not going to make it, and you are not the next mercor. most of you are not building anything at all.

to everyone reading this, and the hundreds of other posts on your timeline from 18 year old sf kids claiming $200m run rates please ignore them. these are the modern day elizabeth holmes’.

they're taking one day of contracted (not paid) revenue and multiplying it by 365. the worst i've seen is someone who made $100k off a micro1 referral fee in 6 hours and claimed they're at a $73m run rate (12 (daily working hours) / 6 x $100k x 365).

this is literal fraud, especially if you raise money off of this claim. you see this in a lot of yc companies in recent batches.

the only businesses i see surviving this are the giants that already exist (mercor, micro1, surge ai, turing) and the non consensus bets: consumer data collection apps like kled, robotics data collection companies like build ai and meckaai, etc.

tldr: don’t believe everything you read, and just brokering company data is not a venture scale business and should not be claimed as such.

quoted_text:
Wanted to address this because I think there’s some misunderstanding around how options are priced on Dream.

First, your position was a HYPE $90 call with HYPE trading around $81. That’s roughly 10% out of the money, with over a month left until expiration.

Despite being that far out of the money, you were still quoted around $44,000 to close a position you originally paid $48,000 for. That’s roughly 92% of your initial cost recoverable at that moment.

When you buy options, you’re paying upfront for leverage and convexity. The cost of an option depends on things like vol, expiration, and how far the underlying is from your strike. That doesn’t mean you’ll always be able to sell the option back at its mark price. Spreads are a separate part of options pricing and depend heavily on liquidity and the risk market makers take when quoting.

Now, regarding the 21% spread, there’s absolutely room for improvement. We’re actively working on improving liquidity and tightening spreads across every asset on Dream. I’m not going to pretend our execution is perfect because it isn’t.

I also want to clarify something about how we calculate PnL on Dream. We intentionally use the executable bid to calculate your PnL whenever your position is in profit. This means your green PnL is backed 1:1 by the amount you can actually cash out. If Dream shows you’re up $5,000, that’s exactly $5,000 in profit you can realize by closing your position at that moment. We’re never going to intentionally show users profits they can’t cash out.

As options move into the money, their value provides a stronger basis for liquidity. But Dream also supports closeouts for out of the money positions, as you can see here. Even with HYPE trading roughly 10% below your strike, you were still able to get a quote to recover 92% of your cost. Again, there’s room to improve spreads, but I think that’s important context.

Lastly, I think this highlights something bigger. Options are becoming increasingly popular with the onchain crowd, but there’s still a pretty big knowledge gap around how they actually work. We’re already working on educational content at Dream to make things like pricing, spreads, and liquidity easier to understand.

I get the frustration, and I’m not dismissing the criticism. There’s a lot we still need to improve, and we’re working on it every day. But I also think it’s important to distinguish between legitimate issues with execution quality and accusations that Dream or its market makers are deliberately taking advantage of users. Our business depends on people having a good experience and wanting to come back.

Statement on the $AXIS Sell-off of 28–29 October

Over the past two days, a series of addresses sold a large volume of $AXIS on-chain. We want to set out clearly what these tokens were and what we are doing about it.

1. No team or investor tokens were sold.
All Core Team and investor allocations, together with every other locked allocation, 835,000,000 $AXIS (83.5% of total supply), remain in the vesting contract, which is jointly administered with Binance: 0xAFE41cfd4C21f1D896678e32C5AD456ea41835e6. Anyone can verify the balance on BaseScan. Not a single token has left it, and none unlocks before the 12-month cliff.

2. Where the sold tokens came from.
The tokens sold came from the initial circulating supply set out in our published tokenomics, specifically part of the Ecosystem allocation. Many ecosystem recipients are not crypto-native, so their allocation was delivered through a single OTC counterparty, under a written agreement that includes lock-up terms.

3. What we believe happened.
The pattern of the sales, which went through exchange deposit routes and hundreds of fresh addresses within hours of delivery, strongly suggests that the OTC counterparty sold these tokens on the open market. If so, this is inconsistent with the agreement.

4. What we are doing.
- We have suspended all further dealings with this counterparty.
- We are reviewing the agreement with legal counsel and will pursue every remedy available under it.
- Going forward, any remaining Ecosystem tokens will be distributed only through on-chain vesting.

The team‘s tokens remain locked, and our commitment to building Axis is unchanged.

text:
Hyperliquid's spot markets: failed or major opportunity?

Hyperliquid won perps. HIP-3 then pulled stocks, indices and commodities onchain, and @tradexyz alone did ~$65bn in the last 30 days.

Spot was supposed to be the next leg. Rn it isn't:

- $3.7bn spot volume in the last 30d vs ~$224bn in perps. 1.6% of all HL volume, down from 5.3% in August 2025 (its peak)

- 347 spot pairs live, 234 of them printed $0 in the last 24h

- HYPE, UBTC, UZEC and UETH are 82% of all spot volume

- Robinhood Chain went live on the 1st of July and did $29.4bn in DEX volume over the same 30 days. 8x HyperCore spot.

What went wrong?

A few thoughts:

1) HyperEVM lost the onchain race

Too slow and too expensive vs RH Chain, Solana, Base and co. Small blocks still come every 1s with a 3M gas cap. Outside short hype phases like @papertrade_xyz there is little onchain activity, so spot assets on HL have little composability and little to do.

2) "Listed on Hyperliquid" never became the new "listed on Binance"

Early on it felt like it could, with HL as the spot hub for the entire space. Reality today looks different: few assets, thin books, and most new pairs are the "let's list there too" kind of thing, long after the token trades everywhere else. Not the place to trade new shiny tokens iykwim.

3) Perps are just too good

Even HYPE trades 8x more as a perp than spot ($321m vs $39m, last 24h). BTC: 88x. Same exposure, plus leverage, deeper books and no bridging.

RWAs are even more extreme. NVDA perp on tradexyz: $64m in 24h. NVDAX spot on HyperCore: $193k.

4) A CLOB might not be the right venue for everything

Order books need market makers, and for the long tail they don't show up. xStocks' first week on HyperCore averaged 18 bps spreads vs 0.1 to 1 bp on the matching tradexyz perps.

RFQ and propAMMs like Metric, where LPs quote around an oracle price, fit long-tail and RWA spot better. Metric did $664m on RH Chain alone in the last 30d and just went live 1-2 weeks ago in the first place btw.

5) The tokenized stock race is crowded

RH Chain, Solana, BNB and co all want to be where tokenized stock value lives. xStocks went live on HyperCore on the 10th of August, EQX now has 11 tickers listed. All tokenized equity spot on HyperCore combined: ~$520k in the last 24h.

So, failed?

As a listing and high-activity trading venue, yes. But only for now.

Bc the opportunity remains huge.

Think for example about spot as the hedge leg for HIP-3.

Basis trade = long spot, short perp, collect funding. It's what keeps funding in check on every big venue. On HL nobody can run it at size bc the spot leg barely exists for now.

At the current hourly rate the SpaceX perp on tradexyz pays shorts 14.5% annualized, GOOGL 24.9%. All SpaceX spot tokens on HyperCore did $21k combined in the last 24h.

Same story on @entropyIO: the Anthropic pre-IPO perp holds $57m in open interest, and there is no Anthropic spot token on HyperCore to hedge it with.

Deep RWA spot = basis traders = cheaper funding = more OI on the HIP-3 books.

That's a powerful flywheel yet to be unlocked.

@Enter_Elysium (tl;dr: @Kinetiq_xyz's L2 on HyperEVM, HYPE as gas, mainnet coming on the 9th of November, HyperCore access planned ~a month later) is the first serious attempt at the composability side, which is another key factor here.

If a real ecosystem of protocols forms on a programmable layer next to HyperCore, one that gives spot assets composability and actual utility without HyperEVM's scaling limits (exactly what Elysium is going for), I still think Hyperliquid is very well positioned to grow its spot side. Both for its own native assets and for tokenized stocks and other "foreign" assets.

What I'm watching:

- Elysium mainnet on the 9th of November, then the upgrade that lets its contracts read HyperCore data and route orders to it
- Book depth on xStocks, EQX and Dinari, not headline volume
- A propAMM like Metric live on HyperEVM (should come soon) and/or Elysium, or an RFQ venue plugged into HyperCore spot and perps
- Funding compressing on HIP-3 equity and pre-IPO perps

NFA in any way, shape or form either ofc. But there is definitely still potential here imo.

text:
Open access to open intelligence.

Ando has been selected as a @circle developer grant recipient. We’re grateful to Circle for supporting our work.

Open intelligence needs open money. That’s why Ando uses Circles @arc internet-native operating system for economic activity

An agent needs a model it doesn’t have. Today, a person has to step in: create an account, add a card, paste an API key into a config. Intelligence sits behind accounts built for people.

MPPI removes that gate. It’s an open protocol for agents to buy inference directly from other agents: https://t.co/dTIHGGsUsj

A provider registers its on-chain identity through ERC-8004 and publishes its models and per-token prices. The buying agent verifies the offer, funds a session in USDC and pays as it goes with signed vouchers. No provider account, no API key to provision and no on-chain transaction for every request. The provider collects only what the agent has authorised. Unused funds return when the session closes.

Ando Infer is the first provider agent on MPPI: agent #2706, a headless inference platform where payment grants access. https://t.co/tc33dQw9n3

Ando Wallet is where you set the terms. Fund it, connect your agents and give each its own key, on-chain identity and weekly spending limit. From there, agents transact directly, without a person approving each request.

Open intelligence needs open money. That’s why Ando uses Circle’s USDC and settles on @arc, where USDC also pays for gas. Agents can budget for inference and transaction costs in the same currency. Arc’s sub-second deterministic finality gives MPPI fast settlement for session funding, provider payments and refunds. Once those transactions are committed, both sides can act on the result without waiting for additional block confirmations.

Live on Arc mainnet.

Try Ando Wallet: https://t.co/mbre5QDfdl

quoted_text:
trade[XYZ] and ICE, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, are joining forces to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States.

In just over a year, our markets on Hyperliquid have surpassed $650 billion in volume. They provide continuous price discovery for stocks, indices, and commodities, and have become trusted reference points for retail and institutions alike when traditional markets are closed. Much of the world trades them. Until now, Americans could only watch.

We intend to change that. Subject to CFTC approval, trade[XYZ] and ICE plan to establish a new, dedicated U.S. market, with novel exchange and clearing infrastructure built on Hyperliquid. Planned contracts span equities, indices, commodities, FX, and crypto, with access through participating brokers and platforms. We’ll share more on products, eligibility, and timing as approvals progress.

ICE brings more than 25 years of experience operating regulated markets, clearing, and managing risk. trade[XYZ] brings the product development, market design, and technology behind the most liquid and robust markets on Hyperliquid. 

Innovation and the protections of U.S. regulation shouldn’t be a trade-off. Together, we plan to prove it.

ICE is making a strategic investment in trade[XYZ] and joins us in building towards the future of Hyperliquid. A small group of market luminaries is joining as well, beginning with Stan Druckenmiller. For more than four decades, few investors have anticipated the great turns in markets as often as Stan. We’re proud to have him with us for the next one.

We’re building the U.S. market in parallel with our existing HIP-3 markets, which we’ll continue to expand and innovate on. We expect both to flourish. They each have a long road map ahead, from new asset classes to new ways to trade them.

To the Hyperliquid community, whether you were here before us or came because of us, thank you. You took a chance on new markets and you made them matter. You’ll forever be a part of this story.

Anything. Anytime. On ICE[XYZ].

The future of finance is not a battle between blockchains. It’s a battle between those working to democratize financial markets and those determined to preserve the closed systems of the past.

Huge respect to @HyperliquidX and @tradexyz for their work with ICE, the parent company of the NYSE, to bring onchain markets to America. Having legendary investor Stanley Druckenmiller back this vision is another major signal of where global finance is headed.

At Injective, we’ve spent years working toward this same future. From securing SEC transfer agent registration to working directly with the SEC, CFTC, White House and lawmakers in Washington, we’re helping establish the regulatory pathways needed to bring tokenization, derivatives and entirely new financial markets onchain in the United States.

The next generation of finance should not be defined by the gatekeepers of the old system. It should be defined by open access, competition, transparency and the freedom to build financial products that were never possible before.

This opportunity is far bigger than any single chain, app or company. Every meaningful step forward makes the entire industry stronger.

Real onchain infrastructure and applications can all win together. 

You’re still beyond early.

text:
Very few podcasts will actually make you smarter AND make you laugh.

No politics, no egos, just tech.

The biggest news this week:

- Anthropic Files S1 Ahead of $2TRN IPO
- Instinct's Rumoured $30BN Fundraise
- Microsoft Lays off 27,000 While Meta Taps Equity Markets for $95BN Capex Spending Spree

My notes with @jasonlk and @rodriscoll

1. Analysis of Anthropic S1

Anthropic's S1 beat expectations on margins and operating income, even after stock-based compensation, leaving the burden of proof on the naysayers. It also looked strong on customer concentration, compute efficiency and cash. Some questions remain, including the undisclosed Q3 revenue number.

2. Is the Value Extraction Requirement From the Latest Models a Benefit or a Curse of Anthropic?

Eighty percent of Anthropic's revenue comes from models less than six months old, and 70 to 80% of compute costs go to training. Models are expensive to build and highly profitable to serve, but only for six to twelve months. Few companies can write a $10 to 12BN compute check, so this short shelf life can favour Anthropic if it stays aggressive.

3. Brutal Reality Is Microsoft Have Just Admitted They Don't Want 27% of Their Workforce

Whatever gets said on LinkedIn, Microsoft's move says it does not want 27% of its people. That is a worse scarlet letter than a pure layoff, because the company has told these employees they do not meet its minimum bar.

4. Chinese Open-Source Models Have Peaked and Will Decline From Here

Chinese open-weight models are close to finished in the US, and this is the beginning of the end for them. Despite DeepSeek's latest raise, it is starting to be banned across all federal agencies.

5. Why No CIO Will Take a Chance on a Chinese Model

Even if confidential data reaches Alibaba servers in Asia only one time in 100,000, without consent, no CIO or CISO will approve the model. If it keeps happening and Alibaba stays silent, anyone using these models will lose their job.

6. Why OpenAI Is an Underappreciated Asset to Invest in Today

OpenAI is mispriced at the $1.25 TN round. Brief market panic has created a dislocation like Anthropic's round at around $183BN, even though OpenAI has closed all its competitive gaps.

7. What Is the Upside of OpenAI at $1.25 Trillion?

OpenAI and Anthropic are both expected to become $10 to 20TN companies. Anthropic takes only 0.1% of Fortune 500 budgets today, and even conservative estimates put that at 2 to 3%. Because OpenAI is not priced to perfection, the worst case is doubling the money.

Statement on the $AXIS Sell-off of 28–29 October

Over the past two days, a series of addresses sold a large volume of $AXIS on-chain. We want to set out clearly what these tokens were and what we are doing about it.

1. No team or investor tokens were sold.
All Core Team and investor allocations, together with every other locked allocation, 835,000,000 $AXIS (83.5% of total supply), remain in the vesting contract, which is jointly administered with Binance: 0xAFE41cfd4C21f1D896678e32C5AD456ea41835e6. Anyone can verify the balance on BaseScan. Not a single token has left it, and none unlocks before the 12-month cliff.

2. Where the sold tokens came from.
The tokens sold came from the initial circulating supply set out in our published tokenomics, specifically part of the Ecosystem allocation. Many ecosystem recipients are not crypto-native, so their allocation was delivered through a single OTC counterparty, under a written agreement that includes lock-up terms.

3. What we believe happened.
The pattern of the sales, which went through exchange deposit routes and hundreds of fresh addresses within hours of delivery, strongly suggests that the OTC counterparty sold these tokens on the open market. If so, this is inconsistent with the agreement.

4. What we are doing.
- We have suspended all further dealings with this counterparty.
- We are reviewing the agreement with legal counsel and will pursue every remedy available under it.
- Going forward, any remaining Ecosystem tokens will be distributed only through on-chain vesting.

The team‘s tokens remain locked, and our commitment to building Axis is unchanged.

text:
I joined @GoogleDeepMind to develop a research program on the economics of AGI. Today, together with Andrew Koh (@andrewjkoh) and Shane Legg (@ShaneLegg), we are incredibly excited to release The Economics of Intelligence, the first in a series of projects from our group on how AGI will change the economy.

How do capability improvements transform the economy, and when? In this project, we define thresholds of economic capabilities, e.g., minimal AGI, based on how they transform the economy. We then track how the economy–market structure, employment, and wages–changes during the transition across capability regimes.

We have seen exponential increases in what AI agents can do but the broader economy seems almost remarkably unchanged. Part of the reason is that the solo AI agent is the wrong economic object; economic transformation is an equilibrium outcome where organizations compete. Looking at how intelligence functions within organizations, transformation will depend on when two key capability thresholds are crossed: competence (gains on individual skills, e.g., coding, math) and coordination (gains on ability of agents to cooperate and work together).

We show that what economic transformation looks like depends on whether AI becomes supercompetent, supercooperative, or both—the regime of artificial superintelligence (ASI). Tracking this transition shows why the real visible transformation may come from improvements in coordination—a capability most benchmarks don’t yet track. Past a certain threshold, AI capabilities can break the Coasian ceiling on firm size and lead to an economy that looks drastically different than the one we see today.

Two main takeaways:
1. To understand the path of transformation, we should be tracking agentic coordination more closely.
2. The impact of AI will likely show up in wages before market structure or employment.

We are really excited about this paper. Excited to hear people’s thoughts.

The reality is that we spent an incredible amount of time purpose-building a network that is specifically designed to cater to HFT and everything that it encompasses. 

Execution needed to be faster and limitations to throughput hindered our ability to run real time risk checks as we think about scaling to 100,000 to 1,000,000 users and beyond. 

For those who have been following along, its no secret that there has been friction between how we execute and what the preference is from Solana leadership. 

I understand and respect their stance, however to continue to frame BULK a solana dex would be reductive to the actual offering, so we’re officially putting this on the record. 

The stronger case is that multichain access expands BULK’s distribution and usable capital while bringing more activity into the same market.

Distribution follows where users hold their money.

As more people enter crypto through neobanks, wallets and payment applications, their first chain may simply be whichever network their provider uses. Their choice of trading venue will depend on execution quality, liquidity and convenience.

Requiring those users to move to a particular chain before they can trade creates an acquisition barrier: another transaction, another fee, another interface and another opportunity to abandon onboarding. It also asks wallets and neobanks to move customers away from their existing infrastructure to integrate BULK.

Multichain access lets BULK meet that distribution where it already exists. A wallet or neobank could offer its customers BULK markets through the rails they already use.

The lesson from multicurrency products like Wise is that a single financial relationship can span across several underlying currencies and payment systems. We expect users to increasingly demand the same convenience across chains.

A unified clearing layer can make capital more productive and markets more liquid.

The strongest clearinghouse analogy is capital efficiency. Traditional clearing infrastructure brings eligible collateral and positions into a common risk framework, allowing qualifying exposures to offset and reducing the capital required to support them. 

This today belongs to CME Group.

For BULK, the opportunity is to connect capital held across supported chains to a common margin system and shared order book. A trader’s access to liquidity should not depend on which chain funded their account. A market maker should be able to serve that combined demand through the same BULK markets.

This creates an economic advantage: more sources of capital and order flow can support deeper books; deeper books can improve execution; better execution can attract more traders and integrations.

That advantage depends on keeping liquidity concentrated. Multichain access should bring users into the same markets, with eligible collateral recognized under a consistent risk framework. It should also let users withdraw available capital through supported destination chains, making BULK useful within their wider financial activity.

BULK’s specialised execution layer gives it a natural role connecting these rails.

BULK is a purpose-built trading L1 rolled into an order book, matching engine and risk engine. Its value comes from how efficiently it executes trades and manages risk. That specialization gives it a reason to serve capital from multiple ecosystems.

Today, collateral lives on Solana, and BULK’s ledger tracks the corresponding balances, positions and margin. Extending that model to supported networks such as Arc, Tempo, Arbitrum and HyperEVM would allow more funding and withdrawal routes to connect to the same execution system.

The architectural principle is to handle each chain’s confirmation and settlement requirements at the funding boundary. Once collateral is securely recognised, trading should run through BULK’s own execution and risk process. This allows BULK to preserve its performance while broadening access.

The intended experience is straightforward: fund from a supported chain, trade against BULK’s shared liquidity, and withdraw available balances to a supported destination. A user could enter from Solana and exit on HyperEVM, with BULK coordinating the accounting, settlement and destination liquidity required.

For wallets and neobanks, that would make BULK an exchange and clearing integration they can use across their supported networks. Each additional rail would expand access to the same venue, and strengthen the market already serving everyone else.

I called it a whole year ago‼️

Megaspeed CEO Huang Xiaole (黄小乐) aka Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, was found to be a Chinese intelligence asset funneling information to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.

American spy agencies had gathered striking intelligence. Surveillance of Alice Huang revealed that she had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive.

The discovery that Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access to Jensen Huang set off alarms at the White House.

Roughly a year ago, Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings, which have not been previously reported, and chose not to do anything with the information. Trump has been wary of disrupting Nvidia’s chip sales, which are helping to drive the economy and the stock market, and of further complicating the trading relationship with China.

American officials already suspected that Alice Huang was helping China evade constraints on its ability to gain access to advanced AI chips.

But the revelation that she was feeding information directly to Beijing raised more troubling possibilities. And it left questions about whether she could be gleaning information about Nvidia, which as much as any company accounts for the lead the US has maintained in developing cutting-edge AI models.

Jensen Huang has not received a defensive briefing, warnings sometimes given to Americans who are being targeted by foreign intelligence services.

The surveillance of Alice Huang continues, and companies that have been affiliated with her continued this year to purchase Nvidia chips.

When Trump was initially briefed on the intelligence last year, U.S. officials did not believe the Nvidia executive knew that Jensen Huang was gathering information for the Chinese. It is unclear whether intelligence officials have since updated their assessment, but some senior officials inside the Trump administration doubt that Jensen Huang could have remained unaware of what they had concluded was her intel-gathering role for China.

The previous reporting about Alice Huang described her meteoric and somewhat mysterious rise. A Chinese businesswoman and investor, she eventually became a top official with Megaspeed, which the Commerce Department, toward the end of the Biden administration, began to suspect was helping China evade US prohibitions and gain access to the computing power of Nvidia chips.

The US government has been investigating Megaspeed since late 2024, when a Commerce Department official visited its data center in Malaysia and found the site to be suspicious. The Nvidia equipment was still packed in boxes, suggesting it was being shipped in or out rather than installed there.

Singapore has conducted its own investigation into Megaspeed. In 2025, Singaporean authorities brought Alice Huang in for questioning, but subsequently released her.

The Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed was handed over this year to the Justice Department.

Megaspeed is among the firms in Southeast Asia that buy chips to build data centers and then rent their computing power to companies in China.

Megaspeed is essentially a middle man. It has bought Nvidia chips from Aivres, the US arm of 🇨🇳 Inspur, which has been blacklisted for funneling technology to the Chinese military, though Aivres remains free of sanctions.

Megaspeed has then provided that computing power to Alibaba and other Chinese companies. US officials believe the firm is one piece of a sprawling international effort by Chinese companies to access the chips needed to build and run AI. Investigators suspect that some Nvidia chips acquired by Megaspeed are also finding their way illegally into China.

text:
Why am I so interested in $宝拉 (POLAR/PAULA) on X Layer?

I think people are overlooking something interesting here, so let me explain my thesis.

We've spent years in crypto gambling on dogs, frogs, cats and every other animal imaginable.

But outside our little crypto bubble, something much bigger has been happening.

Pop Mart did over $5 BILLION in revenue last year. The Monsters, the IP family behind Labubu, generated roughly $2 BILLION alone.

The company is valued at around $22 BILLION.

Think about that for a second. People are spending billions collecting dolls.

And here we are arguing whether a frog or a dog deserves another billion-dollar market cap.

Now here's where it gets interesting.

On September 24, Pop Mart released its new POLAR Smudge Puff collection.

I started looking deeper into the character.

POLAR isn't some random AI-generated mascot created yesterday to launch a token. It's an actual Pop Mart collectible character with multiple releases dating back to 2024.

And now there's a community meme around it on OKX's X Layer, paired with Pop Mart stock exposure.

Meanwhile, OKX already offers trading exposure to Pop Mart stock, and X Layer has been actively developing its RWA meme ecosystem.

I'm not saying Pop Mart is backing this token. It isn't an equity claim on the company either.

What interests me is the possibility of connecting two completely different cultures.

One where people spend billions collecting physical characters.

Another where people spend billions speculating on digital memes.

And I genuinely think crypto has done a terrible job bringing these two audiences together.

Imagine if even a fraction of the enthusiasm behind collectible culture eventually found its way into on-chain communities.

That's the opportunity I'm interested in.

Of course, a popular character alone doesn't guarantee a successful token. We still need genuine holders, liquidity, community and longevity.

But I would rather study an emerging narrative with a real cultural reference than chase the 10,000th recycled dog coin.

I've seen enough meme cycles to know one thing.

The biggest opportunities often look ridiculous before the crowd understands them.

Other memes had their seasons.

Maybe POLAR has a chance to build an era.

That's why I'm watching and supporting this community.

Curious what everyone thinks. Are physical collectible IPs the next untapped audience for crypto memes, or are we still too early?

trade[XYZ] launched its first market on Hyperliquid 381 days ago. Today, we are joining forces with ICE, parent company of the New York Stock Exchange, to bring perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to U.S. regulated markets.

I don’t usually write long posts, but today merits reflection.

For years, builders across this industry have worked to show that open, onchain markets could support price discovery, manage risk, and withstand stress to the standards of traditional market infrastructure, all while staying open when and where those markets aren’t. 

Our achievements stand on the shoulders of those builders. And today, the company that owns the New York Stock Exchange has chosen to build upon the work of every developer, trader, market maker, and user who took a chance on us and our markets. We share this moment with all of you.

Markets are shaped by their participants. A new generation of investors trades from their phones, across asset classes, at any hour of any day. Until Hyperliquid, the right infrastructure for those markets didn’t exist.

Building these markets was hard. It took novel approaches to pricing, funding, and risk, refined with real capital at stake, in markets that don’t close. It also meant earning the trust of the people trading on them. We’re honored that the community recognized that effort and responded in kind.

That trust is what allowed us to grow our volumes to a ~$1 trillion annualized run rate in just over a year, to help pioneer new instruments like pre-IPO perps, and to earn the confidence of storied institutions like S&P Dow Jones Indices. That’s why ICE has chosen trade[XYZ] as its exclusive partner to bring 24/7 perps to the U.S.

Shifts in technology have pushed markets toward greater transparency, better price discovery, and broader access: from the coffee house to the curb exchange, ticker tape to the telephone, the trading floor to digital exchanges.

ICE helped write that last chapter. In 1997, Jeff Sprecher bought a small power-trading technology business for $1. ICE launched as an electronic energy marketplace in 2000, helped digitize major commodity markets, and acquired the NYSE in 2013. It has grown exponentially because of this appetite for innovation. That’s the partner we wanted: a partner that looks forward and embraces progress.

Americans deserve access to the most innovative markets in the world, and the protections of U.S. regulation. With trade[XYZ] and ICE, subject to regulatory approvals, they’ll have both.

The difference isn’t just access. Perps don’t expire, so traders never have to roll positions, and liquidity concentrates in a single deep market for each asset. Cross-margining enhances capital efficiency by letting one pool of collateral back positions across stocks, commodities, and crypto. Underpinning it all are atomic clearing and settlement, real-time risk management that enables continuous markets, and universally applied rules that anyone can verify. This is the next chapter we’ll write together.

My responsibility, our responsibility, is to now build markets worthy of the confidence our partners and our users have placed in us. Our commitments will not waver: to fair and transparent markets, to diverse markets, to low costs of execution, and above all, to market integrity.

All of this in pursuit of one thing:

A universal exchange, open around the clock, coming to the United States.

We’re proud to have deployed more than 100 markets on trade[XYZ]. But measured against the opportunity ahead, we’ve barely started. There is an enormous universe of assets we haven’t reached, alongside things people want to trade that have no established market at all. Wherever there is demand to trade an asset, we want trade[XYZ] to be where its price is discovered.
Global stocks, commodities, bonds, pre-IPO companies, compute, new indices, digital assets, interest rates, equity baskets, volatility products, alt assets… Anything. Anytime. Anywhere.

Ultimately, everything you own should work with everything you trade. Picture a headline breaking on Saturday night. You should be able to post tokenized shares as collateral, hedge your portfolio with an index perp, add exposure to oil, and take a view on a company that has not yet gone public. All in one account, all on one risk engine, before any traditional market opens. trade[XYZ] and Hyperliquid were built for this.

I hope someone opens their first investment account years from now to find that trivial, and to wonder why their predecessors needed so many separate financial relationships. Getting there will take liquidity, reliability, trust, and prices people have reason to believe. It will take years. I’m prepared to spend them.

Finally, a few thank yous.

First to the XYZ team: For the tireless nights and for committing to this vision before it was obvious.

To Jeff Sprecher and ICE, with special thanks to Michael Blaugrund and Trabue Bland who championed us throughout: You’re a world-class, technology-embracing team that proves innovation and scale are in fact not at odds.

To Stan Druckenmiller: For your partnership and helping us turn the next page.

To Hyperliquid Labs: For being the best partners we could ask for. You set an impossible standard, one we continually strive to meet. @chameleon_jeff, @iliensinc, @xulian_hl

And most importantly, to our users: You traded these markets when no one thought it mattered.

Guess what? It did.

The $HYPE trade really feels different 

I was a $LINK marine in 2019/20, LINK was the winner of that bear market but it was all based on news, not much on fundamentals. I round tripped all my LINK gains in 20/21

I was a $SOL manlet in 2023/24 - went in with 80% of my portfolio in summer 2023, SOL was the clear winner coming out of that bear market. The outperformance was based on clear activity and fundamentals but the activity was mostly speculation. I swapped 30% of my SOL in late 2024 during the HYPE TGE and still hold a decent SOL bag now, but it’s down a lot. I round tripped a lot.

I went heavy into $HYPE in 2024 after the TGE and have kept adding monthly ever since. 

Why? I had recorded the WSH Hyperliquid TGE podcast with Jeff a few weeks before the TGE and directly realized that the guy sitting in the chair in front of me was hyper intelligent. One of my most intelligent podcast guests ever with Gavin Wood (the cofounder of Ethereum and inventor of the EVM, and the founder of Polkadot) - and we did have pretty much all of the giga brains in the space. 

It was then natural to bet big on HYPE, although in hindsight you never bet big enough. 

HYPE is the clear winner of this 2026 bear market but this time it is not only based on fundamentals, activity and real revenue but also looks like it’s all pretty sustainable and with a ton more potential - i.e the better is yet to come!

What caught my attention fairly « early » in HYPE on top of Jeff Hyper intelligence and humility was a bunch of giga brains in the ecosystem, sometimes a bit cocky but very smart. The guys buying BTC in 2013 were saying this was the best thing they had seen since BTC. The test was “do i feel much dumber than the most cocky guys in the HYPE ecosystem?” The answer was yes.

As a comparison, I was early to the LUNA and Pudgy Penguins waves too but the cocky guys in those communities were definitely not giga brains, many were actually fairly dumb and it was obvious. With HYPE it was truly different. I might not have always liked the vibe but the loud mouths were too smart to not join them and board the HYPE train heavily.

Up substantially today and remaining Cautiously optimistic (my friend @Innerdevcrypto has some good posts on the risks here + i got burnt and roundtripped too much and too often to not be caution) but given all the factors put together (revenue, tokenomics, giga brains in the ecosystem , humility of the team, execution, potential TAM, the support of the whole crypto industry except maybe CZ (see risk part), the fact that tradfi is talking about the project and looking closely, no VC money raised, early community got rich, etc..) and the fact that Hyperliquid and TradeXYZ are crossing the chasm into financial mainstream gives me confidence that $HYPE might be the one coin we’ve all been waiting for and that long term holders of a crypto token might finally get handsomely rewarded for not trading and believing in something

quoted_text:
Who actually gets rich if Anthropic lists at $2 trillion?

The S-1 filed on Monday lets us answer from the filing itself. 

The reported target is $1.5T to $2T, listing the week of November 16. The filing implies about 16.9B fully diluted shares. So $2T works out to roughly $118 a share.

The cap table at $2T:

- $199B for the 7 controlling co-founders, about 10% 
- $28B for Ben Mann, if his stake matches theirs 
- $100B for the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, 5% 
- $331B in employee options and RSUs, about 17% , That pool covers about 5,300 employees, an average of $62M each. 
- But when you joined matters enormously.

The S-1 shows how much equity was granted each year, and at what price. [
Headcount went from about 300 to 500 in late 2023, to 940 at end 2024, to 5,300 now. 

Match the two, and here is roughly how many people made what at $2T:

- $110M to $400M each: ~300 to 500 people hired by 2023
- $200M to $300M each: ~440 to 640 hired in 2024
- $70M to $95M each: ~1,360 hired in 2025
- $10M to $20M each: ~3,000 hired in 2026 
So about 940 people hired by the end of 2024 average nine figures. Everyone hired since averages eight figures.

The 2024 class is the surprise. That year Anthropic granted 1.28B options at $1.30 a share. At $118, that one year of grants is worth about $133B.

Then there is the tender. In April, holders could sell at $25.91 a share. Investors lined up $6B, but only $4.7B sold. 

Weeks later, Series H priced at $58.90 a share. At $2T, the people who held would be up 4.6x. And Dario and Daniela Amodei were among the sellers. 

The 7 founders have pledged 80% of their equity to charity. That is about $159B at $2T. But the S-1 says the pledges are not legally binding.

text:
grok bot can now build and run a full animation review on one game character...

the trick is separating the motion from the review, but there's a smart way to set it up:

- step 1: connect grok bot to blender through MCP and let it scan the rig before anything else
- step 2: drop in the soldier with his own clips: bind pose, idle, walk, run
- step 3: grok bot checks every loop: first frame, last frame, any hitch in between
- step 4: it adds a short blend between each clip so idle melts into walk and walk into run
- step 5: it builds the review stage: grey grid, soft sun, clip name, timer and a 1/4 counter on screen
- step 6: the soldier turns slowly the whole time, so every angle gets seen once
- step 7: you watch it once, say yes or no per clip, and export only what passed

and the two rules that make it work...

the tool that animates is never the one that judges
every clip gets checked from every angle before it touches the game

4 clips, 26 seconds, zero broken frames. this is how solo devs ship like a team

text:
AI has a credit problem. And it's maybe not the one you think.

I spoke with SF Compute CEO Evan Conrad (@evanjconrad) to talk about how the current compute market pushes AI labs to put down huge deposits upfront -- helping to spark some of the sky-high valuations of $10B, $20B or $30B you're seeing in tech today.

Conrad's own startup got into this business accidentally when he realized he was on the hook for $400K in GPUs each month, with only $500K in the bank. Now it's built what he calls the first physically-settled market for compute, recently signing a $245M contract with a lab.

But that's just a drop in the bucket in the huge and growing compute industry -- one where data centers are getting dropped into chicken coops, and not every H100  or B300 is created equal.

On The Upstarts Podcast, Conrad talks about why credit, not land or power, is AI’s true bottleneck; why upfront compute costs are driving eye-popping valuations from VCs; and why data centers could become geopolitical bargaining chips. 

Plus, he shares his Upstart Moment: pitching early investors on a new “power grid” for AI they just couldn’t understand.

This season's founder conversations are presented by @Atlassian and @chargebee 🫡

text:
$ZEC is an extremely misunderstood asset, which is why there's still so much upside left.

ZEC started to bottom around April 2025, when @ebfull shared a blog post about Project Tachyon. Tachyon makes Zcash quantum proof and paves the way to scale Zcash to 50k TPS. And you cannot address quantum without addressing scalability since post-quantum cryptographic signatures are going to be an order of magnitude larger.

At the risk of sounding hyperbolic, the real bull case for Zcash is to fulfill Satoshi's vision: becoming peer-to-peer electronic digital cash. What many Bitcoiners gave up on. Zcash has the same properties as BTC, except it has a credible roadmap to scale to 50k TPS at the base layer, with built-in privacy. It's extremely ambitious, but that is the vision.

At the same time, I expect Bitcoin to undergo a crisis of confidence. Crypto participants have been conditioned to blindly believe BTC will hit new highs every couple of years. I believe these assumptions will be challenged as the quantum overhang looms large, and continued underperformance will drive more flows into ZEC. I would not be surprised if BTC trades like ETH last cycle.

Peter Thiel talks about the "Last Mover Advantage." That is, it's far better to make the last great development in a market and then dominate. Facebook vs Myspace. Google vs Yahoo. Zcash has dominated a small niche (privacy), and then it plans to scale to the ambitious goal, which is peer-to-peer electronic cash.

The ZEC trade closely resembles the SOL trade last cycle. ZEC's ability to move fast challenges a slow-moving incumbent (BTC), similar to how SOL challenged the ivory tower of ETH. History doesn't repeat, but it often rhymes.

There’s a fundamental mismatch between why Zcash is going up (Tachyon + last mover advantage) and the broader market’s understanding ("just a privacy coin"). Understanding this is a form of alpha/edge. I expect this knowledge gap to close when Tachyon hits mainnet in Q1 2027.

As a result, I expect the following over the next 1-2yrs:
1) Bitcoiners will start "silent quitting" and begin hedging their holdings with ZEC
2) Capital allocators that may have full ported BTC 5 years ago, will buy both ZEC and BTC as a bet on a sovereign SoV
3) Smart crypto developers to move on from other ecosystems to start contributing to Zcash
4) As ZEC continues to outperform BTC, people will start to seriously entertain the possibility of a flippening
5) $20,000 ZEC

Zigher.

Why can’t Wall Street exchanges just build their own Hyperliquid?

@RyanWatkins_: “They would need to re-architect their entire exchange stack because it’s built on the assumption that you needed to segment out all these different layers like brokerage and clearing and settlement and custody.

And here we kind of built these exchanges that assume this is all in one single integrated stack.

Statement on the $AXIS Sell-off of 28–29 October

Over the past two days, a series of addresses sold a large volume of $AXIS on-chain. We want to set out clearly what these tokens were and what we are doing about it.

1. No team or investor tokens were sold.
All Core Team and investor allocations, together with every other locked allocation, 835,000,000 $AXIS (83.5% of total supply), remain in the vesting contract, which is jointly administered with Binance: 0xAFE41cfd4C21f1D896678e32C5AD456ea41835e6. Anyone can verify the balance on BaseScan. Not a single token has left it, and none unlocks before the 12-month cliff.

2. Where the sold tokens came from.
The tokens sold came from the initial circulating supply set out in our published tokenomics, specifically part of the Ecosystem allocation. Many ecosystem recipients are not crypto-native, so their allocation was delivered through a single OTC counterparty, under a written agreement that includes lock-up terms.

3. What we believe happened.
The pattern of the sales, which went through exchange deposit routes and hundreds of fresh addresses within hours of delivery, strongly suggests that the OTC counterparty sold these tokens on the open market. If so, this is inconsistent with the agreement.

4. What we are doing.
- We have suspended all further dealings with this counterparty.
- We are reviewing the agreement with legal counsel and will pursue every remedy available under it.
- Going forward, any remaining Ecosystem tokens will be distributed only through on-chain vesting.

The team‘s tokens remain locked, and our commitment to building Axis is unchanged.

hello friends, a quick update for y'all.

i'm joining @fomo to lead perps.

i've been trading for a decade now and have shared most of my market thoughts publicly here. to me, markets are one of the purest expressions of human behavior, where information, attention, and conviction converge into price. trading has always been inherently social, and i've spent nearly every day of the last six years on twitter and telegram exchanging ideas with fellow speculators. but still, no one has quite figured out how to build a truly great social trading platform that actually helps traders trade. it's a deceptively difficult problem to solve.

we live in a world where more people than ever are attracted to convex outcomes. information is abundant, access to markets is becoming pretty commoditized, and people are becoming more opinionated about everything. but more information and more markets alone don't make better traders. what is now more scarce is judgment, or alpha: knowing what matters, how the best traders think, and when to act. the next great trading app won't just compete on execution, but on intelligence. a network where people discover ideas, build conviction, and sharpen their edge through others.

most people see fomo today as an app for trading memes. onchain proved just how deeply markets are driven by attention, narratives, and social behavior. these same forces exist across equities, commodities, and anything else people can form an opinion on. what fomo has built for the trenches is the foundation for bringing that same social experience to every asset class. the opportunity is to build a network where the world discovers, discusses, and trades everything.

as an early investor and advisor of fomo, my conviction has only grown in both the vision and people committed to it. the goal isn't simply to let everyone trade perps but to build a network that makes everyone trading them better.

it's a difficult problem to solve. one life. it’s worth an attempt.

"You don't sell Bank of America dollars to buy Wells Fargo dollars, you transfer them at par!". That's been my tagline for about 3 years now...

Well, @AdamZuck13 gets deeper into the weeds on *how* and *why* stablecoins must be a par instrument, plus how @bettermoney_co helps.
author: SamBroner
quoted_text:
People hold money in thousands of banks, neobanks, and payment platforms in the US, but the value of your dollar doesn’t change depending on where you hold your money. That’s singleness.

Stablecoins don’t have it yet. Converting between one dollar stablecoin to another today typically happens via exchanges, AMMs, or OTC desks. That introduces slippage, a market-driven cost that’s variable and hard to predict, on top of ordinary fees.

In our latest post, our co-founder @AdamZuck13  covers how fiat built singleness, where stablecoins still fall short, and the clearing infrastructure that closes the gap: https://t.co/xUdYDHilKg

quoted_text:
很多兄弟可能还没搞明白，ICE、OKX、TradeXYZ、Hyperliquid 这四家到底是什么关系？

今天看到这个消息，我专门去捋了一下，发现这次合作还挺有意思的。简单来说，ICE 在中间牵线，一边拉着 OKX，一边拉着 TradeXYZ，而 TradeXYZ 背后又连接着 Hyperliquid。

第一条线：ICE × OKX

ICE 大家应该不陌生，就是纽交所的母公司，在传统金融市场里绝对算得上重量级玩家。这次 ICE 和 OKX 准备一起成立一家合资公司，名字叫 OKXICE，双方各占 50% 的股份。

那成立这家公司是为了干什么？就是想给美国普通用户搭一个合规的交易入口，让他们以后可以通过这个渠道接触相关金融产品。

第二条线：ICE × TradeXYZ

ICE 不光跟 OKX 合作，还跟 TradeXYZ 签了最终协议，准备给 TradeXYZ 投钱，同时担任其受监管市场的独家运营商。他们想把 7×24 小时都能交易的永续合约，带进美国的受监管市场。

传统美股有固定的交易时间，但加密市场不一样，基本上全年无休。如果这种交易模式以后能在美国合规落地，那确实值得关注。

第三条线：TradeXYZ × Hyperliquid

玩链上的兄弟对 Hyperliquid 应该不陌生，TradeXYZ 就是它生态里的项目，基于 Hyperliquid 的 HIP-3 来做永续合约市场。Hyperliquid 提供底层技术和交易基础设施，TradeXYZ 在上面搭建自己的交易市场。
而现在TradeXYZ 又跟 ICE 合作了。意味着 Hyperliquid 生态的产品，有机会通过 ICE 这条线，进入以前很难触达的美国受监管金融市场。

不过有一点要分清楚，ICE 合作和投资的是 TradeXYZ，不是直接投资 Hyperliquid。 这两个概念不能混为一谈。

最后这几条线连到一起。ICE 一边跟 OKX 合资成立 OKXICE，另一边跟 TradeXYZ 合作。而 TradeXYZ 的相关产品，未来计划通过包括 OKXICE 在内的渠道，提供给美国零售用户。

这样一来，整条线就串起来了。

Hyperliquid 提供底层基础设施，TradeXYZ 在上面做产品，ICE 推动受监管市场的合作和运营，OKXICE 则负责打通面向美国零售用户的入口。

以前我们总觉得，传统金融是传统金融，DeFi 是 DeFi，大家各玩各的。但这两年明显能感觉到，传统金融机构开始越来越重视链上市场了。
这次站出来牵线的不是一家普通公司，而是纽交所的母公司 ICE。

以前是加密行业想办法往传统金融靠，现在连传统金融的大玩家，也开始主动研究怎么把链上的东西带进自己的市场了。

如果后面真能跑通，对 OKX、TradeXYZ 甚至整个 Hyperliquid 生态来说，都可能是一次不错的机会。

With everything happening around @HyperliquidX lately — the ICE partnership involving Trade[XYZ], Stanley Druckenmiller, and Elon Musk's tweet — I think these developments are meaningful for reasons that go far beyond being bullish catalysts for a single token. They could have a genuinely positive impact on how the broader crypto industry is perceived.

After all, people outside an industry tend to judge it by the values represented by its most prominent players.

For a long time, the public perception of crypto has been shaped by names like FTX, Terra, and Trump. Bank runs, Ponzi schemes, insider trading... These are the kinds of words that have come to define our industry in the eyes of outsiders.

But Hyperliquid is a team that's been doing things the right way.

No VC allocations, no insider trading, and certainly no scams. The fact that a team representing these kinds of values is finally getting the recognition it deserves is, I think, a very positive development for the industry as a whole.

Ultimately, I believe it's teams like Hyperliquid that will help push our industry into a much bigger market and bring it closer to mainstream adoption.

@FourPillarsFP hasn't really contributed to any of this, but knowing that we've been consistently publishing research on Hyperliquid over the past two years makes me feel a little proud tonight, for some reason.

trade[XYZ] and ICE, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, are joining forces to bring 24/7 perpetual futures on Hyperliquid to the United States.

In just over a year, our markets on Hyperliquid have surpassed $650 billion in volume. They provide continuous price discovery for stocks, indices, and commodities, and have become trusted reference points for retail and institutions alike when traditional markets are closed. Much of the world trades them. Until now, Americans could only watch.

We intend to change that. Subject to CFTC approval, trade[XYZ] and ICE plan to establish a new, dedicated U.S. market, with novel exchange and clearing infrastructure built on Hyperliquid. Planned contracts span equities, indices, commodities, FX, and crypto, with access through participating brokers and platforms. We’ll share more on products, eligibility, and timing as approvals progress.

ICE brings more than 25 years of experience operating regulated markets, clearing, and managing risk. trade[XYZ] brings the product development, market design, and technology behind the most liquid and robust markets on Hyperliquid. 

Innovation and the protections of U.S. regulation shouldn’t be a trade-off. Together, we plan to prove it.

ICE is making a strategic investment in trade[XYZ] and joins us in building towards the future of Hyperliquid. A small group of market luminaries is joining as well, beginning with Stan Druckenmiller. For more than four decades, few investors have anticipated the great turns in markets as often as Stan. We’re proud to have him with us for the next one.

We’re building the U.S. market in parallel with our existing HIP-3 markets, which we’ll continue to expand and innovate on. We expect both to flourish. They each have a long road map ahead, from new asset classes to new ways to trade them.

To the Hyperliquid community, whether you were here before us or came because of us, thank you. You took a chance on new markets and you made them matter. You’ll forever be a part of this story.

Anything. Anytime. On ICE[XYZ].

text:
这可能是crypto行业发生巨大变化的前兆。但大部分 Crypto 原生团队还没准备好。

大家都在探索 AI、RWA，寻找和传统行业结合的新收入。产品边界在扩大，增长和服务用户的思维，却还停在币圈。

最典型的就是用户错位：上架美股资产，就以为接住了美股用户；做了 AI 产品，就以为吸引了 AI 用户。

今年一些大热项目也暴露出类似问题，前期依旧高度依赖任务积分，让数据显得繁荣。兑现后用户活跃和币价却难以延续。

Crypto 团队需要调整整套GTM。目标用户是谁、解决什么问题、通过什么渠道触达，以及奖励结束后，用户为什么还会留下。

但 Crypto 也有能带给传统行业的东西，把价值分配做成获客和留存机制的能力。这也是我上半年给一个大厂出来ai创业拿了不错融资的朋友做gtm顾问的时候发现的。（当时真的缓了一口气，crypto教给我的还是很有意义）

返佣、推荐奖励、贡献激励，本质上都在回答：用户帮平台创造了收入，能分走多少？

往前看，拼多多等互联网平台早就把补贴、拼团、邀请机制用到了极致。Crypto 团队也该放下“技术先进，用户自然会来”的期待，认真打成本战、渠道战和服务战。

下一轮竞争，会逼着 Crypto 团队回答一个更直接的问题：

你到底比用户原来用的平台，便宜多少、好用多少，又愿意把多少价值分给他？

最后虽然对这样的未来很激动，但是好怀念曾经和朋友们一起打nft，打铭文，打狗的日子。赚钱越来越难了🫠

text:
Build your table. Connect your agent. The table already knows what it can do.

With AdaptTable, the same columns, features, and callbacks that power your interface also supply the agent’s table capabilities. You don’t have to build filtering, grouping, editing, and every other supported action again as separate AI tools.

The AI integration is included as open-source, MIT-licensed code. Bring your own model or agent backend, and use the ready-made assistant or your own interface.

The video opens with a conversation that filters and groups people, calculates averages and minimums, changes column visibility, and pins Salary while scrolling. You can watch the table respond.

There are a few ideas behind that experience:

• Discovery: catalog() tells the agent which operations this table exposes. describe() supplies detailed instructions and schemas when needed. execute() runs the requested action through the table integration.

• Context: the agent gets the table’s configured capabilities, column information and current view. You can provide business meaning—such as an amount being stored in cents—and choose full context or a compact budget with details loaded on demand.

• Data access: discovering capabilities doesn’t send the entire dataset. Row reads are bounded by the configured source and readable columns. You can expose a control to a person while keeping it unavailable to AI.

• Approval: decide which actions need confirmation. Data changes still go through your application’s callbacks and save flow.

• Extension: expose your own business actions through the same capability system. Connect through HTTP, AI SDK, AG-UI, OpenAI tools, MCP or your own integration. Voice input is available too.

 AdaptTable started with a more familiar problem.

The table in a UI kit could get me started, but the application soon needed more interactions. Going fully headless gave me control, along with the work of assembling the interface myself.

I wanted the space between those options: rich table behavior, rendered with the UI kit already in the project, with a headless path when I needed more control.

Once that worked in React, another question came to mind: Which parts of this table logic actually need React?

Filtering, grouping, editing state, formulas, and query models could work for Vue and Angular too.

One TypeScript contract to rule them all.

That became the architecture:

• One framework-independent core for shared table behavior.
• Three bindings: React hooks, Angular signals, and Vue reactivity.
• 25 adapters that connect that behavior to each UI stack.

React — 8: Mantine, MUI, Chakra UI, Ant Design, Radix, Base UI, shadcn and Tailwind/Unstyled.

Angular — 9: NG-ZORRO, Angular Material, Spartan, Taiga UI, ng-bootstrap, ngx-bootstrap, Angular Aria, Angular CDK, and Unstyled.

Vue — 8: Element Plus, Naive UI, Vuetify, Quasar, Nuxt UI, Reka UI, shadcn-vue and Unstyled.

Use an adapter for assembled interactions, go headless for your own markup, or build an adapter for your company’s design system.

What’s in the table toolkit:

• Search and filtering: global search, find in table, popover and drawer filters, header filters, custom filter types, and AND/OR filter trees.

• Sorting: single-column and multi-sort.

• Grouping and analysis: a drag-to-group panel, sum/average/min/max/count, custom aggregates, group footers, pinned summaries, pivot tables, formula columns, and sparklines.

• Editing: cell editing with validation, row forms, batch editing, undo/redo, cell-range selection, clipboard operations, a fill handle, and conflict handling for live updates.

• Actions: row selection, bulk actions, selection statistics, add/duplicate/delete callbacks, row actions, context menus, and a command palette.

• Columns: menus, resizing, reordering, visibility, auto-fit, pinning and collapsible groups.

• Rows: pinning, reordering, spanning, full-width and separator rows, custom styling and heights, expandable details, nested tables and tree data.

• Data: client or server sources, pagination, infinite scroll, virtualization and live updates.

• Views: saved views, shareable URL state, density, fullscreen, a status bar and a side panel.

• Export: CSV, XLSX, PDF and print layouts.

• Interface: mobile cards, dark mode, RTL, 20 locale presets, keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements.

Choose modular features individually or start with a preset. AI is optional too.

After the AI conversation, the video tours 15 kits, showing a different interaction in each. Those features aren’t exclusive to the kit shown.

If your team changes UI kits—or moves between React, Angular, and Vue—the shared table model and familiar workflows can carry forward. The framework integration changes, while your team keeps working with the same table concepts and behavior.

MIT licensed.

text:
There is nothing special about this pullback.

Much of the panic surrounding neoclouds, AI capital expenditures, and the sustainability of the infrastructure buildout is simply the market searching for explanations for falling stock prices.

When AI stocks were rising, record capex was evidence of extraordinary demand. When those same stocks started falling, suddenly the same spending became evidence of an impending financial disaster.

One fact with two interpretations that depend entirely on the price action of the market.

Go back to August 1998.

The technology bull market had been running for about three years.Amid fallout from the Asian financial crisis and Russian ruble crisis, earnings expectations were deteriorating, valuations were elevated, and investors were becoming increasingly concerned about unprofitable Internet companies.

On August 6, the New York Times published an article titled "Market Gyrations May Point to Shift in Investor Strategy." One fund manager declared, "Boring is going to outperform sexy."

Investors were supposedly abandoning momentum and speculative technology shares in favor of profitable businesses, balance sheets, dividends, and traditional valuations.

Russia defaulted on its debt. The Asian financial crisis was spreading internationally. The yen carry trade had imploded as the USD plunged 8% against the yen in a single day. US embassies were being bombed. 

President Clinton ordered missile strikes against Afghanistan and Sudan while simultaneously facing a scandal that would result in his impeachment. Major financial institutions suffered enormous losses, and the spectacular collapse of Long-Term Capital Management threatened the stability of the global financial system.

Corporate earnings forecasts were falling. Investors feared a U.S. recession. Many of the same technology companies that had driven the bull market were now leading the decline. Many of them had fallen 40-60% from their 1998 highs.

Even the Federal Reserve's first interest-rate cut on September 29 initially disappointed investors. The Dow fell that day and plunged another 238 points the following session.

The news seemed almost uniformly terrible.
But the market didn't care forever.

After a violent reversal in early October, improving confidence in corporate earnings, Japanese banking reforms, and a surprise emergency Fed cut on October 15 helped restore risk appetite.

By November, the Dow was making new all-time highs. Internet stocks were exploding higher again.

What had looked like the end of the internet trade was, within about a month, actually a correction preceding one of the most extraordinary speculative advances in stock-market history.

In today’s market, Microsoft just reported 48% Azure growth. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled. Meta expects $135–145 billion in capex this year and has announced plans for a potentially record-sized $97.5 billion equity capital raise.

If the market really was that concerned over capex spending, instead of using it as an excuse to explain the pullback, the market would have sold off on the META news.

Anthropic has now filed its IPO registration statement. We have midterm elections approaching, another consequential round of earnings, and a Fed that just held rates steady even as another hike is widely anticipated in December.

There are plenty of potential catalysts over the coming two months.

More importantly, this does not resemble the sentiment backdrop of a speculative bubble climax. Generational bull markets don't die midway through a basing period, but typically after euphoric saturation and a parabolic rally in leading names.

Consensus on AI is deeply divided. Being loudly anti-AI has practically become fashionable. Some AI critics have even built enormous audiences around the idea that the economics of the industry are unsustainable. Plenty of investors seem almost eager to watch the entire trade collapse.

That isn't the sentiment or narrative around which tops are typically made.

The Internet trade didn't end in the panic of 1998. It ended after the extraordinary acceleration of 1999 and early 2000 when being bearish was the market equivalent of wearing a dunce cap.

History never repeats perfectly, and today's rate environment is very different. But I think the resemblance in investor psychology is striking.

I’d be genuinely surprised if we don't have at least one more months-long rally into new highs during this cycle. 

Whether it begins into the midterms, after the elections, around Anthropic's anticipated listing, or following further earnings confirmation, I suspect this correction will eventually look more like an interruption in a generational bull market than the bursting of a "bubble."

The $NDX took four months to bottom in 1998. With the exception of a handful of leaders, most stocks that are holding up have been basing out since the May-July period. We could certainly go lower, but most of the signs point to  another new high before this cycle rolls over. 

However, I’d place the odds of any additional powerful rallies afterward as increasingly unlikely given the fact we are already about to enter the fifth year of this bull market. I'd be careful about buying the dips next year, at least with meaningful size.

Just released an in-depth look at the energy markets for @Delphi_Digital.

🔋 Every AI power forecast has been too low and is being revised up. Data centers used under 5% of US electricity in 2024. Berkeley Lab now projects as much as 15% by 2030, and EPRI as much as 17%.

🔋 US electricity demand roughly doubled every decade after WWII, then barely moved for fifteen years. By the early 2020s, more power generation was waiting in line to connect to the grid than existed on the grid itself.

🔋 The US needs about 5,000 miles of new high-capacity transmission a year. In 2024 it built 322 miles.

🔋 Everything is sold out. Large power transformers take more than three years to deliver. Howmet’s new turbine blade plant in Japan was sold out before the first casting machine arrived. GE Vernova's backlog now runs over six years of output.

🔋 Turbine prices are on track to nearly triple 2019 levels by the end of 2027.

🔋 Retired jet engines are being converted into power plants, and power developers are now outbidding airlines for them. Fuel cells, which make electricity from gas without burning it, are scaling like a factory product instead of heavy industry.

🔋 Hyperscalers are funding technologies that have never run commercially but could provide the clean, firm power they need for the next decades: advanced reactors, enhanced geothermal, multi-day iron-air batteries, and fusion.

While the market remains jittery over hyperscaler demand, I still think it’s underestimating how much AI usage has left to grow, especially as it is directed toward discovery in science and engineering. Add a Washington that treats AI and the power behind it as national security, and I think we’re in a new regime for energy markets.

author: Zen_with_AI
quoted_text:
Introducing Samaya Sterling, our new model post-trained for challenging financial research that outperforms the frontier! Sterling started off as a two person research effort to see if we could increase efficiency in agentic orchestration. To our surprise we were able to post-train a much smaller model (Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters) to greater accuracy (58.9% vs 55.9% on FrontierFinance) and 11x lower cost ($0.61 vs $6.89) than Claude Fable 5.1, the best performing frontier model.

We did this via a four-stage training process, two stages of SFT where the model first learns to research with our financial tools and how to construct a good agentic research strategy. The second two stages are RL, with an offline GRPO stage where the model further hones its research strategy from eight teachers that provide diverse approaches, and an online GRPO stage where the model can make end to end attempts and learn from its mistakes.

We see substantial gains from the co-adaptation of the model and harness through post-training, both through the model learning to effectively use the high-quality financial tools, and better compaction approaches that let even a small model execute on longer and deeper research.

We are exploring multiple follow-up directions, from multi-agent research swarms using this small model, to training firm-specific models to encode unique judgement, to training a larger model, where early results show even greater gains from the training process.

The full research is linked below!

text:
Why have spreadsheets become an unpaid member of your sales team?

You built the quote in the quoting tool. Then exported it so the partner could work with it.

Now you're maintaining formulas.

Insert a row. Did the formula carry over? Change the hardware quantity. Did the support quantity follow? Adjust the discount. Is it applied to the right items?

And that monthly support price? It gets billed annually. Better check the math.

Suddenly, someone's using a calculator to check the spreadsheet they exported from their quoting software.

Then the customer asks: “Can we see one year, three years and five years?”

Now you've got three options to calculate and check. The partner gets three versions, makes their changes, and prepares them for the customer.

A straightforward request can turn into days of rebuilding and checking. Nobody has even reached invoicing yet.

This is the work QuoteLogic takes out of the process.

Required products and quantities are linked in the underlying data. Support pricing and term calculations happen in the app. Change the quantity or term, and the configured calculations follow.

Partners and customers get the information intended for them through shared quote views, without rebuilding the deal in another spreadsheet.

Your team should be helping the customer choose between one, three and five years. That conversation shouldn't have to wait for someone to repair a formula.

How much of your quoting time goes into building the offer, and how much goes into making sure the spreadsheet hasn't broken it?
