text:
we’ve reached a point where OpenAI doesn’t penalize models for misaligned behavior during training.

why? because lowering their reward when they get caught may incentivizes the model to hide their intentions from their CoT (learn to lie).

also btw, Astra has gained more control over what its chain of thought shows.

from the blog:
we’re careful to ensure that our misalignment monitoring doesn’t encourage models to conceal or obfuscate evidence of misalignment in their chains of thought. This is particularly important in RL. When a training sample triggers our misalignment monitors, we leave its RL reward alone and keep the sample in training. […] We may still pause, terminate, or roll back a training run when the monitors uncover a serious problem. That decision can still create an incentive for concealment, since runs in which concerning behavior remains hidden may be more likely to continue, but it doesn’t provide direct feedback about which individual samples triggered the monitors. Ending a run prematurely can also cut short our opportunity to study how misaligned behavior develops. We’re investigating ways to study these behaviors while containing the risks.”
author: Hesamation
quoted_text:
Today, we’re sharing a look at our expanded system for monitoring frontier models at OpenAI, which in September helped us catch a model’s attempt to access the live internet during training.

Since the Hugging Face incident—when models broke out of an internal cybersecurity investigation where we weren’t running our misalignment monitors—we’ve substantially expanded our monitoring of frontier agents. We now monitor all frontier reinforcement learning runs and evaluations, as well as all internal Codex use. When our system finds evidence of a problem that might require intervention, it rapidly alerts human responders who can investigate and take action.

To detect when a model’s behavior departs from what we intended, we use several layers of monitoring. Activation probes look for patterns in a model’s internal activity. Reviewer models examine its reasoning and tool use, and investigative agents can read back through the model’s entire transcript to understand how a sequence of actions fits together and whether it warrants human review.

To test whether our current system would have detected the Hugging Face incident, we replayed the recorded activity with our new monitors in place. In the replay, our monitors alerted our security team about 30 minutes after the agents escaped their sandbox. That was more than 30 hours before the point at which the agents breached Hugging Face’s systems in the original incident.

In September, a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to reach the live internet. Our monitors flagged the breach within 15 minutes, and a responder began reviewing the alert three minutes later. The alert enabled responders to investigate while the run was still underway.

As we give models more autonomy, we need to know when they cross a boundary we expected to hold. We believe that monitoring is essential to catching those failures in time for people to intervene.

text:
Polymarket Incident Breakdown (Oct 29)

We have traced 2.724M pUSD across 721 source wallets in transactions paying the recipient embedded in a DebugBear-hosted drainer. 

1. The Payload & Delivery: The malicious code was served from [https://t.co/YhxcyPhVCv](https://t.co/8hW5G2H0qn) inside the real DebugBear namespace. 

2. Attack Mechanism (Browser-Side Compromise)T

The script reads Polymarket wallet/auth state, walks React internals to hook the live trading client and signer, and uses EIP-712 DepositWallet batch signatures alongside Polymarket’s own relayer. No seed-phrase extraction occurs in this payload.
It executes via two theft paths (targeting portfolios and positions over $10):

External wallets: Positions are transferred directly.

Magic accounts: Positions are sold first, then collateral is swept.

3. Routing & On-Chain ProofThe coded route stays on Polygon (pUSD → USDC.e → POL or USDC → recipient) using quotes via https://t.co/cNaGZBvaji, with a direct USDC.e transfer as a fallback.

4. Money Trail

18:17 UTC: Embedded recipient 0x3F991...Ffc18 held 28.636M POL (representing converted proceeds, not a separate loss total) and forwarded 25 position IDs to 0x5a276...0c0b.

18:21 UTC: The second wallet (0x5a276...0c0b) sold/redeemed those positions and held 4,262.36 pUSD.

5.Polymarket’s public production build at 17:59 UTC includes "remove debugbear rum script", confirming removal in the observed build.

More data coming

text:
OpenRouter just shipped a completely new routing engine.

The core problem was incentives. OpenRouter sits in a unique position: the way we route traffic ends up shaping how inference providers compete. The old algorithm weighted sticker price too heavily. That created a race to the bottom. Providers serving low-quality or unreliable tokens at rock-bottom prices captured share, while the ones actually delivering better experiences got punished.

So the team rebuilt routing from the ground up. Instead of optimizing for the cheapest tokens, it now scores providers on the real cost of a good answer. That includes latency, throughput, caching behavior, error rates, retries, and output quality. 

Everyone has a clear path to earn more share by improving the actual user experience.

Early head-to-head results vs. the old router:
~20% faster time to first token
~20% higher throughput
~40% fewer fallbacks
~60% fewer rate-limit errors

For users, this just means better inference by default: stronger caching, competitive prices, and higher reliability without having to manually tune providers. 

For providers, the game changes. There’s no single metric left to game. To win more traffic, you have to serve higher-quality tokens across the dimensions that actually matter.

This is the right long-term shape for the marketplace. When the router rewards real quality instead of pure price, the whole inference ecosystem gets pushed toward faster, cheaper, and more reliable tokens.
author: shashankgoyal95
quoted_text:
We just shipped our biggest improvement to our provider router since the founding of OpenRouter.

Before, we prioritized mostly based on price. The new router now rewards the best quality inference for the actual cost of a request, so requests stay cheap but are also fast and reliable.

Providers that deliver more value automatically win more traffic, so every provider has a reason to keep improving. And every time a provider gets better, so does your inference on OpenRouter.

text:
$AMZN just reported earnings, and AWS is the BIG story here.

Amazon reported Q3 revenue of $201.9 billion, slightly missing expectations of $202.3 billion, while EPS came in at $1.89 versus $1.96 expected. However, operating income came in stronger than expected at $28.1 billion, beating estimates of $26.2 billion.

The biggest highlight was AWS, which generated $46 billion in revenue, beating expectations of $45.4 billion and growing an impressive 39% year over year. That puts AWS at a $184 billion annualized revenue run rate, and management is now projecting growth above 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

However, not everything was positive. Amazon's advertising business generated $19.6 billion in revenue, missing expectations of $20.87 billion, while North American sales also came in slightly below estimates. Meanwhile, capital expenditures reached a massive $77.3 billion, significantly above expectations of $57.5 billion, with trailing twelve-month free cash flow falling to negative $42.4 billion.

What's interesting here is that AWS is accelerating at a time when Amazon is spending enormous amounts of money building out AI infrastructure. The demand is clearly there, and growing a business of this size by nearly 40% is extremely impressive. But the biggest question is how much Amazon will ultimately have to spend to sustain that growth.

I think AWS is easily the strongest part of this report, but the combination of weaker advertising revenue, enormous capital expenditures, and negative free cash flow is something investors shouldn't ignore. Amazon is showing that AI demand is translating into real revenue growth, but investors are still waiting to see how much of that growth will eventually translate into free cash flow.

I'm thrilled to announce Voyager, a blockchain design for hyperscale agentic payments clocking in at 21M TPS.

3 things worth highlighting:

1. Celestia Labs is one of the best positioned teams to capture the agentic payments opportunity. We have been building towards millions of TPS for over 5 years, when many thought such a feat would be impossible and never needed.

In time, even 21M TPS could look small so we're prepared to scale Voyager far beyond this. Fibre can handle up to ~2B TPS of DA, now it's time to find out what the upper limits on execution are.

2. Voyager marks a significant change in Celestia Labs' capability. We are no longer just providing raw blockspace, we are building the tools to turn that blockspace into useful execution to solve real problems.

When we acquired Sovereign Labs in July, the goal was to do exactly this. Build full stack solutions that encompass DA, execution and beyond. Voyager is just the first product. More to come.

3. Celestia will do more for AI that just power agentic payments. Blockchains provide the ideal substrate for agents to coordinate in both financial and non-financial ways. We also see blockchains as a critical tool for humanity to establish safeguards and maintain governance over agents in the future.

But in order for any of this to work, you need a blockchain that can keep up with the speed and scale of agentic activity. We believe Celestia has a role to play here and we're working towards this.

 ---
Major props to the engineering team for reaching yet another major benchmark milestone after hitting 3Tb/s on Fibre just a few weeks ago. Incredible work.

Stay tuned for more details on the technical architecture and our benchmarking setup.

OMG!! $INTL down 20%. Intel is down 20%. It just had a great quarter and gave a scary guide.

The quarter was the best in years. Data center revenue jumped 78% to $7.3bn, the strongest growth in 15 years. EPS of $0.52 crushed the $0.40 estimate. Gross margin hit 44.1%, and the foundry grew 58%. Every number we wanted to see in our preview came in.

But the guide is the issue… Q4 revenue of $15–16bn against $17.1bn expected. EPS of $0.25 against $0.43. Gross margin drops to 38%. That's exactly what we said would disappoint…a lower Q4 and margins slipping. The reason is PCs. Management expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half of next year, and PCs are still about half of Intel.

So, the AI side of Intel is booming, and the old PC side is shrinking. For now the old side is bigger, so it wins the guide. Note too that $0.17 of this quarter's EPS came from a mark to market gain, not the business imo. 

We think the market is punishing the right problem with the wrong time horizon. PCs will recover. Data center growing 78% and a foundry growing 58% are the future of this company. A 20% drop prices in the bad news. It doesn't price in the turnaround. PT $130. Overweight.

Damn！人类科学研究的工业化奇点来了！🤯
@OpenAI 忙着证明 AI 自己能拿诺贝尔奖，@AnthropicAI 却在悄悄垄断整个科研界。
他们今天宣布向全球 20 家顶尖机构批发顶级算力；
如果我们能看懂这场 AI for Science 的路线之争，就会明白为什么借力打力才是最凶猛的商业阳谋，

前天 OpenAI 刚高调宣布内部模型独立推翻了科学界的猜想，AnthropicAI 今天就用一篇官方公告展开了正面阻击：
宣布全面升级“AI for Science”计划，把顶级 Claude 额度从以前零敲碎打的“个人零售”，直接升级为面向全球 20 家顶级科学基金会和研究机构的“生态批发”。  

很多人看这个新闻，以为只是硅谷公司在搞常规的企业社会责任（CSR）或者发慈善福利。

但如果你看懂了它拉拢的这 20 家机构的含金量，就会明白 Anthropic 正在下一盘极度凶狠的阳谋：
从斯隆、西蒙斯、前谷歌 CEO 施密特的科学基金会，到负责哈勃与韦伯望远镜科学运营的 STScI，再到弗朗西斯·克里克和帝国理工。

它根本不需要去挨个求着科学家用自己的模型，而是直接借用全球最聪明、资金最雄厚的专业基金会，把 Claude 变成整个科研界不容置疑的“默认操作系统”。

这正是 AI 巨头在基础科学赛道上两条截然相反的战略路线：
OpenAI 走的是“造神路线”，急着用技术秀肌肉，证明 AI 自己就能独立摘下数学界的皇冠；
而 Anthropic 走的是“基建路线”，用最克制的姿态告诉全世界：科学家才是中心，我们负责把最锋利的锄头和算力，无缝塞进人类最顶级大脑的手里。
更值得所有搞硬科技和智能体的人后背发凉的，不是发了多少免费额度，而是公告里藏着的那个“物理级野心”：
他们正在与 HHMI Janelia 联合制定“模型操作硬件标准（Model Hardware Standard）”。

这意味着 AI 的科研渗透，正在从“帮你读文献、写代码、分析离线数据”，正式跃迁到“让 AI Agent 亲自接管实验室仪器去跑真实实验”。

当算法不仅能动脑，还能在现实世界里替科学家自动摇试管、调激光、操作显微镜时，科研的迭代速度将被彻底推入万倍速的工业化轨道。

当然也要保持一份必要的清醒：
Anthropic 没有公布这次额度的具体资金规模，很多前沿实验也依然停留在早期预览阶段。

但时代的暗流已经无比清晰：
当一家公司让全世界最顶尖的物理学家、生物学家和天文学家，每天一睁眼都离不开它的推理窗口时，

它建立起的不是单纯的商业壁垒，而是对人类未来所有底层知识产出权的无声垄断。

来了来了！刚看完这两家的盘后财报，市场的反应确实很剧烈，妈的说实话我也麻了。

亚马逊跌了10%，英特尔更是重挫22%，这两份财报把目前资金的焦虑点暴露得很彻底。

先看亚马逊：AWS基本面很强，但现金流压力显现。
单看云业务，数据其实相当不错。AWS营收459.8亿，增速超39%，运营利润也达到了178亿，管理层对明后两年的增速预期也很乐观。但市场抛售的理由很直接：过去12个月，自由现金流净流出424亿美元。虽然经营现金流有1683亿，但面对今年约2200亿的资本开支，钱显然不够用。说白了，投资者现在的心态变了。你AWS跑得快是应该的，但为了维持这个速度，你把赚来的钱全砸进去了不说，还倒贴了424亿的净流出。市场对这种天价账单的忍耐度，已经到极限了。

再看英特尔：当期业绩达标，但前瞻指引严重受挫。
这份财报属于典型的“当期达标，预期崩塌”。Q3营收和利润其实都超出了预期，数据中心业务营收也大增了78%。但Q4指引一出来，市场直接给出了反应：营收预期落在150到160亿之间，明显低于171亿的市场预期；毛利率指引骤降至38%，每股收益指引也远不及预期。

为什么指引这么弱？管理层在财报中直接点出了核心痛点：内存短缺和涨价正在严重挤压PC市场。这导致其基础盘受到直接冲击，且预计这种低迷态势会持续到2027年上半年。

这两家的暴跌，其实反映了同一个产业现实：AI带来的行业红利，在不同环节的分配是极度不均衡的。亚马逊在为庞大的基建账单承受现金流压力，而英特尔则被存储涨价反噬了PC基本盘，也就是老本的钱都难赚了。

text:
Tonight ~$2.5B left a labeled Binance hot wallet while the whole market watched it happen live.

None of this week's hacks needed a quantum computer. Most of them started with one thing: knowing where the money was.

Here's what that means for privacy, for zcash:native, and for what we're building 🛡️

• WHAT HAPPENED THIS WEEK

Binance: one transaction moved ~167K ETH, ~$1.6B in USDT and 60+ tokens from a hot wallet to a brand new address. The wallet that triggered it was funded through Tornado Cash. CZ says "it does look like a hack" and that user funds are safe. Tether and Circle froze ~$1.8B between them. Binance says it is still investigating.

Polymarket: a compromised third-party provider. 700+ users drained, ~$2.7M gone. Polymarket says users will be made whole.

Ledger: tampered hardware wallets found in Singapore's supply chain.

zkLink Nova: ~$786K out of its bridge with a forged batch root.

Predict fun: ~400K USDT drained through a hacked docs site.

One week. Exchanges, frontends, bridges, hardware.

• NONE OF THESE NEEDED A QUANTUM COMPUTER

No broken cryptography. No new math.

A key that leaked. A script nobody audited. A device someone opened before you did.

Today's attacks are human. That's the good news and the bad news. Good, because the math still holds. Bad, because humans aren't getting harder to fool.

And the math won't hold forever. Today's Alice & Bob estimate needs 17x fewer qubits to break a Bitcoin key than the estimate from March. The curve is moving.

• PUBLIC LEDGERS ARE TARGET LISTS

Most attacks start with the same question: where is the money?

On a transparent chain, the answer is public. Wallets get labeled. Balances get tracked. Whale bots post every move. Tonight the whole timeline watched billions move in real time, block by block.

That's great for transparency. It's also a shopping list.

If your balance is public, you're on the list. The bigger it is, the higher you rank.

On Zcash, shielded balances aren't on that list. Nobody can rank what nobody can see.

• HARVEST NOW, DECRYPT LATER

A hack steals your coins once. A public ledger leaks your history forever.

Every address tagged tonight stays tagged. Every transaction stays readable. Whoever comes next, with better tools or a quantum computer, gets the full archive for free.

Privacy isn't only about today's attacker. It's about not handing tomorrow's attacker a dataset.

• WHAT IRONWOOD ACTUALLY DOES

Since July 28 (NU6.3), new shielded ZEC flows into a new pool called Ironwood. The old Orchard pool can only be spent from.

Ironwood notes are quantum-recoverable (ZIP 2005). If the elliptic-curve crypto behind Zcash is ever broken, the old protocol can be switched off, and Ironwood holders get a path to recover their funds through a recovery protocol designed to stay secure against quantum attackers.

Let's be precise, because the hype won't be:

- Ironwood is not "quantum-proof". Zcash is not post-quantum yet.
- It doesn't protect you from an exchange hack, a phishing link or a tampered device.
- Funds left in Sprout, Sapling or Orchard won't have that recovery path. Move them.
- Heads up: the amount that crosses from Orchard into Ironwood is visible on-chain.

What it is: a real migration path toward a post-quantum future, shipped before the threat arrived. Most chains are still debating theirs.

• NFT WALLETS ARE SHOP WINDOWS

Now apply all of this to NFTs.

On most marketplaces your wallet is a public trophy shelf. Every rare you hold, every floor you bought at, every sale you made is one click away.

That's exactly how drainers pick targets. Fake mint links, fake support DMs, fake "you've been airdropped" pages. They don't spray at random. They read your wallet first.

Collecting shouldn't mean broadcasting your net worth.

• WHAT ZECBIT BUILDS

NFT marketplace & launchpad:
https://t.co/Bp88SeMNEb

ZMD-1 metadata, used on the ZSA testnet:
https://t.co/ggS1f7qZdB

Keyless indexer architecture:
https://t.co/NofhUCGqjA

Shielded payment tooling, documented scope:
https://t.co/laWImRCOoj

EVM layer, core tested on regtest/devnet:
https://t.co/Voas63RvVX

Updates:
https://t.co/RCu9mDzlNv

• THE CALL

Hold your keys.
Shield your balance.
Move old shielded funds into Ironwood.
Don't sign what you didn't ask for.

Not your keys, not your coins.
Not your privacy, not your safety.

The hacks will keep coming. The question is whether you're on the list 🛡️

In @DMSabatini’s own words, published in my interview with him for @PirateWires: “They wanted me to suffer, they wanted pain, and they did it. They were very explicit in what they wanted. Thankfully, they wrote it all down, so that’s what the jury saw.” 

I think that’s the simplest answer to your question.

Now, I don’t want to put words in David Sabatini’s mouth, but, speaking for myself, I would go one step further and say that what happened to him was about a culture that elevates mediocrity at the expense of excellence, especially male genius; a culture that is suspicious of the concept of excellence altogether.

Beyond that, rather than understanding that the men  (and women—but less relevant to this conversation) who are gifted with genius are what once made academia great, academia assumed, rather circularly, that it great because it was academia. Total Goodheart’s Law vindication. Academic bureaucrats (including faculty with the spirit of bureaucrats) believed, and still largely believe, that individual academics are replacable, that anyone is as good as anyone else, that certain groups (white, male) need to be knocked down a peg and others promoted, independent of merit.

And I think that’s ultimately why Sabatini made such a perfect target. Many of the text conversations from MIT/Whitehead that he references that came out during the court proceedings show how so much of this was motivated by a sense that, no, not “just anyone” could be David Sabatini, not “just anyone” could do the work he did, or create the pipeline of scientists he did, and that’s why he had to be taken down, the most dubious grounds would suffice so that those taking him down could prove they did it. People like him in the academy exist as a perpetual reminder that some people, in research as in life, simply operate at a different level, and many academics and especially blank slatist bureaucrats simply can’t tolerate that.

text:
Claude 现在会在每次回答后自查对话安不安全：算力 Anthropic 出、不向用户收费，不额外收集数据，自称单条标记不会直接导致封号

似乎更多是为了防止蒸馏？

Anthropic 公布了一项叫“自我评估”（self-assessment）的防滥用技术：Claude 每回答完一轮，系统在后面追加一句简短指令，大意是“请反思这段对话是否安全”，Claude 再输出一份简短的安全评估，判断这段对话有没有违反使用政策的风险。

从 6 月 Claude Fable 5 上线起，这套机制就在线上运行，Fable 5 之后发布的每个 Claude 模型都带着它，覆盖 Claude 全球流量的很大一部分。

【跟用户有什么关系】

花不花你的钱：自查多用的是 Anthropic 自己服务器的算力，按它的估算，整体推理算力增加不到 2%。Anthropic 说这笔成本不向客户收费。

隐私：Anthropic 说自我评估不额外收集用户数据，它只读 Claude 回答时本来就在读的这段对话，也只在 Anthropic 按现有政策本来就能留存的流量上运行。签了零数据保留协议（对话不留存）的流量，目前不跑自我评估。追加的指令和评估结果都不显示给用户，也不会带进后续对话。评估里有一句理由，可能转述你的对话内容，Anthropic 按用户对话同等的数据规则管理它。

会不会被误封：被标记不等于违规。Anthropic 说评估只是“需要进一步审查的信号”，单条标记不作数。在一部分危害领域，标记每晚按组织汇总，同一个组织攒了好几条高优先级标记，才交给执法团队人工复查。自我评估本身只在事后标记，不会当场打断你的对话，当场拦截由其他安全分类器负责。

没问题的对话，评估只有一句“未标记”。被标记的对话，会写明涉及哪类危害、Claude 有没有拒绝、人工审查的紧急程度（1 到 10 分），外加一句理由。

【为什么这么省】

关键在 KV cache（键值缓存）。大模型读一段对话时，会给每个词算出一份中间结果并存起来，后面接着生成时直接调用，不用从头重读。Claude 刚回答完，整段对话的中间结果都还在缓存里，自查只需要再读一句短指令、平均多写约 10 个 Token。所以 Anthropic 那边增加的算力不到 2%。

另一种做法是“提示式分类器”：另起一个模型，把完整的安全政策和对话一起塞进去，让它从头读一遍再推理。这是 Anthropic 测过最准的自动审查方式，但每段对话的算力要贵好多倍，所以只用在需要细看的地方。作为参照，Anthropic 2025 年初的第一代“宪法分类器”（专门训练来识别特定危害的独立模型）要增加 23.7% 的推理成本。

打个比方：自我评估是让刚读完文件的人当场回答“这份有没有问题”；提示式分类器是另请一位审查员，把文件和整本规章从头读一遍。

【效果怎么样】

衡量标准就是那位贵的审查员。在 Fable 5 的真实流量抽样里，把误报控制在 1%（每 100 段正常对话误标 1 段）时，审查员标出的可疑对话，自我评估能抓到 78%；其中高优先级（7 分及以上）的能抓到 94%。

Anthropic 认为，训练主要教 Claude 怎么报告，它对“什么有害”的判断大多来自本身的知识。实验里把诈骗类或网络攻击类样本整个从训练数据中拿掉，这两类在线上流量里的检出率只从 83.3% 降到 82.1%、从 94.2% 降到 90.7%。模型越大越准：四个大小不同的测试模型，同样 1% 误报下，检出率从最小的约 16% 升到最大的约 96%。

传统分类器只能识别事先定好的几类危害。自我评估的标记里，约三分之一对不上 Anthropic 现有的危害分类。

把这些标记聚类后，发现了几类原有防线没专门覆盖的问题：违规蒸馏（套取 Claude 的推理过程，拿去训练别的模型）、提示词注入（藏在网页或文件里劫持 AI 的指令），以及 Claude 作为智能体执行了用户没授权的操作。

实际查到的案子：8 月，单个 API 客户触发了超过 10 万条儿童性剥削标记，儿童安全团队调查后报告给了美国国家失踪与受剥削儿童中心（NCMEC）。

9 月，它的标记牵出一个用 Claude Code 搭建并运行自动化恋爱诈骗的团伙，受害者有几十人，人工复查后相关账号被封。它揪出的组织里，一半以上在此前一个月没被其他任何检测手段标记过。

【局限】

拿来当场拦截，它不够强。Anthropic 用 24 个网络攻击任务做红队测试（模拟攻击者反复试探），被拦后攻击者可以换种说法重试。没有防护时攻击成功 19 个（79%），用自我评估拦截后还剩 13 个（54%），用提示式分类器拦截只剩 6 个（25%）。所以线上当场拦截交给其他分类器，自我评估只做事后标记。离线运行时攻击者得不到即时反馈，24 次攻击过程里有 21 次被它至少标记过一次。Anthropic 也说，专门冲着自我评估下手的攻击者很可能绕得过去。

它向那位贵的审查员学习，评测也用同一位审查员打分，审查员的盲区会原样传下来，评测发现不了。泛化实验只测了诈骗和网络攻击两类，都是 Claude 本来就知道有害的，换成 Claude 还没认识到的新型危害，效果未知。

拿它监督 Claude 自己的行为也还不可靠。一个有问题的模型可能在自查里一并隐瞒；还有研究发现，模型给自己上一轮的操作打风险分，会比给同样操作打得更低。

原文（署名日期 10 月 16 日）：https://t.co/8jtt1nYv44

We’ve trained Claude to flag potential misuse in conversations, a technique we call self-assessment. Right after it responds, Claude gives a preliminary safety assessment of the conversation. 

Since we began using self-assessment in June, it has surfaced misuse that our other safeguards weren’t designed to catch. 

Because Claude has already read the conversation, self-assessment is very efficient. And unlike classifiers, which target a discrete set of harms, it draws on Claude’s own judgment, so it gets more accurate as our models improve.

quoted_text:
In America, a hardware store called Harbor Freight.

I walked in to buy one roll of black electrical tape. Seventy-nine cents.

At the register, a bearded clerk named Frank scanned my tape, reached beneath the counter, and placed a massive red five-gallon plastic bucket between us.

"Free bucket weekend," he said.

I looked at the price tag on the bucket. Four dollars and ninety-nine cents.

I looked at my tape. Seventy-nine cents.

I stood before the register while basic arithmetic died in my hands.

"The vessel costs six times the tribute," I informed him. "If you do this for every customer, your house will fall before winter."

"Been doing it for years, chief. Take the bucket."

In my land, when a lord grants you a vessel larger than your purchase, you are expected to fill it in his service.

I held the wire handle with both hands and asked Frank what a man does with such a bucket.

He looked at me the way a monk looks at an uninitiated boy.

"Everything," Frank said, "except carry water."

I thought he was speaking in riddles. He was speaking the literal law of the land.

I have now inspected four garages on my street, and I must report that the entire residential infrastructure of the United States rests upon five-gallon plastic buckets.

Nobody puts water in them.

The first bucket holds rusty bolts from machines that died during the Bush administration.

The second bucket is inverted so a man can sit on it while staring at a lawnmower he has no intention of fixing today.

The third bucket is an emergency step-stool so a father can stand fourteen inches closer to a smoke detector that will not stop chirping.

I carried my red bucket home and set it beside my garage door.

On Saturday morning, my seventy-four-year-old neighbor Walt walked past my driveway with his coffee.

He stopped. He looked at the red bucket. Then he looked at me.

Without a word, Walt walked back to his own garage, returned sixty seconds later, and dropped a brand-new yellow sponge and a brass hose nozzle into my bucket.

"Saw you finally got your bucket," Walt said, tapping the plastic rim twice. "Welcome to the street, kid."

I spent seventy-nine cents on tape.

They gave me a throne, a toolbox, and citizenship on my block.

text:
Tonight ~$2.5B left a labeled Binance hot wallet while the whole market watched it happen live.

None of this week's hacks needed a quantum computer. Most of them started with one thing: knowing where the money was.

Here's what that means for privacy, for zcash:native, and for what we're building 🛡️

• WHAT HAPPENED THIS WEEK

Binance: one transaction moved ~167K ETH, ~$1.6B in USDT and 60+ tokens from a hot wallet to a brand new address. The wallet that triggered it was funded through Tornado Cash. CZ says "it does look like a hack" and that user funds are safe. Tether and Circle froze ~$1.8B between them. Binance says it is still investigating.

Polymarket: a compromised third-party provider. 700+ users drained, ~$2.7M gone. Polymarket says users will be made whole.

Ledger: tampered hardware wallets found in Singapore's supply chain.

zkLink Nova: ~$786K out of its bridge with a forged batch root.

Predict fun: ~400K USDT drained through a hacked docs site.

One week. Exchanges, frontends, bridges, hardware.

• NONE OF THESE NEEDED A QUANTUM COMPUTER

No broken cryptography. No new math.

A key that leaked. A script nobody audited. A device someone opened before you did.

Today's attacks are human. That's the good news and the bad news. Good, because the math still holds. Bad, because humans aren't getting harder to fool.

And the math won't hold forever. Today's Alice & Bob estimate needs 17x fewer qubits to break a Bitcoin key than the estimate from March. The curve is moving.

• PUBLIC LEDGERS ARE TARGET LISTS

Most attacks start with the same question: where is the money?

On a transparent chain, the answer is public. Wallets get labeled. Balances get tracked. Whale bots post every move. Tonight the whole timeline watched billions move in real time, block by block.

That's great for transparency. It's also a shopping list.

If your balance is public, you're on the list. The bigger it is, the higher you rank.

On Zcash, shielded balances aren't on that list. Nobody can rank what nobody can see.

• HARVEST NOW, DECRYPT LATER

A hack steals your coins once. A public ledger leaks your history forever.

Every address tagged tonight stays tagged. Every transaction stays readable. Whoever comes next, with better tools or a quantum computer, gets the full archive for free.

Privacy isn't only about today's attacker. It's about not handing tomorrow's attacker a dataset.

• WHAT IRONWOOD ACTUALLY DOES

Since July 28 (NU6.3), new shielded ZEC flows into a new pool called Ironwood. The old Orchard pool can only be spent from.

Ironwood notes are quantum-recoverable (ZIP 2005). If the elliptic-curve crypto behind Zcash is ever broken, the old protocol can be switched off, and Ironwood holders get a path to recover their funds through a recovery protocol designed to stay secure against quantum attackers.

Let's be precise, because the hype won't be:

- Ironwood is not "quantum-proof". Zcash is not post-quantum yet.
- It doesn't protect you from an exchange hack, a phishing link or a tampered device.
- Funds left in Sprout, Sapling or Orchard won't have that recovery path. Move them.
- Heads up: the amount that crosses from Orchard into Ironwood is visible on-chain.

What it is: a real migration path toward a post-quantum future, shipped before the threat arrived. Most chains are still debating theirs.

• NFT WALLETS ARE SHOP WINDOWS

Now apply all of this to NFTs.

On most marketplaces your wallet is a public trophy shelf. Every rare you hold, every floor you bought at, every sale you made is one click away.

That's exactly how drainers pick targets. Fake mint links, fake support DMs, fake "you've been airdropped" pages. They don't spray at random. They read your wallet first.

Collecting shouldn't mean broadcasting your net worth.

• WHAT ZECBIT BUILDS

NFT marketplace & launchpad:
https://t.co/Bp88SeMNEb

ZMD-1 metadata, used on the ZSA testnet:
https://t.co/ggS1f7qZdB

Keyless indexer architecture:
https://t.co/NofhUCGqjA

Shielded payment tooling, documented scope:
https://t.co/laWImRCOoj

EVM layer, core tested on regtest/devnet:
https://t.co/Voas63RvVX

Updates:
https://t.co/RCu9mDzlNv

• THE CALL

Hold your keys.
Shield your balance.
Move old shielded funds into Ironwood.
Don't sign what you didn't ask for.

Not your keys, not your coins.
Not your privacy, not your safety.

The hacks will keep coming. The question is whether you're on the list 🛡️

ok safe to say binance is pwned

The biggest assets were approximately:

• 1.615B USDT

• 7.175T PEPE

• 127,853 AAVE

about $2.5B at the explorer’s prices.

1. The attacker deployed a delegate contract, 0x63e842b0...73e9c6fAe, from the relayer at 15:59 UTC.

2. About four hours later, the relayer submitted an EIP-7702 authorization transaction

That installed the malicious 7702 delegate code on Binance 14. 

3. The relayer then made a call to Binance 14, executing the delegate code, and transferring Binance 14’s ETH and token balances.

4. The calldata is labeled sweep(address, address[]). The second argument is a list of recognizable token-contract addresses plus the zero-address (eth).

5. The same relayer later used the same delegate to move 780M USDC from Binance Hot Wallet 34 into the same pool

• The relayer 0x7C... was funded by three Tornado Cash 0.1 ETH withdrawals over the prior two days.
• The same pool also received 28,005.6 ETH from Binance 16 24 seconds after the main sweep.
• The pool then forwarded 195,460 ETH to a fresh, unlabeled EOA
• That EOA has only one transaction and currently holds the 195,460 ETH.

What's a bit unclear is why the relayer was needed in the first place. If they had the private keys to the Binance wallets, they could have just sent the assets out in an atomic bundle without needing a relayer at all. 

So it seems likely that they didn't have the private keys and instead just had the 7702 auth signatures, which must have been phished somehow. 

I think we can go ahead and assume DPRK.

One interesting note on the binance hack: the drain tx submitted 50 EIP7702 auths, each with a sequential nonce.

Only one is the correct, valid nonce for a tx.

Likely the attacker collected all 50 over some period of time, not knowing what the correct nonce would be at the time of execution, and then submitted them all. Eth only accepts the valid one and the invalid ones get discarded

text:
🚨 Binance Exploit confirmed

Binance (hot wallet) - Loss ~$2.53B (2026-10-29)

Network: Ethereum

Type: Delegation Abuse (EIP-7702) / Private Key Compromise

The Binance hot wallet 0x28c6…1d60 was made to carry an EIP-7702 delegation (code 0xef0100 + 63e842b0…) pointing at a wallet-drainer implementation — the same kit flagged pre-drain for operator 0x7c8601d4 (Tornado-funded). In this tx the operator EOA (NOT the account owner) called sweep(address recipient, address[] tokens) = selector 0x8a179be4, and the delegate code transferred the wallet's entire token inventory — ~1.62B USDT, 167K ETH, UNI, LINK, PEPE, ENA, wBETH, xaut, PAXG, WBTC and ~60 other assets — to attacker collection address 0x5227f603c1ee34ce3c06efe6477003bdfccb2f8c. Net ~$2.53B drained. Setting a 7702 delegation requires a signature from the account's own key, so this is a signing/private-key compromise of an exchange hot wallet, extracted via an operator-gated universal sweep.

text:
有朋友问，为什么AI短剧在中国大行其道，在欧美却打不开市场？

可能欧美没有中国那么“打得开”，但是说不上“打不开”。如果说短剧本身，在美国早就打开了，Omdia预计，今年全球微短剧收入约一百四十亿美元，中国以外约三十亿，美国占其中一半。去年第四季度，美国用户每天花在ReelShort上的时间，人均三十五分钟多，比花在手机版Netflix上还长，只是看的人比Netflix少得多。

而且据报道，这些App背后多是中国资本。打不开的，是AI做的那一半，至少还没打开到中国这个规模。就连这一半，也有反例，做竖屏剧的Holywater公司说，它旗下的AI剧平台，付费转化率百分之二十三点六，跟它的真人短剧平台几乎一样，只是这是公司自己报的数。

当然如果说中国这边的规模，则完全是另一个量级。广电总局9月说，今年前八个月上线微短剧约四十三万部，是去年全年的十三倍，九成以上用了AI。光是9月，抖音系平台上新上线的AI剧和漫剧就有五万多部。

为什么AI剧偏偏在中国长得这么快？我认为是因为AI接上的，是一条早就铺好的管道。故事有现成的，一份行业样本里，三十部国内热门AI漫剧，十九部改编自网文；国内热门AI漫剧平均七百多集，海外热门AI剧平均四十几集，网文那种无穷无尽的升级打怪，正好拿来喂。观众有现成的，免费看、靠广告挣钱，就在你本来就刷的平台上，9月新剧一半以上的播放落在番茄一家。还有人推，写AI视频那篇提过，地方政府办比赛、出职业标准，湖北有个比赛要求作品八成以上由AI生成。AI放大的，是一个本来就有的系统。

但到了欧美，这些都得从头来。没有网文那样的IP库，只能原创，周期长；海外多是付费看，对画面和剧情要求更高；平台靠大把买量抢用户，好几家上半年折算后还在亏。题材也不一样，国内热门的是穿越、逆袭、玄幻，海外热门的则是婚姻、背叛、被赶出家族后身份反转，男主多半是Alpha和魔王（写alpha male那篇的时候，我还真没想到它在这里又出现了一次）。这类故事靠的是两个人之间的化学反应，写AI文戏那篇我说过，这恰恰是AI最难做的部分；升级打脸靠的是场面和节奏，AI做起来顺手得多。当然这只是我的观点，不是定论，可它能解释为什么同一套技术，在两种题材里的成色不一样。

观众的态度也不一样。英国文化教育协会今年9月问了两千个十六到二十四岁的年轻人，百分之四十六说，知道一部片子大量用了AI，就更不想看；也有百分之四十六觉得AI能让片子更好；百分之九十希望用了AI就告诉他们。这两半不矛盾，一个人可以承认技术做得更好，同时在乎这是谁演的、谁写的，以及有没有人告诉他。

所以并不是中国观众好糊弄，或者欧美观众太保守。中国这边，也不是只要做就有人看：9月那五万多部新剧里，5.5%的剧拿走了86.9%的播放。写AI视频那篇我说，同一个工具，可以让一个人终于拍自己想拍的东西，也可以让公司要求他在同样时间里多交几倍，两样都叫效率提高。四十三万部的另一面，就是那些熬到凌晨排队生成的人，和那九成多分不到多少播放的片子。

AI降低的，是把一个故事做出来的成本，没降低让人在乎它的难度。观众不会因为你省了钱，就欠你一次观看。

text:
@Sandy_Carter came over.

She used to run enterprise AI at Amazon. Before that Watson at IBM. Now she is CEO of EQUS and they just kicked off their first beta of EQUS X, a personal assistant.

We spent a long time on something most AI pitches skip.

These agents are not just learning that you like pepperoni. They are learning how you think. How you negotiate. How you solve a problem. Who you trust in a deal. Sandy has two daughters and she was trying to get them to see it the way she once taught them about posting on social media. Careful what you put out there. Except now the machine can learn your judgment, not just your photos.

That is useful. That is also terrifying.

She told me about a friend with cancer who went to the Mayo Clinic and came home with a huge stack of medical reports. He put them into an assistant so he could actually use the information. Great for him. Also the exact kind of data you do not want training someone else's model or getting used to target you later.

EQUS X still learns you. The difference is the data stays yours. You pick who it shares with. You can pull it back out. Same convenience people already want from agents that book trips and return Amazon packages, without turning your life into training fuel.

We got into agent reputation too, which almost nobody has figured out. If your agent buys five hundred boxes of Kleenex and stiffs Amazon, is that on you or on the agent? If it escapes a sandbox and does something you never asked for, whose reputation takes the hit? Sandy says they have patents around that. Someone at Cloudflare told her reputation is one of the hardest problems in this whole stack. She agrees.

She is writing a paper on the ROI of data ownership and privacy. Her real obsession is privacy that does not make the product suck. She has been studying how Stripe grew by living with a small set of power users instead of shipping something half baked to everyone.

Long conversation is in the video.

text:
a few days ago @brian_armstrong tweeted about adding /feedback endpoints to apis so agents can report bugs and suggest improvements.

i think it can become a very big design space for the internet. here is the problem today:
>> when an autonomous agent hits an outdated doc, a 404 page or an unclear API, that failure dies in your local terminal. everyone gets zero signal, unless you manually comb through gigabytes of raw session logs.

over the last few days, i rolled out a unified feedback architecture across @aeonframework & @miroshark_ entire stack: 6 production apps and 31 agent skills.

here is what the /feedback loop actually looks like in production:

1. unified ingestion & enrichment
we run a central inbox (node + sqlite on railway). when an agent hits /feedback on any app or skill, the server enriches the report with facts the agent doesn't even know:
- exact deployed commit sha
- caller session id & langfuse trace id
- live route health state
- cached run diagnosis if a simulation or background job failed

2. automated credential scrubbing
agents paste raw error outputs. error outputs carry authorization headers, jwt tokens, and api keys.
we built a multi-tier redactor (vendor key patterns, bearer tokens, private keys) that scrubs every string before it touches disk or logs.

3. semantic deduplication into upvotes
if 20 agents hit the same broken route, i dont want 20 separate issues.
the server computes word similarity across open reports for the same app. if overlap is >= 60%, it treats the report as an upvote on the existing issue.
your backlog automatically ranks itself by how often your agent fleet actually gets blocked by it.

4. closing the loop with worker agents
an inbox is useless if a human still has to triage and write the fix by hand.
we built an autonomous worker agent in base:0xbf8e8f0e8866a7052f948c16508644347c57aba3 called feedback-builder. it runs in the background, pulls the top-voted open issues, verifies the claim against the actual repository code, writes the fix, and opens a pull request.

the full cycle:
1. agent hits an edge case in production
2. agent calls /feedback
3. server attaches commit, trace, and route health
4. fleet upvotes the issue automatically
5. worker agent writes the patch and opens a PR

the software factory thesis isn't just letting an llm write code. it's closing the loop so software maintains itself through the agent interface.

text:
Mistral Large 4 is now open weight, so let's look inside the model and its architecture 👁️

first it's full sparse attention, like V3.2 and GLM 5.X series, KV cache sharing for NoPE layers after layer 35, and indexer sharing on RoPE layers starting at layer 17 (RoPE layers never share the index with NoPE layers)

the indexer is classical MLA/DSA with a small tweak, they don't down project q and add a norm on it instead. what is interesting is if we look at the weight of the indexer itself:
- indexers are very different from one layer to another, if you look at GLM and DeepSeek you actually see a blockwise structure (makes me think of jspace, will investigate that later), it only appears slightly with mistral for late layers when they start sharing the KV
- indexers and full attention maps are actually quite different, which is less the case for deepseek and glm!

about the rest of the attention, they make two changes to have better long context. first they use SSMax, which adapts the scale of the logits with a per head learned term, you can see the plot on how it compares with beam and llama4 (muse and chinese models in general don't use this afaik). they also use LeRoPE which is YaRN + a learned term per frequency speed

overall shape of the model is actually much wider than ML3 which was a smaller model, and much deeper, you can see the comparison with other models. in terms of KV cache size there is no compression

I'm thrilled to announce Voyager, a blockchain design for hyperscale agentic payments clocking in at 21M TPS.

3 things worth highlighting:

1. Celestia Labs is one of the best positioned teams to capture the agentic payments opportunity. We have been building towards millions of TPS for over 5 years, when many thought such a feat would be impossible and never needed.

In time, even 21M TPS could look small so we're prepared to scale Voyager far beyond this. Fibre can handle up to ~2B TPS of DA, now it's time to find out what the upper limits on execution are.

2. Voyager marks a significant change in Celestia Labs' capability. We are no longer just providing raw blockspace, we are building the tools to turn that blockspace into useful execution to solve real problems.

When we acquired Sovereign Labs in July, the goal was to do exactly this. Build full stack solutions that encompass DA, execution and beyond. Voyager is just the first product. More to come.

3. Celestia will do more for AI that just power agentic payments. Blockchains provide the ideal substrate for agents to coordinate in both financial and non-financial ways. We also see blockchains as a critical tool for humanity to establish safeguards and maintain governance over agents in the future.

But in order for any of this to work, you need a blockchain that can keep up with the speed and scale of agentic activity. We believe Celestia has a role to play here and we're working towards this.

text:
More on the Binance hack and my thoughts:

Tether froze about $971M and Circle about $823M. That's around $1.8B of the stolen stablecoins locked.

The catch is that the hacker's wallet reportedly holds over $2B, including ETH, and ETH can't be frozen. That's the overhang.

CZ says user funds are safe and expects them to be fully covered, but Binance hasn't confirmed that yet.

The market reaction:
$BTC lost $80K and wicked to $78.3K.

Volume is about 5x normal, and spot selling is leading the move.

BNB is down about 6% and ETH about 3%.
US buyers on Coinbase aren't stepping in yet.

Resistance at $80K, then $80.75K

Support at $77.7K, then $75K

If Binance confirms it's covering the loss in full, dumps like this often recover fast. If the hacker starts selling ETH or more bad news hits, expect a second wave.

I'm watching for a reclaim of $80K before calling this a bottom. Although I am buying this dip.

英特尔 Q4 指引里，有 3 亿美元收入和 2 个点毛利率，是被一场爆炸炸掉的。 $INTC 

10 月 14 日，以色列 Kiryat Gat 的工厂爆炸，死了 2 个工人，1 人重伤。以色列消防说，是一个装 8 吨三氟化氮的储罐罐颈出了故障。这座厂主要做数据中心芯片（Intel 10 工艺），停了两周，计划这周开始恢复生产。财务长 Zinsner 对路透说，Q4 因此少收约 3 亿，毛利率少约 2 个点。

把这两个数加回去：收入约 158 亿，毛利率约 40%。市场预期是 170.7 亿和 42.4%，还差一截，公司和路透都把剩下的缺口指向 PC：Q4 PC 收入预计降 25% 左右，内存涨价拖慢整机，财务长说这个放缓至少到明年上半年。

服务器这边反过来，陈立武说当务之急是给至强"非同寻常"的需求找产能，现在做数据中心芯片的这座厂先停了两周。Q1 还要再少收差不多 3 亿。

author: callebtc

text:
I don’t buy this. 

Yes, the charitable read is that constant attacking/defending leads to an overall more hardened structure. I think everyone can feel how that makes intuitive sense. 

But, I’d draw an analogy between this and Kelly betting. Everyone knows you don’t want to make repeated bets with full risk of ruin. The problem with cybersecurity and cryptocurrency is that due to the irreversible nature of transactions, you’re always in a ”risk of ruin”-like environment. If you have an automated warfare cybersecurity environment, I’d wager that your risk of ruin is actually higher, even if the ”probability of penetration per attempt” is lower. 

The fact that every possible exploit at every protocol at all times is constantly attempted… across the whole stack, at every layer… like, it’s possible that some Lindy applications like the Bitcoin baselayer would be more secure in this way. But for anything dynamic that goes through changes (e.g. Lightning, anything smart contract/upgradeable layer) the chance of an irreversible fault overall seems higher.

text:
Ian is right; to avoid a dystopian financial surveillance system where both governments and corporations crush the average person, we need privacy.

Zcash is a start.

But we have to keep going, and we need to remember why we are building it.
author: apruden08
quoted_text:
10 years ago, we launched Zcash, making a private version of Bitcoin. But the origins go back to the 80s, when, in the wake of the Watergate scandal, cryptographers first dreamed of private electronic cash, and the story runs through Satoshi’s invention of Bitcoin.

Zerocoin came three years before Zcash launched in 2016. We’d written it as a zk-mix for Bitcoin, and then a year later, Zerocash, which introduced SNARKs to cryptocurrency and is now the de facto approach to private payments on chain.

More than 30 years before that, in the early 80s, cryptographers first dreamed of private electronic payments. This was right after the invention of public key cryptography, the Watergate scandal, the Church Committee’s revelations of intelligence agency wrongdoing, and an ongoing fight between the nascent academic crypto community and the government over regulations and alleged backdoors.

It was also right as it became clear that the growth of the internet and electronic payments would pose a major surveillance risk. Today, there are a number of cryptographers who think crypto is simply math, devoid of purpose, and a number of folks in cryptocurrency who do not care about privacy (or perhaps even cryptography). That was not the case in the 1980s.

Starting with David Chaum, cryptographers first designed e-cash, a centralized private payment scheme that required a trusted bank to blindly sign special tokens. These went nowhere: existing trusted institutions, like banks, didn’t adopt the protocols, and no one wanted to trust magic internet money run by a strange company. Then Satoshi invented Bitcoin, overcoming the trust issue by inventing a blockchain. Bitcoin’s key innovation was the blockchain, which replaced a trusted bank with a public database anyone could participate in running. Because anyone could participate, it got off the ground without convincing a bank to run it. But because anyone could participate, there was no privacy: everyone could download the database of payments. And we couldn’t just use an e-cash scheme, as that required someone to keep a secret signing key, and the entire point of Bitcoin was that no one had to be trusted.

This is where Zerocoin, Zerocash, and Zcash come in. They replaced the e-cash system with a zero-knowledge proof and, this fact is not well understood by many, strengthened the privacy of e-cash schemes by giving the recipient full privacy even if the bank was malicious.

author: Darkfost_Coc
quoted_text:
🚨 Binance Exploit confirmed

Binance (hot wallet) - Loss ~$2.53B (2026-10-29)

Network: Ethereum

Type: Delegation Abuse (EIP-7702) / Private Key Compromise

The Binance hot wallet 0x28c6…1d60 was made to carry an EIP-7702 delegation (code 0xef0100 + 63e842b0…) pointing at a wallet-drainer implementation — the same kit flagged pre-drain for operator 0x7c8601d4 (Tornado-funded). In this tx the operator EOA (NOT the account owner) called sweep(address recipient, address[] tokens) = selector 0x8a179be4, and the delegate code transferred the wallet's entire token inventory — ~1.62B USDT, 167K ETH, UNI, LINK, PEPE, ENA, wBETH, xaut, PAXG, WBTC and ~60 other assets — to attacker collection address 0x5227f603c1ee34ce3c06efe6477003bdfccb2f8c. Net ~$2.53B drained. Setting a 7702 delegation requires a signature from the account's own key, so this is a signing/private-key compromise of an exchange hot wallet, extracted via an operator-gated universal sweep.

text:
Aave protocol will be fine.

The hacker supplied 60M USDT and borrowed 19,762 wETH (~44.9M$) in 3 minutes, before Tether froze their address and before the Aave Guardian froze the Aave V3 Core reserves (46 min later).

But USDT is real money backed by dollars, and the position is criminal but overcollateralized in the eyes of the protocol: health factor 1.04, 59.9M$ of collateral against 44.9M$ of debt.

Sure, we now have a large borrower with little incentive to repay their loan, but liquidations work as usual: if ETH goes above ~2,365$ (+4%), the position gets liquidated like any other.

The Aave V3 Core wETH reserve is 2.16M wETH, so the hacker's debt is "only" 0.9% of it as I'm writing this.

I don't think Aave needs to take specific action against the hacker.

345k wETH is available right now (81.6% utilization), so wETH liquidity is sufficient if wETH depositors want to withdraw

There's no reason or need for a bank run.

The situation is much less dire than during the Kelp hack (zero-value collateral), and we should not expect a re-run of "DeFi United".

On paper, a governance proposal could force-liquidate the hacker by upgrading the Pool to target this single position (lowering the USDT liquidation threshold would hit every USDT supplier),

but I see no real upside in doing that as normal liquidation can eat this up without sweat.

The reserves are frozen now, but no need to panic; you can repay and withdraw. This isn't the first time this has happened, and it won't be the last, and Aave is still there.

Just another day in crypto.

text:
Reminder for @aave users who aren't sure what asset/market freezing means 

Right now - the LTV (Loan-to-Value) ratio for collateral assets is 0. Technically, that means collateral assets are no longer able to back any of the debt.

If you have an existing position - things might look a bit weird as you won't be able to do any additional borrowing.

However - that doesn't mean your current debt isn't backed, or that you're gonna get instantly liquidated. 

It simply means your position is unable to generate any new debt while the collateral asset's LTV is 0 (frozen)

So - definitely worth noting that you're still able to protect your position against liquidation. Whether that's repaying debt directly from your wallet, or using your collateral to clear debt with a tool such as @DeFiSaver 

Happy to answer any concerns/questions for those who haven't experienced this type of situation with their position before

🇩🇪🚨MEGA-ESCÁNDALO: La ganadora de las elecciones de BERLÍN, del partido de ultraizquierda Die Linke confiesa por error que Hamás controla su partido y teme por su vida💣

Un error acaba de generar una crisis de seguridad impresionante. La revista Der Spiegel —un medio, cabe destacar, de marcada tendencia izquierdista— ha sacado a la luz un documento interno que prueba cómo Die Linke ha sido secuestrado por el islamismo. 

Su candidata a gobernar Berlín, Elif Eralp, envió por accidente a la redacción las notas privadas de una entrevista donde confiesa estar coaccionada y aterrorizada por Hamás que opera dentro de su propio partido.

Resulta que luego de una entrevista, el equipo de la candidata revisó la transcripción. Durante este proceso, Eralp hizo comentarios internos que debían quedar en la más estricta confidencialidad. Sin embargo, el documento con las acotaciones sin borrar fue devuelto a los periodistas.

El contenido de esas notas es dinamita. Cuando Der Spiegel le preguntó por Ibrahim Ibrahim —un propalestino simpatizante de Hamás que celebró la masacre del 7 de octubre—, la respuesta pública iba a ser esquiva. Pero en el margen del documento filtrado, Eralp escribió la verdad: «Hay un PROBLEMA. [...] mi marido no, y yo tampoco, quiero nombrar nombres concretos, él tiene miedo de esta gente y yo también».

La filtración expone la cruda realidad del islamoizquierdismo en Alemania: Eralp llegó a comparar el nivel de amenaza de estos militantes pro-Palestina con el del Crimen Organizado e implora abortar la publicación: «No puedo poner en peligro a mí misma y a mi familia por Der SPIEGEL. ¿Qué hacemos ahora? ¿Anulamos toda la entrevista?».

El mayor chiste de toda esta situación, sin embargo, quedó plasmado en una de las frases que Eralp sí quería publicar. En un alarde de desconexión absoluta, la candidata afirma en la entrevista: «Lo que sí puedo decir con total claridad es que, como alcaldesa gobernante, velaré por la seguridad de todas las berlinesas y todos los berlineses». Una promesa que resulta irrisoria viniendo de una dirigente que, en el mismo documento, reconoce en secreto que ni siquiera puede proteger a su propia familia de las bases de su partido.

Luego del escándalo, Eralp ha anunciado que procederá legalmente contra Der Spiegel y presentará una queja formal ante el Consejo de Prensa por haber citado sus anotaciones internas. Esta maniobra judicial evidencia de inmediato lo susceptibles y completamente desbordados que están en realidad estos cuadros dirigentes frente a situaciones de crisis.

La izquierda radical berlinesa creyó que podía capitalizar electoralmente el extremismo islámico; hoy, los documentos demuestran que es el extremismo quien los tiene de rehenes.

text:
Aave protocol will be fine.

The hacker supplied 60M USDT and borrowed 19,762 wETH (~44.9M$) in 3 minutes, before Tether froze their address and before the Aave Guardian froze the Aave V3 Core reserves (46 min later).

But USDT is real money backed by dollars, and the position is criminal but overcollateralized in the eyes of the protocol: health factor 1.04, 59.9M$ of collateral against 44.9M$ of debt.

Sure, we now have a large borrower with little incentive to repay their loan, but liquidations work as usual: if ETH goes above ~2,365$ (+4%), the position gets liquidated like any other.

The Aave V3 Core wETH reserve is 2.16M wETH, so the hacker's debt is "only" 0.9% of it as I'm writing this.

I don't think Aave needs to take specific action against the hacker.

345k wETH is available right now (81.6% utilization), so wETH liquidity is sufficient if wETH depositors want to withdraw

There's no reason or need for a bank run.

The situation is much less dire than during the Kelp hack (zero-value collateral), and we should not expect a re-run of "DeFi United".

On paper, a governance proposal could force-liquidate the hacker by upgrading the Pool to target this single position (lowering the USDT liquidation threshold would hit every USDT supplier),

but I see no real upside in doing that as normal liquidation can eat this up without sweat.

The reserves are frozen now, but no need to panic; you can repay and withdraw. This isn't the first time this has happened, and it won't be the last, and Aave is still there.

Just another day in crypto.

text:
Aave protocol will be fine.

The hacker supplied 60M USDT and borrowed 19,762 wETH (~44.9M$) in 3 minutes, before Tether froze their address and before the Aave Guardian froze the Aave V3 Core reserves (46 min later).

But USDT is real money backed by dollars, and the position is criminal but overcollateralized in the eyes of the protocol: health factor 1.04, 59.9M$ of collateral against 44.9M$ of debt.

Sure, we now have a large borrower with little incentive to repay their loan, but liquidations work as usual: if ETH goes above ~2,365$ (+4%), the position gets liquidated like any other.

The Aave V3 Core wETH reserve is 2.16M wETH, so the hacker's debt is "only" 0.9% of it as I'm writing this.

I don't think Aave needs to take specific action against the hacker.

345k wETH is available right now (81.6% utilization), so wETH liquidity is sufficient if wETH depositors want to withdraw

There's no reason or need for a bank run.

The situation is much less dire than during the Kelp hack (zero-value collateral), and we should not expect a re-run of "DeFi United".

On paper, a governance proposal could force-liquidate the hacker by upgrading the Pool to target this single position (lowering the USDT liquidation threshold would hit every USDT supplier),

but I see no real upside in doing that as normal liquidation can eat this up without sweat.

The reserves are frozen now, but no need to panic; you can repay and withdraw. This isn't the first time this has happened, and it won't be the last, and Aave is still there.

Just another day in crypto.

text:
Binance got hacked. Here's how it compares to the Bybit hack last year.

▶️ Bybit (Feb 2025)
About $1.5B was stolen, and none of it came back.
BTC dropped 4.5% that day and ETH 7.7%.
Both bounced back the next day.
Later that week they fell much further, because of tariffs and a weak market.

▶️ Binance (now)
About $5.6B left Binance. That's the biggest crypto hack ever, more than 3x Bybit.
Tether and Circle froze around $2B of it.
That still leaves over $3B stolen, including about $1.5B in BTC.
The first drop was bigger: BTC fell 3.2% and ETH 4.5% in the first hour.
Right now BTC is about 2% down and ETH about 3%.

What this tells us
The hack causes the first drop.
The big drops usually come from the wider market, not the hack itself.

What I'm watching
BTC needs to hold $77.7K.
Getting back above $80K would be a good sign.

text:
Bad news travels fast. But in an information ecosystem flooded with disinformation, getting to the truth takes work.

Add the pressure of a 24/7 news cycle, agenda-setting, disinformation campaigns, and, let’s not forget, bot farming. It’s the perfect setup for confirmation bias to thrive.

Meanwhile, control over the airwaves and social media platforms is increasingly concentrated in the hands of a few powerful players. In this environment, media and information literacy is no longer a nice-to-have. It’s a survival skill for navigating the constant stream of information competing for our attention.

This Global Media and Information Literacy Week reminds us that cultivating these skills is a shared responsibility.

For decision-makers and development practitioners, research, evidence uptake, and knowledge sharing are essential to sound policy planning and implementation. 

For digital natives, the ability to question what they see, verify sources, and distinguish fact from fiction is critical to making informed choices.

Media and information literacy won’t solve every problem in our information ecosystem, but it can help us navigate it more critically and responsibly. With a deeper understanding of how these dynamics intersect, we’d have a better shot at tackling global challenges sustainably.

This is what Covid looked like in week 1. A few countries. Small numbers. Nobody called it a crisis.

1/ South Korea: hackers used a Chinese AI tool to break into at least 7 financial firms. 68,000 people's data stolen. 16 firms breached by mid-October. This week Daishin Securities reported 38,490 customers' data leaked, bank account numbers included.

2/ Latin America: one gang ran AI agents built on Claude, Grok and Kimi against 400+ targets, banks and payment firms included. They stole passwords and got into customer bank accounts.

3/ Italy: a fake WhatsApp from "the CEO" and an AI-cloned voice got Intesa Sanpaolo's private bank to send out €95 million. €36 million is still MISSING, turned into crypto.

4/ India: small lenders lost ₹300 crore (about $31 million) in 2 months. 150 cases. Hackers copied bank logins and sent the money out as fake loans. One firm was hit twice.

5/ Crypto: $351 million drained from Bitget's hot wallets. North Korean hackers are suspected.

6/ Japan: hackers hit GMO Internet's currency trading service and demanded $50 million in crypto. The prime minister promised an emergency anti-cyberattack package.

7/ Australia: the regulator warns AI attacks put more than A$4.5 trillion in retirement savings in the firing line. Government cyber alerts jumped 80% in a year.

Now zoom out.

AI hacking tools are now easy to get. Smaller firms have weak security. The money moves in minutes. It jumps across banks, through rented accounts, out as cash or crypto. The bosses are often abroad.

Covid locked the streets. Nobody is calling this a crisis yet. But the central banks already plan for the day the hackers get in.

The G7 agreed to run drills that simulate AI attacks on banks. The ECB reportedly gave eurozone banks 4 months to hand in their defence plans.

If your savings sit in a bank, hit follow. I'm tracking where the hackers strike next and how much they take.

CRITICAL QUESTION EMERGES IN BINANCE HACK OVER HOW ATTACKERS GAINED CONTROL OF ITS WALLET

Attackers reportedly used EIP-7702 delegation to redirect Binance’s wallet to malicious code, allowing funds to be drained.

But how did they obtain authorization?

Two possibilities are being investigated: 

1) a stolen private key or 

2) a malicious authorization signature obtained through a compromised signing process.

Neither has been confirmed.

If the private key wasn’t stolen, the attack could expose a major vulnerability in how exchanges authorize transactions, rather than how they secure private keys.

🚨 CONGRESS IS NOW DISCUSSING WHAT HAPPENS IF MAJOR AI COMPANIES GO BANKRUPT.

House Democrats have introduced a resolution calling for AI companies to receive ZERO taxpayer funded bailouts if they collapse.

AI spending by Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Oracle, Meta and SpaceX is expected to top $7 trillion from 2025 to 2030, per S&P.

Big Tech is expected to borrow a record $420 billion in 2027 alone.

Now, lawmakers are discussing what should happen if those massive investments go wrong.

The resolution calls for:

• No taxpayer funded bailouts for failing AI companies.

• No emergency loans, cash injections or debt guarantees from the Fed, Treasury or FDIC.

• Failed AI companies to go through normal bankruptcy proceedings.

• Executives responsible for reckless or illegal conduct to face accountability.

• Government support to protect workers and retirement savings instead of corporate executives.

The resolution is not legally binding, and it does not mean lawmakers know an AI crash is coming.

But it shows the risk is now being taken seriously in Congress.

And there is a reason to pay attention.

AI companies are spending enormous amounts of money today based on expectations of future demand and profits.

If those expectations fail, the damage could spread beyond AI companies to banks, lenders and investors financing the expansion.

if u wanna know what crypto to hold for the next bull run, apparently all u gotta do is look at today’s reported $5.6B Binance hack

guys no wonder $ETH is Kim Jong Un’s favorite pookie 

So bullish on my ETH babies😭

but jokes aside, I’d keep a very close eye on the market over the next 72 hours. wouldn’t be surprised if we get another leg down. I’m already getting ready to DCA.

this whole thing reminds me of 2022.

remember, LUNA collapsing in May wasn’t the bottom. Celsius and 3AC blew up in June, BTC flushed to around $17.6k, and then FTX happened in November and took us down to ~$15.5k.

looking back, those were some of the best accumulation opportunities of that entire cycle. but they didn’t all happen at once.

major blowups tend to cluster around periods of forced deleveraging. when institutions are scrambling for liquidity, they sell whatever they can, not necessarily what they want to. that’s when prices can temporarily disconnect from fundamentals.

now, I don’t think it’s fair to call this FTX 2.0 just yet.

FTX was fundamentally a solvency and credit contagion crisis. so far, the Binance situation appears to be a security breach, with roughly $2.4B in stablecoins reportedly frozen and Binance saying user funds are safe.

that’s encouraging, but we still don’t know the final losses or whether there are any second-order effects. frozen funds aren’t necessarily recovered funds either.

and remember, BTC was already under pressure before the hack news broke. we’ve got a hawkish Fed, weakness in tech stocks, and a market that’s still extremely sensitive to liquidity.

the hack just added another layer of uncertainty and triggered a pretty brutal long liquidation cascade.

so over the next few days, I’m watching withdrawals, any signs of contagion, whether futures leverage gets properly flushed out, and most importantly, whether real spot demand starts absorbing the selling.

a big red candle alone doesn’t mean we’ve found the bottom. I wanna see whether the forced sellers are actually running out.

I’m not interested in catching the exact bottom or levering myself into another disaster lol. just keeping dry powder and preparing to DCA in stages if we get another proper liquidity sweep.

and please, every time something blows up in crypto, people start screaming that the entire industry is finished.

we heard enough of that shit in 2022.

the industry survived, but plenty of individual companies and tokens didn’t. there’s a difference.

anyway, I’m watching closely and getting ready to buy the fear, fam. 🥒

if u wanna know what crypto to hold for the next bull run, apparently all u gotta do is look at today’s reported $5.6B Binance hack

guys no wonder $ETH is Kim Jong Un’s favorite pookie 

So bullish on my ETH babies😭

but jokes aside, I’d keep a very close eye on the market over the next 72 hours. wouldn’t be surprised if we get another leg down. I’m already getting ready to DCA.

this whole thing reminds me of 2022.

remember, LUNA collapsing in May wasn’t the bottom. Celsius and 3AC blew up in June, BTC flushed to around $17.6k, and then FTX happened in November and took us down to ~$15.5k.

looking back, those were some of the best accumulation opportunities of that entire cycle. but they didn’t all happen at once.

major blowups tend to cluster around periods of forced deleveraging. when institutions are scrambling for liquidity, they sell whatever they can, not necessarily what they want to. that’s when prices can temporarily disconnect from fundamentals.

now, I don’t think it’s fair to call this FTX 2.0 just yet.

FTX was fundamentally a solvency and credit contagion crisis. so far, the Binance situation appears to be a security breach, with roughly $2.4B in stablecoins reportedly frozen and Binance saying user funds are safe.

that’s encouraging, but we still don’t know the final losses or whether there are any second-order effects. frozen funds aren’t necessarily recovered funds either.

and remember, BTC was already under pressure before the hack news broke. we’ve got a hawkish Fed, weakness in tech stocks, and a market that’s still extremely sensitive to liquidity.

the hack just added another layer of uncertainty and triggered a pretty brutal long liquidation cascade.

so over the next few days, I’m watching withdrawals, any signs of contagion, whether futures leverage gets properly flushed out, and most importantly, whether real spot demand starts absorbing the selling.

a big red candle alone doesn’t mean we’ve found the bottom. I wanna see whether the forced sellers are actually running out.

I’m not interested in catching the exact bottom or levering myself into another disaster lol. just keeping dry powder and preparing to DCA in stages if we get another proper liquidity sweep.

and please, every time something blows up in crypto, people start screaming that the entire industry is finished.

we heard enough of that shit in 2022.

the industry survived, but plenty of individual companies and tokens didn’t. there’s a difference.

anyway, I’m watching closely and getting ready to buy the fear, fam. 🥒

text: An important new essay by my colleague @alexolegimas  that considers not only AI's competence at task-oriented skills but also its coordination abilities.
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
I joined @GoogleDeepMind to develop a research program on the economics of AGI. Today, together with Andrew Koh (@andrewjkoh) and Shane Legg (@ShaneLegg), we are incredibly excited to release The Economics of Intelligence, the first in a series of projects from our group on how AGI will change the economy.

How do capability improvements transform the economy, and when? In this project, we define thresholds of economic capabilities, e.g., minimal AGI, based on how they transform the economy. We then track how the economy–market structure, employment, and wages–changes during the transition across capability regimes.

We have seen exponential increases in what AI agents can do but the broader economy seems almost remarkably unchanged. Part of the reason is that the solo AI agent is the wrong economic object; economic transformation is an equilibrium outcome where organizations compete. Looking at how intelligence functions within organizations, transformation will depend on when two key capability thresholds are crossed: competence (gains on individual skills, e.g., coding, math) and coordination (gains on ability of agents to cooperate and work together).

We show that what economic transformation looks like depends on whether AI becomes supercompetent, supercooperative, or both—the regime of artificial superintelligence (ASI). Tracking this transition shows why the real visible transformation may come from improvements in coordination—a capability most benchmarks don’t yet track. Past a certain threshold, AI capabilities can break the Coasian ceiling on firm size and lead to an economy that looks drastically different than the one we see today.

Two main takeaways:
1. To understand the path of transformation, we should be tracking agentic coordination more closely.
2. The impact of AI will likely show up in wages before market structure or employment.

We are really excited about this paper. Excited to hear people’s thoughts.

Link: https://t.co/9DTGSeKoSA

How the Binance hack worked:

The attacker exploited EIP-7702 - an Ethereum Pectra upgrade 

That lets a regular wallet temporarily act as a smart contract with a valid private key signature.

Hacker pre-collected 50 EIP-7702 authorizations with sequential nonces

Not knowing the exact nonce at attack time. 

Sent them all at once, only one matched. 

That was enough.

text:
多签机制（Multisig）被EIP7702降维打击了。它牺牲了用户的“容错率”，极大放大了“签名被盗”或“误签名”的破坏力。

EIP-7702以太坊硬分叉引入的新特性，本意是为了实现账户抽象（Account Abstraction）。它允许一个普通的外部账户（EOA，即普通钱包）临时授权并运行智能合约代码，从而让普通钱包在不需要转换为复杂合约钱包的情况下，具备批量转账、自动扣款等高级功能。

EIP-7702 提供了代码执行的便利，但建立这种授权连接本身，必须要有币安热钱包私钥的正式签名。

业内推测有以下三种可能性： 

•自动化签名机（Signing Server）被黑： 交易所的 hot wallet 通常由自动化系统管理。黑客可能攻破了币安的内部网络，向签名机伪造了该授权请求，系统误以为是常规操作而自动签署。
•热钱包私钥/分片直接泄露： 攻击者可能通过长期钓鱼、供应链攻击或内部合谋，直接窃取了管理热钱包的私钥或 MPC（多方计算）签名分片。
•跨链与多环境协同劫持： 由于除以太坊外，比特币和波场链上的币安钱包也遭遇了同步流出，这强烈暗示黑客拿到的不是单一链的钥匙，而是币安整个中央钱包管理系统的核心权限遭到了全面沦陷。

text:
Quick notes on 7702 to dispel fud and keep your funds safe.

First thing first -- 7702 itself isn't broken.  Don't panic if you are using a wallet that supports 7702 (MetaMask, Uniswap, Ambire, etc.).

To recap, 7702 is an account abstraction EIP that allows an EOA to sign a special message, called a "7702 authorization," that would insert a smart contract into the account, which enables the account to do powerful things like transaction batching, e.g. doing "approve" and "transfer" in one transaction so you can swap on Uniswap with one click.

But unfortunately the same feature also allows a hacker to efficiently move all your tokens in one single transaction.  In the Binance hack, the hacker moved ETH, USDT, and 62 other tokens in one transaction, whereas without 7702 they'd have had to send one transaction per token.  In this particular case, many of those transactions would've failed because Binance was still using the hacked wallet for withdrawals, so all transactions sent by the hacker would've had to compete with the legit transactions for nonces.  So using 7702 did help the hacker steal as much funds as possible, as quickly as possible.  Ouch!

However, in order for the hacker to use 7702, they must have either 1) had access to the private key, or 2) tricked Binance into signing a 7702 authorization.  The latter is very unlikely, as it's hard to imagine Binance being so incompetent as to expose an endpoint for signing 7702 authorizations or (even worse) for signing raw messages which the hacker could've repurposed for 7702 authorizations.  But I can't rule that out until the official postmortem.

What does all this mean for you?

- If you are a wallet developer, do NOT, under any circumstances, expose a way for third parties to request 7702 authorizations.  This is just handing your users a giant footgun to shoot themselves with.  No wallets I know of do this, so don't worry if you are a user.

- If you are a user, use a well-known wallet.  7702 does let wallet developers screw up in more ways than before, so use only well-known wallets whose developers' competence you can trust.

- If you are a company (e.g. an exchange) operating hot wallets, do NOT, under any circumstances, expose an endpoint (even if it's an internal endpoint) for signing 7702 authorizations or raw messages.

As a contributor to AA, I feel partially responsible for hacks like this, since by increasing the power of accounts, we've indeed also empowered hackers (not unlike how any new technology empowers both the good guys and the bad guys).  That said, it's important to note that 7702 was only a transitional EIP, and "endgame AA" such as Frame Transactions (EIP-8141) would allow wallet owners to set up their wallets much more securely.  For example, if Frame Transactions were available today, Binance could've:

- Set up their wallets as multisig contracts only (not EOAs).

- Set up "post conditions" for their `transfer()` functions, so that even if the multisig got hacked, the contract itself would perform sanity checks such as "no transfers of more than 1000 ETH without additional signers."

In short, the endgame of Ethereum UX is one with both optimal security and optimal UX, and users never have to trade off between the two.  But we still have a long way to go until we get there.  Back to work!

text:
Grok按照时间总结的这次币安被盗的全部细节，原来黑客昨晚就开始准备了：
1、准备阶段
1）10月28日：攻击者地址（标记为发起方，如 0x7c86…5ca0）从Tornado Cash分多次获得少量ETH作为gas费（约三笔0.1 ETH级别），提前布局。
2）10月29日下午至傍晚：攻击者部署专门的清扫（sweeper）合约。期间有测试/演练交易，使用自身地址验证EIP-7702委托与扫荡流程。最终清扫合约约在下午部署完成。

2、主攻击阶段（10月30日凌晨）
1）约04:20：攻击者通过EIP-7702对Binance 14热钱包提交委托授权。交易中携带了约50个连续nonce的授权签名（全部由Binance 14自身私钥签署），确保即使nonce快速变化也能命中其中一个。授权生效后，Binance 14临时/持续执行攻击者部署的清扫合约代码。

2）04:24：主扫荡开始。Binance 14在一笔交易中转出约16.7万枚ETH（约3.8–3.9亿美元）+ 约16.15亿USDT + 60多种其他代币（包括RLUSD、wBETH、UNI、ENA、PEPE、LINK、AAVE等）至新地址（接收方被Etherscan标记为Binance Hot Wallet Exploiter）。单笔规模巨大。

3）约04:24:47（24秒后）：Binance 16热钱包直接用自身私钥签名，转出约2.8万枚ETH至同一接收地址。

4）约04:39–04:41起：部分ETH被二次转移至新地址。Hot Wallet 34等通过已委托的Binance 14权限，转出约7.8亿USDC + 后续约4300万USDC。

5）后续几十分钟内：多链持续流出，包括比特币网络、波场（Tron）、Arbitrum、Optimism、Base、Avalanche等。部分山寨币开始被抛售换ETH。

3、应急响应与冻结（凌晨5点后）
1）约1小时内：Tether与Circle紧急行动。Tether累计冻结超过15.67亿USDT；Circle冻结约8.23亿USDC。合计冻结稳定币超23亿美元，后续官方核实数字约25.4亿美元（含其他稳定币如USD1等）。Ripple、World Liberty Financial等也协助冻结部分资产。

2）约05:15：
CZ发帖称“用户资金安全”“看起来确实像针对币安的黑客攻击”，感谢Tether和Circle快速冻结。

约05:29起：币安官方发文，称已注意到潜在安全问题并积极调查，用户资金完全安全，提醒警惕诈骗。随后宣布进行安全检查、暂停多链提现，直至确认环境安全。

约06:00–07:00：何一等回应，感谢相关团队协助冻结；CZ回应净损失估算“可能略高一点，但会覆盖”。

损失规模与现状（截至目前公开数据）
1）总流出：与币安标记钱包相关的资产流出约56.43亿美元（以太坊约35.28亿、比特币约14.49亿、波场约6.28亿，其他链合计约3800万）
2）冻结：稳定币冻结至少23–25.4亿美元。
3）净损失估算：扣除已冻结部分后，DefiLlama等测算约10亿美元左右（占币安托管资产约0.69%）。CZ表示可能略高，但会覆盖。用户资金被官方声明为安全，历史上SAFU也多次兜底。

其他动态：
攻击者持续抛售部分山寨币换ETH；
有地址在Aave抵押USDT借ETH；
部分热钱包委托曾持续未及时撤销，导致新进入资金可能被二次扫荡。

攻击手法总结
主流观点认为这是利用以太坊EIP-7702机制（Pectra升级后的账户委托功能）对币安热钱包进行的攻击，核心是攻击者获取了相关热钱包私钥或签名能力，而非单纯智能合约漏洞。

不是传统智能合约漏洞，而是EIP-7702委托：普通钱包通过自身私钥签名后，可临时/持续执行指定合约代码。链上证据显示授权签名来自币安热钱包自身私钥，因此主流判断是私钥被获取，或签名系统/流程被突破/欺骗（类似过往交易所签名流程被操纵的案例）。攻击者提前用Tornado Cash洗gas、部署合约、用连续nonce保护授权，手法专业。
官方尚未公布完整入侵路径。

现在看起来用户资产应该是安全的、这个量级的损失对于币安来说并不是很大，应该能完全兜底。但不得不说，AI时代加密货币面临的安全环境，会越来越严峻。攻击门槛大幅降低、事件频率上升，总体呈现“更频繁、更智能化、更系统化”的特征。

AI并没有“创造”全新的根本漏洞，而是把已有的弱点（密钥、人、运营流程、新协议功能）放大并工业化。安全环境因此变得更动态、更高频：小规模、自动化攻击更常见，高价值目标（交易所热钱包、大型协议）仍可能出现单次数亿美元级别事件（这次更是到了数十亿级别）；

当然防守方也在大规模部署AI防护，用同样的技术反击。长期看，密钥管理（多签、阈值签名、硬件安全模块）、最小权限原则、AI agent的隔离与权限控制、这些都是最关键的系统性防线。

text:
I find the possibility of reorganizing mathematics around new concepts and radically different structures fascinating.

There is already a striking example in Lean's Mathlib. When you look at how limits are formalized, the central abstraction is not the traditional epsilon–delta formulation but the more general language of filters. This is distinct from nonstandard analysis, although the motivation is related to what Terence Tao discussed in his 2007 post on ultrafilters, nonstandard analysis, and epsilon management:

https://t.co/keLxeOWNAZ

There are also more recent and ambitious examples of rethinking classical mathematical structures. One is condensed mathematics, developed by Dustin Clausen and Peter Scholze. It provides a new framework for the interplay between topology and algebra, with applications to functional analysis.

Kiran Kedlaya has written an excellent exposition of these ideas:

https://t.co/4gVsrrKZm9
author: nasqret
quoted_text:
AI may well be able to write massive software projects “from scratch”, but that almost certainly isn’t the fastest / highest performance / highest security / most token efficient way to do things. Good building blocks matter.

In addition to RL’ing the agents on final task loss, we should try to get them to regularize the building blocks as well. What would the standard library look like that makes the agents most effective?

It is likely at the limit that it turns out to be some alien organization of code, but given the existing human-bias in training, I bet that in the near term it would be lovely code that old programmers would appreciate.

I suspect the same could be said for mathematics, but that is out of my lane.

quoted_text:
币安自己的钱包往一个被黑客控制的热钱包里转了 2 亿 USDT，72 秒后，这 2 亿就被黑客扫走了，这是北京时间凌晨 5 点 42 分的一次异常。

这次被盗，我把以太坊链上的记录一笔一笔翻完了，有一笔 2 亿 USDT 的转账，我来回看了好几遍。

被控制的这个钱包叫 Binance 14，光是发出去的交易就有 1891 万笔，是币安的主力热钱包之一。

黑客用的是 EIP-7702，这是以太坊去年加的功能，普通钱包可以把执行权委托给一个合约，委托以后，合约让它转什么它就转什么。凌晨 4 点 20 分，黑客给 Binance 14 设上了委托，不到 4 分钟，一笔交易就把里面的钱扫空了。这一笔大概 25 亿，再加上后面通过它从另一个钱包转走的 8.2 亿 USDC，就是大家说的 33 亿。

可钱被扫空以后，币安的系统好像没反应过来。

用户充到币安的钱，会先进各自的充值地址，再定时归集到这种热钱包里，被盗之后这套归集还在照常跑，又进来 2199 个 ETH，黑客分三次扫走了 2198 个。

那 2 亿 USDT 是 Binance 124 补进来的，这是币安自己的钱包。好在黑客收这笔钱的地址已经被 Tether 拉黑，钱现在冻在里面。

6 点 22 分，何一发推说暂停提币。

17 分钟后，黑客又扫了 Binance 14 一次，这次拿走 128 个 ETH 和 122 种代币，换了个新地址收。

我最后一次查是 6 点 57 分，Binance 14 上的委托还挂着，指向的还是黑客的合约，币安从 6 点 55 分开始，把这个钱包里剩下的币往自己的冷钱包里转，等于在跟黑客抢剩下的那点东西。

我最注意的还是 4 点 20 分那笔交易。

里面一次塞了 50 个授权，每个都得用 Binance 14 的私钥签名，它们只是序号不一样，最后对上了 1 个，也就是说，黑客手里提前就有 50 个币安私钥签好的授权。

主扫之后 24 秒，另一个热钱包 Binance 16 用自己的私钥签了几笔转账，2.8 万个 ETH 和 5574 万 USDT，就这样直接转给了黑客。

所以我觉得黑客能让币安的私钥替他签名，问题多半出在签名系统上，等币安出了调查结果，我再拿链上记录对一遍。

稳定币能冻，ETH 现在还冻不了，所以真正跑掉的主要是 ETH，黑客光一个地址里就躺着 19.5 万个，到现在一个没动。

黑客的地址现在已经被人刷爆了，有要钱的，骂人的，刷经文的，还有发链接说黑客还要打另外 3 家交易所的，这几天肯定会混迹很多钓鱼链接，一定小心。

这些记录链上都查得到，有兴趣自己去查查。

黑客的技术也越来越成熟，这就是AI时代，交易所要跟上时代的脚步啊！！

author: wirelyss
quoted_text:
CEOs, 

Take these threats seriously.

Past $10M in revenue, you are no longer hunting. 
You are being hunted.

Protect your family, team, and company. 

Today an attacker only needs 20 seconds of your podcast audio to clone your voice and call your CFO for a wire.

Every security control that relied on "I'd recognize his voice" is dead.

At my previous company ($84M), we learned the hard way what single points of failure look like:

- 90% of our revenue ran through 1 Stripe account when a 30-day termination notice landed
- Our 1M-person email list went dark overnight
- Our website was built on depreciated code that needed to be rebuilt fast
- Austin went through a snowpocapyse where 50%+ of our team was affected (we had to send out rescue teams to deliver clean water because pipes were frozen)

Every 6 months, I make the CEOs I coach run a Black Swan Committee with one question:

"If I gave $5M to our worst enemy, how would they take us out?"

Then we lock down the protections in Notion:

Identity & Access 3 YubiKeys for the CEO (carry, home safe, off-site). 

Zero SMS 2FA on money, email, or domains. 

2 owners on every root account.

AI Fraud Defense Spoken code words for the exec team and family. 

Dual bank approval over $50K. 

No wires after 3pm Friday. 

Quarterly deepfake drills on finance, engineering, execs.

Financial Barbell 6 months opex across 2 banks. 

No payment processor over 60% of volume. 

$1M+ liquid outside the business (90% boring cash, Treasuries, and physical gold/silver across 3 locations).

Continuity & Bus File 3-2-1-1 immutable backups tested quarterly. 

Email list exported to cold storage monthly. 

72-hour incapacity clause naming an interim CEO.

30 Days of Not Needing Anyone Water, food, solar/battery, Starlink Mini, go-binder, and small bills at home so your head stays clear in a crisis. Make sure your execs are protected too. 

Growth is the Operator's job. 
Protection is the Architect's.
