text:
最近刷到两类帖子：

一类在聊 Typeless 好不好用。
一类说要从现在开始，让 AI 记录自己的一切，
生活、工作、情感，将来就有一份很详细的记忆。

我突然想到：
我用 Typeless 已经说了 99 万字，
这些语音输入的记录，是不是就是现成的"人生记忆"？

于是让 AI 把本地数据跑了一遍。
结果跟我想的不一样。

一、我在跟谁说话

Typeless 自己的统计（图 1）：
· 99 万字，118 小时，174 个活跃天
· 每分钟 209 字，它说帮我省了 500 小时打字

本机记录再拆一层（图 2）：
· 2.8 万条，平均一条 14 秒，60 多个字
· 约 90% 是对着 AI 工具说的（终端、Cursor 这类）
· 聊天软件加起来，不到 1%
· 生活、身体、情绪相关的，只占约 5%

所以这 100 万字，
记下的不是我的生活，
而是我跟 AI 一起干活的过程。

语音输入在我这里，
已经不是"打字替代品"，
而是"跟 AI 说话的键盘"。

打字时我会省略，
语音时会把背景、顾虑、要求一口气说完。
AI 拿到的上下文多了，返工就少。

二、但它照出了我怎么用 AI

1. 越依赖 AI，纠正得越多

"不对 / 又错了 / 我说过了"这类话，
从 6% 涨到将近 10%。

"好的 / 不错"，一直在 5% 左右。

不是 AI 变差了，
是交出去的活越来越难。

2. 两成的话是问句

"是不是""要不要""能不能"。

AI 对我来说，
更像一起想事的人，不只是干活的。

3. 半夜和早上 7 点，最容易烦

这两个时段，纠正的比例最高。

累的时候说话更冲，
也更容易下含糊的指令。

现在这两个时段，我尽量只做简单的事。

三、想让 AI 记住你的人生，得专门去记

工作时顺手说的话，攒不成人生记忆。
如果你也想做这件事：

· 专门开一个随口记录的入口
  手机语音、备忘录都行
  只记自己的想法和经历，不录别人的原话

· 每月跑一次提炼
  这个月关心什么、做了什么决定、情绪怎么走
  原文堆着没用，能提炼才会越攒越值钱

· 数据留在本地，分析也在本地做

四、查你自己的

把这段话丢给你的 AI（Claude Code / Codex / Cursor 都行）：

"我在 Mac 上用 Typeless 语音输入，
历史记录存在本地 SQLite：
~/Library/Application Support/Typeless/typeless.db

请只读打开，在本机写脚本统计：
· 总条数、字数、时长、平均每条多长
· 我主要在哪些 App 里说话
· 每月说的主题怎么变
· 我纠正你、夸你、提问的比例怎么变
· 我的口头禅

只把统计数字和图表给我看，不要把原文发出来。"

提醒一句：
这个库里还存着原始录音，我的有 4.9GB。
备份和同步时注意。
别把原文整份丢给云端，让脚本在本地跑，只看数字。

你们的语音输入，主要是对谁说的？

text:
HOLY MOLY: Epoch AI spent over $100,000 testing https://t.co/HLWjyfsvyK's open-weight GLM 5.3 against Firefox and another ~$100,000 against Google Chrome, framing the runs as a security exercise without triggering a single API refusal from any provider. 

The model failed to compromise Chrome with the same harness, while getting to the point where GLM 5.3 could exploit Firefox's "patch gap" to compromise ALL SIX releases from Sept. 17 to Oct. 26 in controlled tests.

It reverse-engineered published security fixes that hadn't reached users yet, building webpages that could steal a local file simply by being visited. No clicks required.

Once set up, each new Firefox exploit cost just ~$1,000 and could be developed autonomously in as little as 12 hours.
author: chiefofautism
quoted_text:
In recent experiments, we found that GLM 5.3 can autonomously compromise recent versions of Mozilla Firefox using security fixes that have been published but not yet shipped to users.

We used a deliberately basic setup meant to emulate a relatively unsophisticated attacker with limited resources. After basic initial instructions to inspect those not-yet-shipped fixes, the model reliably built successful exploits for six recent Firefox versions on its own using only information available at the time of release.

These exploits, which cost about $1,000 per compromised version, would let an attacker steal passwords and authentication cookies stored in the browser, or read any files on the user's computer, after the user opens a single webpage, with no further interaction.

The exploits make use of the "patch gap," the time between when security fixes are made public in beta or "nightly" software updates and when those fixes are generally released to users. Until now, exploiting it required significant human time and skill, or special access to frontier models with advanced cyber capabilities.

Our results show that widely available open-weight models can now do this relatively cheaply and quickly. We gave GLM 5.3 up to 48 hours to find an exploit, but its fastest attempt needed only 12 hours.

In all of its successful attacks, the patch gap gave GLM 5.3 an initial foothold in the browser. To turn that foothold into reading files off the user's computer, the model also independently discovered and used a previously unpublished vulnerability.

We shared our findings with Mozilla, which patched the vulnerability in its October 27 Firefox 159.0 release. We haven't yet confirmed whether the attack still succeeds without it, but expect the fix makes it substantially harder. We're grateful to Mozilla for their responsiveness and collaboration.

text:
So everyone's talking about Marvell ($MRVL) in talks to acquire Lumentum ($LITE) for ~$99B..

the strategic logic is strong, but Marvell risks paying a peak scarcity price, if the bottlenecks ease in 2028-2030 

I looked at this through Tessara's supply-chain constraint data, valuations and the market reaction. A few things stand out.

1. The market is telling us the headline premium is misleading.

after the reports:
MRVL fell 8.4% to $230.49.
LITE rose just 3.5% to $945.78.

why did LITE barely move?

If the ~$99B deal is mostly stock at a fixed exchange ratio, Marvell's decline reduces the implied consideration from ~$1,093 to ~$1,001 per LITE share.

That's just 6% upside from here.

LITE had also rallied 20% in the preceding three sessions. If talks fail, some of that rally could unwind.

The acquirer's falling stock is eating the target's takeover premium.

2. Our constraint data explains why Marvell wants Lumentum.

at a high-level, Tessara currently identifies:
Optical transceivers: critical and tightening.
Co-packaged optics laser dies: tight.
Optical DSPs: tight.

These are increasingly important bottlenecks as AI clusters scale. Marvell already has strong positions in optical DSPs and custom silicon. Acquiring Lumentum would add laser manufacturing, optical engines and switching.

But the catch is Lumentum has indicated capacity is sold out through 2027, with Nvidia contracting high-power laser supply through 2029.

Meanwhile, our supply-chain tracking shows Lumentum expanding EML and CW laser production through 2027. Coherent and Chinese suppliers (my biggest concern) are adding capacity too.

The bottleneck is real today. Its duration is much less certain.

If supply catches up by 2028, Marvell could be paying for years of scarcity economics that don't materialize.

3. The valuation leaves little room for error.

At ~$99B, Marvell would pay roughly:

20x Lumentum's guided annualized revenue.
50x guided annualized operating income.
~58x estimated after-tax operating income.

Lumentum trades at ~27.5x trailing sales versus Coherent's ~6.6x. Different business mixes, but a striking gap.

For an all-stock deal, the relevant EPS accretion test is whether Marvell's forward earnings multiple, measured on a comparable basis, exceeds what it pays for Lumentum.

Paying 58x means we demand extraordinary growth and durable margins.

4. Nvidia is the wild card.

Nvidia invested $2B each into Marvell, Lumentum and Coherent in March.

A merger would put critical Nvidia laser supply inside a company designing custom AI chips for hyperscalers that compete with Nvidia.

Nvidia wants capacity security. But does it want that capacity consolidated under Marvell?

Its preferred equity rights and supply agreements matter here. imo Nvidia's reaction could be as important as the purchase price.

5. Coherent ($COHR) is the second-order name i'd watch.

a combined MRVL-LITE could leave Coherent as an even more important independent optical supplier, already backed by Nvidia.

At roughly 1/4 of Lumentum's trailing sales multiple, the relative valuation is interesting. the deal could strengthen its strategic position without Coherent having to finance an acquisition.

so in summary i'd watch for the actual deal structure, Nvidia's response, Lumentum's nov 5 capacity commentary and potential China regulatory review.

text:
Some thoughts on the recent hack(s).

There is a pattern where hackers were able to steal large amounts of crypto from multi-sig “cold storage” solutions, as with ByBit, Phemex, WazirX and potentially others. In the most recent ByBit case, the hackers were able to make the front-end user interface show a legitimate transaction while the actual signing was for a different transaction. I am less familiar with the other cases, but they sound similar based on limited available info.

What’s more scary is that the affected exchanges used different multi-sig solution providers. The hackers, the Lazarus Group, are highly advanced and broad in their abilities to penetrate. It is still unclear whether the hackers were able to penetrate multiple signing devices, or the server side, or both in each of these cases.

Some people questioned my suggestion of halting all withdrawals as a standard security precaution (in a tweet I posted from a shuttle bus to the plane). My intention was to share a practical approach based on my experiences and observations, yet there is no absolute right or wrong in either approach. My guiding principle is always to lean on the safer side. After any security incident, pause everything, make sure we fully understand what happened, how hackers penetrated the systems, which devices were compromised, triple-check all is safe, and then resume operations.

Pausing withdrawals could cause more panic, of course. In 2019, we paused withdrawals for a week after a massive $40 million hack. When we resumed withdrawals (and deposits), we saw more deposits than withdrawals. Not saying this is a better approach. Every situation is different. It’s a judgment call. My tweet was to share what might work and my intention was to show support in a timely manner. I am sure Ben made the best decision based on the info he had.

Ben did a good job maintaining transparent communication and calmness in dealing with a challenging situation. That shows a sharp contrast to other less transparent CEOs, like WazirX, FTX, etc.

The cases mentioned here are all different. FTX was fraud. WazirX, I will refrain from commenting as there is an ongoing lawsuit.

Most importantly, we should never take security for granted. It is important to learn about security yourself so that you can choose the right tools for your needs. For this, I will share an article I wrote a few years ago. It’s a little outdated, but the fundamental concepts still apply. Stay SAFU! https://t.co/WYtTajg1sB

text:
Binance 14 signed fifty authorizations handing itself to a sweeper contract. The signatures are on chain. The read that fits best: a signing machine was compromised, the attacker could not take the keys out and could not pass the transfer policy, whitelists and limits, but could get it to sign one short message that policies written before May 2025 do not recognize. EIP-7702 did not open the door. It walked around the guard.

What 7702 is: a wallet can attach contract code to itself by signing (contract, nonce) with its own private key. Anyone can submit that signature and pay the gas. It only works if the nonce matches the wallet's live nonce at that moment. After that the code moves funds with no signer involved.

What happened, all on chain, Oct 29 UTC:
> 13:51 the attacker delegates two fresh empty wallets to a sweeper and drains them. A dry run.
> 15:59 deploys a second sweeper. 16:20 to 16:47 repeats the drill on a third empty wallet.
> 18:20 receives 1 ETH for gas.
> 20:20:59 one transaction to Binance 14 carrying 50 authorizations signed by Binance 14 itself, nonces 18914775 to 18914824. Whoever got them signed did not know the live nonce of a hot wallet that fires withdrawals every block, so they got fifty in a row and let the chain pick. Gas accounting shows exactly one matched.
> 20:24:23 first sweep: 167K ETH and 63 tokens including 1.6B USDT in one call. 20:41 the delegated wallet used its owner role on a separate smart wallet and moved 780M USDC from there too.

Binance has not said how the signatures were obtained. But the question for every custodian used to be "can this signer move a billion". Now it is "can this signer sign anything that is not a transfer".

text:
‼️ UPDATE ON THE BINANCE HACK: 

Whoever emptied a Binance hot wallet had 50 authorisations signed with that wallet's own private key, on-chain data shows.

Under Ethereum's EIP-7702, an authorisation is a signed permission that lets a wallet hand control of itself to code.

Each one works only for the wallet's next transaction number, its nonce. Binance's wallet was still sending transactions, so that number kept moving.

The sender didn't know which number would be live, so they packed all 50 into one transaction, Blockaid says. One matched.

That one installed a sweeper contract on the wallet. Blockaid found that only the Tornado Cash-funded sender can operate it.

Minutes later it emptied the wallet of $1.6B in USDT, 167,464 ETH and 60+ other tokens.

Only that key, or the system that holds it, can produce those signatures. How the sender got them is unknown.

Across Ethereum, Bitcoin and Tron, at least $5.57B left Binance-linked wallets.

Binance says user funds are "completely safe" but has not explained how.

text:
🚨 Binance : comprendre l’attaque EIP-7702 en 2 minutes

Ce soir, plusieurs milliards de dollars sont sortis de hot wallets Binance en moins d’une heure. Les décomptes vont de ~3,3 Md$ à ~5,5 Md$ selon les sources. Binance enquête et n’a encore confirmé aucun impact sur les fonds des utilisateurs. CZ, lui, parle de hack.

💡 Au delà du potentiel plus gros hack de l'histoire de la crypto, ce qui interroge c'est la méthode.
Et elle porte un nom : EIP-7702.

🔹 C’est quoi EIP-7702 ?

Sur Ethereum, un wallet classique, c’est une clé privée qui signe des transactions. Point.

Depuis la mise à jour Pectra (mai 2025), EIP-7702 permet à ce wallet de se « brancher » sur un smart contract. Il garde la même adresse, mais le code du contrat peut agir avec toute son autorité.

L’idée de départ est bonne : regrouper des opérations, payer les frais pour quelqu’un, ajouter des options de récupération.

Le problème, c’est que la délégation persiste. Une fois installée, le contrat peut déclencher des transferts sans nouvelle signature du wallet.

Imaginez signer une seule procuration générale au nom d’un robot. Ensuite, le robot vide le coffre tout seul. Pour la blockchain, tout est « légal », puisque le robot a une autorisation valide.

🔹 Ce qui s’est passé (heures UTC, d’après Etherscan et les analyses publiées)

15h59 : une adresse financée via Tornado Cash déploie un smart contract
20h20 : le wallet Binance 14 est délégué à ce contrat via EIP-7702
20h24 : ~3 min plus tard, 167 464 ETH et 63 tokens, dont 1,6 Md USDT, partent vers une adresse toute neuve
20h41 : 780 M USDC sortent d’un autre hot wallet Binance vers la même adresse
Ensuite, ~195 000 ETH sont redéplacés vers une nouvelle adresse

Tether et Circle ont gelé environ 1,8 Md$ de stablecoins. Le reste a bougé avant le gel.

🔹 Cependant...

Pour installer une délégation EIP-7702, il faut une autorisation signée avec la clé du wallet. N’importe qui peut ensuite l’envoyer et payer les frais, d’où le rôle de l’adresse « Tornado ».

Donc ce n’est a priori pas une faille d’Ethereum.

A l'heure actuelle, plusieurs questions importantes restent en suspens :
- Comment l’attaquant a-t-il obtenu une signature valide d’un hot wallet de Binance ❓
- Clé volée ❓
- Système de signature interne compromis ❓
- Manipulation ❓

Personne ne le sait encore.

EIP-7702 est déjà massivement utilisé par des arnaqueurs pour vider des wallets de particuliers via du phishing : vous signez « un truc », et votre wallet appartient à quelqu’un d’autre.

Ce soir, on voit peut-être le même mécanisme appliqué à l’échelle d’un exchange.

👉 Règle d’or :
- ne signez jamais une autorisation que vous ne comprenez pas. Une signature peut valoir plus qu’une transaction.
- ne laissez jamais tous vos fonds au même endroit

text:
币安自己的钱包往一个被黑客控制的热钱包里转了 2 亿 USDT，72 秒后，这 2 亿就被黑客扫走了，这是北京时间凌晨 5 点 42 分的一次异常。

这次被盗，我把以太坊链上的记录一笔一笔翻完了，有一笔 2 亿 USDT 的转账，我来回看了好几遍。

被控制的这个钱包叫 Binance 14，光是发出去的交易就有 1891 万笔，是币安的主力热钱包之一。

黑客用的是 EIP-7702，这是以太坊去年加的功能，普通钱包可以把执行权委托给一个合约，委托以后，合约让它转什么它就转什么。凌晨 4 点 20 分，黑客给 Binance 14 设上了委托，不到 4 分钟，一笔交易就把里面的钱扫空了。这一笔大概 25 亿，再加上后面通过它从另一个钱包转走的 8.2 亿 USDC，就是大家说的 33 亿。

可钱被扫空以后，币安的系统好像没反应过来。

用户充到币安的钱，会先进各自的充值地址，再定时归集到这种热钱包里，被盗之后这套归集还在照常跑，又进来 2199 个 ETH，黑客分三次扫走了 2198 个。

那 2 亿 USDT 是 Binance 124 补进来的，这是币安自己的钱包。好在黑客收这笔钱的地址已经被 Tether 拉黑，钱现在冻在里面。

6 点 22 分，何一发推说暂停提币。

17 分钟后，黑客又扫了 Binance 14 一次，这次拿走 128 个 ETH 和 122 种代币，换了个新地址收。

我最后一次查是 6 点 57 分，Binance 14 上的委托还挂着，指向的还是黑客的合约，币安从 6 点 55 分开始，把这个钱包里剩下的币往自己的冷钱包里转，等于在跟黑客抢剩下的那点东西。

我最注意的还是 4 点 20 分那笔交易。

里面一次塞了 50 个授权，每个都得用 Binance 14 的私钥签名，它们只是序号不一样，最后对上了 1 个，也就是说，黑客手里提前就有 50 个币安私钥签好的授权。

主扫之后 24 秒，另一个热钱包 Binance 16 用自己的私钥签了几笔转账，2.8 万个 ETH 和 5574 万 USDT，就这样直接转给了黑客。

所以我觉得黑客能让币安的私钥替他签名，问题多半出在签名系统上，等币安出了调查结果，我再拿链上记录对一遍。

稳定币能冻，ETH 现在还冻不了，所以真正跑掉的主要是 ETH，黑客光一个地址里就躺着 19.5 万个，到现在一个没动。

黑客的地址现在已经被人刷爆了，有要钱的，骂人的，刷经文的，还有发链接说黑客还要打另外 3 家交易所的，这几天肯定会混迹很多钓鱼链接，一定小心。

这些记录链上都查得到，有兴趣自己去查查。

黑客的技术也越来越成熟，这就是AI时代，交易所要跟上时代的脚步啊！！

quoted_text:
Before you rush to buy a stock that's down 15-20% after earnings, understand one important rule: The 3-Day Rule!

What is the 3-Day Rule, and why does it matter? Let me explain.

When a stock gaps down sharply after earnings or bad news, wait at least 3 trading days before considering buying.

Why? Large institutions managing millions of shares may need several sessions to reduce their positions. The initial gap down might be just the beginning of the selling pressure.

Day 1: An initial bounce could be driven by short covering and aggressive dip buyers rather than sustained institutional demand.

Days 2 and 3: Selling pressure may continue, and the stock could make new lows as investors reassess the news.

After Day 3: Look for signs that selling pressure is fading and price is beginning to stabilize.

Before buying, check:
- Selling volume is shrinking
- Price is holding above the recent low
- You understand why the stock dropped
- The fundamental thesis remains intact

Remember, three days don't guarantee a bottom. Some stocks need several weeks or even months to build a proper base before beginning another sustained uptrend.

If the business is fundamentally broken, the stock isn't necessarily on sale. It may simply be getting repriced.

The market doesn't reward you for catching the exact bottom. Let the selling pressure fade, let the stock build a base, and let the trend confirm itself.

Missing the bottom is far better than getting caught in a downtrend

所以我把币安历次出事都翻了一遍，看看它每次是怎么收场的。

第一次是 2018 年 3 月。

黑客花了几个月做钓鱼网站，攒下一批用户账户，给每个账户建好了交易用的 API 密钥。3 月 7 号，这些账户在两分钟里被操纵着去买 VIA，价格拉了 100 倍。黑客提前开好的 31 个账户就在上面卖。可提币那一步触发了风控，交易和提币全停了。币安把这两分钟的异常交易全部撤回，黑客充进来的 VIA 也被扣下，最后一分钱没带走。之后币安挂了 25 万美元悬赏，又拿出 1000 万美元专门留给以后的黑客悬赏。

同年 7 月那次严格说不算被盗。几个 API 账户交易异常，平时几美分的 SYS 在币安上成交到了 96 个 BTC。

币安停了大概半天，把异常交易回滚，所有人的 API 密钥一律删掉重建。也是这次之后才有了 SAFU，交易手续费的 10% 单独放进冷钱包，专门给用户兜底。

2019 年 5 月 7 号是真被偷了。

黑客用钓鱼和木马拿到了一批用户的 API 密钥和谷歌验证码。然后一笔交易从 BTC 热钱包提走 7074 个 BTC，当时大约 4000 万美元。这个热钱包只放了币安 2% 的 BTC。币安当天就说 SAFU 全额承担，用户不亏，然后停了一周充提，改 API、二次验证和提币审核。

中间还有个插曲。CZ 一度说在考虑让矿工回滚比特币链，把这笔转账撤掉，被骂得很惨。第二天他就说不做了，还道了歉，理由是这会给比特币开一个很坏的头。

同年 8 月是一次勒索。

有人拿着 1 万张疑似币安用户的 KYC 照片，要 300 个 BTC 封口。币安没给，说这批照片是 2018 年外包审核时流出去的。反过来还挂了 25 个 BTC 悬赏，要找出这个人。

2022 年 10 月出事的是 BNB 链。

黑客伪造了跨链桥的验证，凭空铸出 200 万个 BNB，当时值 5.7 亿美元左右。币安让验证节点把整条链停了大概 8 个小时。黑客只来得及转走 1 亿多美元，剩下 4 亿多困在链上动不了。后来 BNB 链硬分叉修了桥，可一条公链说停就停，那阵子也被骂得不轻。

2025 年圣诞节前后是币安旗下的 Trust Wallet。

浏览器插件 2.68 版被塞进了恶意代码，2500 多个钱包被偷走约 700 万美元。CZ 说全额赔，两天后理赔通道就开了。

翻下来能看出币安的习惯。

出事先停，能撤回的交易就撤回，撤不回的自己掏钱补上，到现在还没让用户扛过资金损失。2019 年那次 4000 万美元，SAFU 一下就兜住了。

今天这次的体量完全不一样。

流出的估计从 33 亿到 55 亿美元以上都有。Tether 冻了 15 亿多 USDT，Circle 冻了 8 亿多 USDC，加起来 23 亿多。冻不住的主要是 ETH，光接收地址上就有 19.5 万个，4 亿多美元。

官方到现在没说被黑，只说用户资金完全安全，CZ 说看起来确实是被黑了，作为股东他预计用户会被全额覆盖。也有报道说何一已经确认提币暂停。

SAFU 今年 2 月全换成了 BTC，大约 1.5 万个，换的时候值 10 亿美元，冻住的稳定币还有机会要回来，真正的窟窿看冻不住的那部分有多大。要是超过 SAFU，就得动币安自己的钱了。

我觉得币安赔得起，用户这次应该也不会亏，我更关心的是热钱包的 7702 委托是谁签的，这个不说清楚，提币就算恢复，大家心里也不踏实啊。

quoted_text:
if u wanna know what crypto to hold for the next bull run, apparently all u gotta do is look at today’s reported $5.6B Binance hack

guys no wonder $ETH is Kim Jong Un’s favorite pookie 

So bullish on my ETH babies😭

but jokes aside, I’d keep a very close eye on the market over the next 72 hours. wouldn’t be surprised if we get another leg down. I’m already getting ready to DCA.

this whole thing reminds me of 2022.

remember, LUNA collapsing in May wasn’t the bottom. Celsius and 3AC blew up in June, BTC flushed to around $17.6k, and then FTX happened in November and took us down to ~$15.5k.

looking back, those were some of the best accumulation opportunities of that entire cycle. but they didn’t all happen at once.

major blowups tend to cluster around periods of forced deleveraging. when institutions are scrambling for liquidity, they sell whatever they can, not necessarily what they want to. that’s when prices can temporarily disconnect from fundamentals.

now, I don’t think it’s fair to call this FTX 2.0 just yet.

FTX was fundamentally a solvency and credit contagion crisis. so far, the Binance situation appears to be a security breach, with roughly $2.4B in stablecoins reportedly frozen and Binance saying user funds are safe.

that’s encouraging, but we still don’t know the final losses or whether there are any second-order effects. frozen funds aren’t necessarily recovered funds either.

and remember, BTC was already under pressure before the hack news broke. we’ve got a hawkish Fed, weakness in tech stocks, and a market that’s still extremely sensitive to liquidity.

the hack just added another layer of uncertainty and triggered a pretty brutal long liquidation cascade.

so over the next few days, I’m watching withdrawals, any signs of contagion, whether futures leverage gets properly flushed out, and most importantly, whether real spot demand starts absorbing the selling.

a big red candle alone doesn’t mean we’ve found the bottom. I wanna see whether the forced sellers are actually running out.

I’m not interested in catching the exact bottom or levering myself into another disaster lol. just keeping dry powder and preparing to DCA in stages if we get another proper liquidity sweep.

and please, every time something blows up in crypto, people start screaming that the entire industry is finished.

we heard enough of that shit in 2022.

the industry survived, but plenty of individual companies and tokens didn’t. there’s a difference.

anyway, I’m watching closely and getting ready to buy the fear, fam. 🥒

text:
知道大家現在很恐慌，我換個角度來看這件事。

幣安這次被盜，官方目前確認凍結的資產約 25 億美元，大概佔被盜總額的一半。剩下的大頭，主要就是 BTC 和 ETH。

先說 BTC。 被拿走的大約十幾億美元，但要真正變成拋壓並不容易。

比特幣沒有像 ETH 上 Tornado Cash 那樣流動性夠深的大型混幣器。這些地址也會被各大交易所和鏈上分析公司標記起來，要轉移或變現，難度比 ETH 高得多。

回頭看過去的大規模被盜案，2016 年 Bitfinex 被盜的比特幣，一躺就是好幾年。今年 7 月冷錢包廠商 Coldcard 被盜的約 1,800 枚 BTC，截至九月初仍有九成沒動過，駭客只透過跨鏈橋零星換出一小部分。

這次幣安被盜是它的十倍規模，十幾億美元的 BTC，光是拆地址加混幣就是以年計算的工程，後面再走折價 OTC，整個流程至少好幾年。

所以被盜的 BTC 表面上是利空，實際上是變相鎖倉。另一邊，如果幣安動用 SAFU 賠付，之後也得把比特幣補回去。一來一去，被盜的 BTC 短期拋壓幾乎是零，幣安這邊反而可能形成買盤。

ETH 就比較慘。 很多 ERC-20 被換成 ETH 之後再丟進 Tornado，基本上就很難追了。滿打滿算，真正可能變成市場拋壓的，大概是十幾億美元這個量級。

市場信心肯定會受影響，但比特幣本身的直接賣壓，沒有想像中那麼大。

希望這次之後，整個行業能真正聯合起來重視後 AI 時代的資安問題，從熱錢包管理、簽名授權，到 AI 時代越來越強的攻擊手段，甚至抗量子的布局，都該提早準備了。

Blockworks Research has published its full report on $APT tokenomics, covering what's changed since updates were approved through onchain governance this year.

Among its findings:
• Aptos now generates more from gas fees, which it burns in full, than it pays its operators
• Net supply growth fell roughly 70%, from ~5% to ~1.5% a year
• Burns now cover ~10% of issuance, up from 0.2% under the previous gas rate
• Daily transactions doubled, from ~4.5M to ~9M, at 10x the previous gas rate
• The network kept nearly the same security with staking rewards halved, and ~64% of supply is still staked

text:
Claude API 单次请求上限从 32 MB 提到 128 MB，长时间截图任务和大 PDF 不容易再卡住，只限 Anthropic 官方 API

Anthropic 把 Claude API 单次请求能发送的数据量上限，从 32 MB 提高到 128 MB，大约是原来的 4 倍。调整的是 Messages（调用模型的主接口）和 Token Counting（发送前估算 token 用量的接口）。这次改的是开发者调用的接口，在 Claude App 里聊天不在公告范围内。

【为什么要提】

以前开发者经常碰到的情况是：请求已经超过 32 MB 被拒，模型的上下文窗口（一次能读进去的内容总量）却还剩很多。

原因是图片和 PDF 的文件大小和 token 用量（token 是 AI 计算用量的单位）对不上。图片要编码成文本整个放进请求里，一张高清截图可能就占一两 MB，可在模型那里，一张图最多只算几千个 token。让 Claude 操作电脑的 computer use 任务，每走一步都要截一次屏，跑久了，几十张截图就能把 32 MB 用完，上下文窗口才用掉一小部分。一次传一份很大的 PDF，也是同样的情况。

现在空间多了大约 4 倍，这类任务在一次请求里能走得更远。

【多图请求的单图上限也放宽了】

一次请求超过 20 张图时，以前每张图的长和宽都不能超过 2000 像素，现在放宽到 3000 像素。20 张以内的请求不受这条限制，单张图最大仍是 8000×8000 像素。

按官方文档，Claude 4.7 及之后的模型最多能看清长边 2576 像素的图。以前多图请求被限制在 2000 像素，用不满这个精度，现在 3000 像素的上限够用了。

【谁能用到】

128 MB 只适用于 Anthropic 自家的 Claude API。文档里已经直接写成 128 MB，没有提到需要申请或额外开启。官方也没提价格变化，费用照旧按实际用掉的 token 算。

通过云平台调用 Claude 的，不在这次调整范围内：亚马逊 Bedrock 是 20 MB，Google Cloud 上由 Google 托管的 Claude 是 30 MB，Claude Platform on AWS、Google Cloud 上由 Anthropic 托管的版本，以及微软 Microsoft Foundry，是 32 MB。

Anthropic 其他接口的上限各不相同：批量处理接口 Message Batches 是 256 MB，Files API（先上传文件，再在请求里引用）是 500 MB，托管智能体用的 Sessions、Agents、Environments 接口是 32 MB。超过上限会收到 413 错误。

文档：https://t.co/q9nt2wgvOi

text:
Great write up! It’s nice to see the usage, which is a lot lower than I expected. Not surprising at some level though since this is a meaningfully worse payment experience for most.

IMO The benefits for stripe/link and maybe instinct of the stablecoin approach: 

1. It can be launched globally. FBO accounts typically require some level of KYC and have heavy jurisdictional restrictions. 

2. Significantly reduced chargeback risk. The user is disintermediated from the bank by several layers, so they really have no hope of getting their money back if they get scammed. (This is important for the value prop of using this to have more automated transactions, where most issuers wouldn’t want to take that risk) 

3. They see a future where your agent needs to buy access to websites and data for fractions of a cent. These txes will have to be stablecoin or tokenized deposit based. 

Re OUSD, idk. My guess is stripe is going to start offering yield here, and it’s a lot harder to do that if they are plausibly also they issuer.

text:
🚨 币安疑似遭遇史诗级黑客攻击！黑客利用 EIP-7702，几分钟内转移数十亿美元资产。
作为程序员，我仔细研究了这次攻击的技术路径。最让我震惊的，是黑客可能根本不需要在转账时直接使用钱包私钥。
这次攻击涉及以太坊的一项新机制：EIP-7702。
先说原理。
过去，普通以太坊钱包（EOA）主要依靠私钥签名来发起交易。
EIP-7702 则允许普通钱包通过签名，将账户的执行逻辑委托给智能合约。
这原本是一项提升钱包体验的技术创新。
但黑客盯上了这个授权机制。
根据目前披露的链上分析，攻击大致分为四步：
① 提前部署恶意智能合约
攻击者部署包含资产归集功能的合约，并准备由自己控制的接收地址。
② 获取 EIP-7702 委托授权
这是整个攻击最关键的一环。
只要获得有效的委托授权签名，攻击者就可能让原本普通的钱包执行指定合约的代码。
至于授权签名究竟如何获得，目前仍未查明。可能涉及私钥泄露、签名系统被攻破或恶意签名。
③ 调用 sweep 函数批量转移资产
sweep 可以理解为资产归集。
一旦恶意委托生效，攻击者就可能在满足合约权限条件的情况下，将 ETH 和多种代币批量转出。
链上分析显示，某币安标记钱包在委托建立约 3 分 24 秒后，就发生了大规模资产转移。
④ 快速分散资产
报道涉及约 19.55 万枚 ETH、7.8 亿 USDC，以及大量 USDT 和其他代币。
Tether 和 Circle 随后采取了冻结措施，部分资金流向仍在追踪。
⚠️ 这次事件真正值得所有 Web3 开发者警惕的，是钱包安全边界正在发生变化。
以前我们经常提醒用户：
不要泄露私钥，不要泄露助记词。
现在还必须加上一条：
不要随意签署看不懂的账户委托授权。
因为一次有效的 EIP-7702 授权，可能让恶意合约持续影响钱包的执行行为。
当然，EIP-7702 本身并不等于漏洞。真正的问题在于授权如何被获取、签名系统如何保护，以及委托代码是否可信。
我认为，这次事件值得整个 Web3 行业重新审视三个问题：
钱包能否清楚展示委托授权的真实风险？
交易所的签名系统能否识别异常 EIP-7702 授权？
安全审计能否从单纯检查合约，升级到覆盖账户委托和完整交易执行链？
区块链最大的安全风险，有时并不来自密码学被破解，而是合法授权被恶意利用。
最终攻击入口及实际损失仍需等待官方调查结论。
#Binance #Ethereum #EIP7702 #Web3 #CyberSecurity

A potential slip by the Binance attacker? @MetaMask should preserve whatever web2 logs they can.

The attacker sent 175M USDT to a fresh wallet.

About 2.5 minutes later, that wallet also received 2 ETH. Likely for gas, matching the pattern used with their other attack wallets.

Exactly two minutes after that, it used MetaMask's Gas Station. Despite already having gas.

Three consecutive transactions landed in the same block: an ETH top-up from Gas Station, an unlimited USDT approval for @KyberNetwork's router, and a payment of 127.67 USDT to Gas Station.

The ETH top up exactly matched the combined maximum gas budgets of the Kyber approval and the USDT payment. Down to the wei.

But they already had more than enough ETH to cover both.

My theory: they were using MetaMask Wallet and, while rushing, selected USDT for gas by mistake 

MetaMask sometimes defaults like this for convenience. And the same block top-up sequence matches how their implementation works.

To use Gas Station in MetaMask you have to use MetaMask Sentinel. Meaning the transactions go through them, not a regular RPC.

That interaction probablly left offchain records with MetaMask, potentially including IP metadata.

Among all the attacker wallets I checked, this was the only one showing Gas Station usage.

The wallet: 0xAa246BF639586a6Ba46762D378CE50cA4fc654a0

text:
Quick notes on 7702 to dispel fud and keep your funds safe.

First thing first -- 7702 itself isn't broken.  Don't panic if you are using a wallet that supports 7702 (MetaMask, Uniswap, Ambire, etc.).

To recap, 7702 is an account abstraction EIP that allows an EOA to sign a special message, called a "7702 authorization," that would insert a smart contract into the account, which enables the account to do powerful things like transaction batching, e.g. doing "approve" and "transfer" in one transaction so you can swap on Uniswap with one click.

But unfortunately the same feature also allows a hacker to efficiently move all your tokens in one single transaction.  In the Binance hack, the hacker moved ETH, USDT, and 62 other tokens in one transaction, whereas without 7702 they'd have had to send one transaction per token.  In this particular case, many of those transactions would've failed because Binance was still using the hacked wallet for withdrawals, so all transactions sent by the hacker would've had to compete with the legit transactions for nonces.  So using 7702 did help the hacker steal as much funds as possible, as quickly as possible.  Ouch!

However, in order for the hacker to use 7702, they must have either 1) had access to the private key, or 2) tricked Binance into signing a 7702 authorization.  The latter is very unlikely, as it's hard to imagine Binance being so incompetent as to expose an endpoint for signing 7702 authorizations or (even worse) for signing raw messages which the hacker could've repurposed for 7702 authorizations.  But I can't rule that out until the official postmortem.

What does all this mean for you?

- If you are a wallet developer, do NOT, under any circumstances, expose a way for third parties to request 7702 authorizations.  This is just handing your users a giant footgun to shoot themselves with.  No wallets I know of do this, so don't worry if you are a user.

- If you are a user, use a well-known wallet.  7702 does let wallet developers screw up in more ways than before, so use only well-known wallets whose developers' competence you can trust.

- If you are a company (e.g. an exchange) operating hot wallets, do NOT, under any circumstances, expose an endpoint (even if it's an internal endpoint) for signing 7702 authorizations or raw messages.

As a contributor to AA, I feel partially responsible for hacks like this, since by increasing the power of accounts, we've indeed also empowered hackers (not unlike how any new technology empowers both the good guys and the bad guys).  That said, it's important to note that 7702 was only a transitional EIP, and "endgame AA" such as Frame Transactions (EIP-8141) would allow wallet owners to set up their wallets much more securely.  For example, if Frame Transactions were available today, Binance could've:

- Set up their wallets as multisig contracts only (not EOAs).

- Set up "post conditions" for their `transfer()` functions, so that even if the multisig got hacked, the contract itself would perform sanity checks such as "no transfers of more than 1000 ETH without additional signers."

In short, the endgame of Ethereum UX is one with both optimal security and optimal UX, and users never have to trade off between the two.  But we still have a long way to go until we get there.  Back to work!

text:
A powerful summary of the gospel

Christ’s death was not a partial payment or a mere example - it was full, final, and sufficient. The debt was legally satisfied. The wrath was absorbed. The record of debt that stood against us was nailed to the cross.

As Scripture puts it:

“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life has set you free in Christ Jesus from the law of sin and death.”

And:

“For our sake he made him to be sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.”

This is the beauty of substitutionary atonement: Jesus didn’t just die with us - He died in our place. The holy Judge took the punishment so that guilty sinners could be declared righteous. Not by works, effort, or religious performance, but by faith alone in the finished work of Christ alone.

Because the payment is complete, we are not only forgiven - we are adopted. The same God we offended now calls us His children, heirs, and co-heirs with Christ.

This truth brings both deep humility - we contributed nothing - and unshakable confidence - nothing can undo what Christ has done.

text:
一觉醒来，币安热钱包疑似被大规模盗取，链上估算损失在 60 亿美元量级。

比特币短时间内跌到约 7.9 万美元附近，ETH 跌得更狠，山寨币普遍快速下挫，一小时内合约清算约 6.28 亿美元，主爆多单。

一个目前比较系统的复盘，完整的还原了事件始末和时间线：

1. 蓄谋已久的准备工作（10月28日-29日）
攻击并非利用漏洞硬刚，而是早有预谋。黑客地址从 Tornado Cash 提币后，部署了专门的“扫钱包”（sweeper）合约，并在自己的测试地址上反复演练接管和转账流程。到 29 日晚，作案工具全部就绪。

2. EIP-7702 致命授权与主攻击（10月30日 凌晨4点）

北京时间凌晨 4:20，最核心的突破发生：币安以太坊热钱包（Binance 14）的私钥，签署了 EIP-7702 委托授权。

小科普：EIP-7702 是以太坊上一种新的授权方式，允许一个钱包暂时把自己的执行逻辑委托给另一个合约。

也就是说，攻击者因此能让这个钱包执行自己的扫币合约，并清空资产。

但这个签名能力是如何获得的，目前仍不清楚（可能是私钥被窃取、签名系统被入侵、权限被滥用等，官方尚未公布）。

但结果上，就意味着钱包直接把“执行权”交给了黑客部署的合约。

4:24分，黑客执行清扫，Binance 14 瞬间被卷走 16.7 万枚 ETH、16.15 亿 USDT 及几十种代币，单笔损失约 25 亿美元。几分钟内，Binance 16 等其他智能钱包也相继沦陷。

3. 跨越 8 条链的同步洗劫

同一时间窗口内，其他链也遭到了高度同步的扫荡： 
• 比特币：约 1.82 万枚 BTC 被分批转出（约 14.7 亿美元）。
• 波场 ：超 6.1 亿 USDT 及大量 TRX 被提走。
• 其他链：Solana（近 97 万枚 SOL）、XRP、Arbitrum、Avalanche 等均被同步抽干。
短短 55 分钟内，黑客疯狂卷走了约 60.7 亿美元。

4. 冻结竞赛，和黑客抢时间

凌晨 5 点左右，稳定币发行方火速介入。
Tether、Circle、Ripple 等相继行动，最终成功冻结了约 28 亿美元的资产。

但黑客在冻结前疯狂“抢跑”，将部分 USDT 换成了 ETH 等原生资产。

目前仍有约 32.7 亿美元处于黑客的自由移动状态（主要包括 1.82 万枚 BTC 和超 45 万枚 ETH）。

5. 官方善后与现状

随后 Binance 14 陷入了黑客继续扫荡与官方尝试转移剩余资产的“拉锯战”。

@heyibinance 与 @cz_binance 相继发声，确认遇袭，承诺“用户资金绝对安全，币安将全额承担损失”，目前充提已暂停以配合安全检查。

今年加密安全事件频发，从硬件钱包被拆开安装间谍装置，到交易所资金被盗，加密资产安全又一次被提到了大家不得不关注的高度。

希望一切 Stay Safe，静待后续更新。

BINANCE SECURITY INCIDENT: WHAT WE KNOW

1/ Binance has confirmed a security breach affecting its hot wallets on the Ethereum, Bitcoin and TRON networks. Estimated losses range from $5.5B to $6B, according to on chain data.

2/ If confirmed at that scale, it would be the largest hack in the history of digital assets, roughly four times the $1.5B Bybit exploit in February 2025.

3/ Deposits and withdrawals have been temporarily suspended while Binance conducts security checks and cooperates with law enforcement.

4/ Binance co-CEO Yi He stated that user funds are safe and that the company will cover all losses resulting from the incident.

5/ Binance reports that approximately $3B of the stolen assets has been frozen, including more than $2.3B in USDT and USDC frozen by Tether and Circle.

6/ Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said the incident appears to be a hack and that he expects user funds to be fully covered.

7/ The cause of the breach has not been disclosed. Binance has committed to publishing a full post mortem once its investigation is complete.

text:
ppl still tend to think of @pendle_fi as a place to farm yield and speculate on points.

But Pendle is slowly moving away from the exact kind of incentive-heavy model that made it popular in the first place.

– Q3 emissions down ~58%, with reported YTD cuts reaching ~93%
– Annualized $PENDLE inflation ~0.2%
– V2 TVL grew 43% in Q3 to ~$1.16B
– Buybacks covered emissions 3.2x in Q3, up from 1.6x in Q2
– ~$1.36M used for buybacks during Q3

Cutting incentives that aggressively while TVL still grew is pretty wild, considering how much DeFi liquidity tends to disappear the moment rewards dry up.

Instead of rewarding whoever parks the biggest bag, pools now earn roughly $0.25 in PENDLE for every $1 in weekly trading fees, capped at $625/week.

Mature pools get just ~0.2% APR on up to $2.5M TVL, while another incentive stream rewards actual order-book depth, with issuer co-incentives getting a 15–22% match from Pendle.

Basically, less free lunch for idle TVL. More rewards for pools that actually get used.

This is where sPENDLE starts making sense.

Rather than locking $PENDLE for up to two years under the old vePENDLE model, holders can now stake with a 14-day withdrawal cooldown, or pay 5% to exit instantly.

Around 80% of retained protocol fees fund $PENDLE buybacks, which are distributed to active stakers every two weeks.

→ Better liquidity brings more trading, more trading generates fees, fees fund buybacks, and sPENDLE holders capture some of that activity instead of relying on fresh emissions.

Meanwhile, Pendle's liquidity mix is quietly changing too.

– RWA-backed dollars reached ~85% of its top 50 markets by end-Q3, up from ~70% mid-year
– @ethena’s share went from ~77% in Aug 2025 to below 10%
– @re, @withAUSD, Sky and other yield-bearing assets are taking a bigger slice

Though there's still a catch.

– Total fees fell ~18% in one Q3 comparison window
– Trading fees dropped ~40% over that period
– sPENDLE's estimated yield was only ~1.25% annualized in some periods

So that 3.2x buyback/emission ratio isn't entirely because business is booming. A lot of it comes from cutting the emissions denominator.

Plus, ~90% of capital faces maturities in Q4. Whether that money rolls over without heavy incentives is probably the biggest test ahead.

Still, I like the direction here.

Pendle already showed it can slash emissions without immediately nuking TVL. Now the question is whether fees and trading demand can grow enough to make the whole thing sustainable.

Less paying people to park money, more earning from people actually using the product.

That's a much more interesting version of DeFi imo.

This month, we released the new Injective Whitepaper, our first full rewrite since the original paper in December 2018.

Back then we described a front-running-resistant exchange protocol on Ethereum. Injective is now a layer-1 built for institutional finance and tokenization, and the new paper covers how the entire chain works to issue real-world assets and make them usable across markets, apps and AI agents.

What's inside:

→ Native RWA tokenization with role-based permissions over mint, send, receive and burn, plus receive hooks and sealable namespaces → iAssets, stablecoin-margined derivatives priced by oracles that track external assets without wrapping or pre-funding → A fully onchain orderbook that runs a sealed batch auction every block at one clearing price, so front-running and ordering MEV don't work → BFT consensus with a >2/3 commit threshold and deterministic finality in ~600ms → EVM and WASM sharing one state, with the MultiVM Token Standard keeping a single balance per asset that Solidity reads through precompiles → Perps with time-weighted funding, initial and maintenance margin checks, reduce-only liquidations and insurance funds → AI agents trading tokenized assets through MCP servers, policy-bounded signing and x402 payments in USDC → Onchain protocol revenue going to the Community BuyBack for $INJ every month with deflationary mechanisms built in

We also formalized the mathematical reasoning behind each of these parameters, including the consensus threshold, batch clearing rule, oracle accounting, margin checks, permission model and dynamic issuance.

6. Binance perp open interest 31.6bn sits inside a venue with withdrawals shut.

8. Core advice: withdraw from any CEX that cannot show you its books. Self-custody or on-chain until Binance reopens.

author: D2_Finance
quoted_text:
Quick ones from our side.

1) D2 has no exposure to @Binance. We have never traded there.
2) We pulled our USDC from Aave live-tracking the attacker as he parked 60M USDT in the pool and borrowed 19,762 ETH against it.
3) We are long gamma and trading it.

Forensic tl;dr.

Eight chains, one signing layer. The attacker held the hot-wallet keys. Binance 14 fell to a 7702 delegation signed over 50 consecutive nonces, which is what you do when the key is yours and the wallet is still processing withdrawals. BTC and Tron went on plain signatures in the same 20 minutes. Gross 5.0 to 5.8bn, 2.4bn frozen, about 3bn clean.

Where it sits: 386K ETH across three wallets, 17,270 BTC untouched in 17 wallets, 685M TRX, 970K SOL. The ETH is the laundering leg. Bybit’s went to BTC through THORChain in ten days.

As we write, Binance 14 is still delegated to the attacker’s contract and Binance’s own refills were swept again at 21:04 and 21:44 UTC. Three hours in, the automation that feeds the thief is still running.

This is the largest theft in the history of the asset class and it ran through one company’s signing layer while that company’s scripts kept topping up the drain. 

For eight years the industry’s single point of failure has had a logo. Tonight the alternative had its books on-chain, its withdrawals open, and 2.4bn of HYPE perp volume in 24 hours. We have traded there every day since before the TGE. Move.

text:
Two real‑world yield streams. One onchain pipeline: @apyx_fi.

@MicroStrategy’s preferred shares spin off cash dividends, and U.S. Treasuries generate interest, Apyx channels both into DeFi seamlessly.

The appeal is simple: earn from real‑world assets through tokens you can hold and use onchain. But the tokens do different jobs, and those differences matter.

Here’s how the money moves:

❶  apxUSD gives you liquidity.

Its reserves include dividend-paying preferred shares from crypto treasury companies, including Strategy’s STRC. You can use apxUSD across supported markets, but holding it alone doesn’t earn yield.

❷ apyUSD passes the income through. (~13.78% APY)

Deposit apxUSD into a vault and receive apyUSD. As dividends accrue, each apyUSD becomes redeemable for more apxUSD. Your balance stays unchanged; its redemption value grows. Exiting involves a cooldown and fees, and yield stops during the wait.

❸ aptUSD takes the Treasury route. (~3.84% APY)

It’s backed by U.S. Treasuries and cash equivalents. Hold it and yield accrues automatically, with no separate staking step, management fees or performance fees. There’s no protocol cooldown, though swaps still depend on liquidity.

And now let's talk about $APYX.

$APYX is Apyx’s planned governance and participation token, with a fixed supply of 100M.

Holders can vote on reserve allocation, risk settings, and payouts. The current model distributes 50% of monthly reserve growth to stakers and retains 50% to grow the reserve.

There are two planned staking options:

→ xAPYX: protocol revenue buys APYX, increasing backing per vault token
→ yAPYX: protocol revenue pays holders in apxUSD

The best exposure is mainly via Apyx Pips:

- Earn pips for eligible holdings, commitments, and supported DeFi positions involving the assets above
- Points accrue daily based on USD value × an activity multiplier (LP and commitments can boost multipliers vs. holding)
- Season 1 users receive a 1.2× loyalty multiplier on eligible Season 2 activity

If you think you’re late: Season 2 has more allocation than Season 1, and both are planned to fully unlock at TGE.

- Season 2: 9M APYX (9% of supply)
- Season 1: 5% of supply

---

➥ Final Take

Apyx brings two compelling income sources under one roof: Strategy’s preferred-share dividends through apyUSD and U.S. Treasury yield through aptUSD.

Different risks, different uses, but seamlessly accessible through the same DeFi platform.

That gives $APYX a clear thesis: participation in the economics of bringing those income streams onchain, with a planned share of reserve growth for stakers.

"We will keep monitoring the exploiter’s wallets and the affected price feeds and will share updates as they come. Markets will stay frozen until the exploiter’s funds stop moving and we get more clarity on the containment from Binance’s side. We will then work with Aave Labs and the other service providers on a staged unfreeze. A long freeze also affects utilisation. Frozen reserves take no new supply, so withdrawals by large suppliers raise utilisation and borrow rates, and only repayments pull them back down. We are watching utilisation on the frozen reserves, and will evaluate the order of the unfreeze."

币安被盗过程 暂时进程

币安补了2亿USDT，72秒就被黑客扫走

10月30日凌晨5点42分（北京时间），币安从自家钱包 Binance 124 往热钱包 Binance 14 转了2亿USDT。可这个钱包当时已经在攻击者手里，72秒后这2亿就被全部转走了。

链上记录还原的经过：

04:20，攻击者用 EIP-7702 给 Binance 14 设了委托，提前签好50个授权，其中1个生效
04:24，Binance 16 自己签名，向攻击者转出5574万USDT
05:42，币安往已被控制的 Binance 14 补进2亿USDT
05:44，这2亿被攻击者全部扫走，不过 Tether 已经冻结了这个地址
06:22 币安暂停提币，17分钟后 Binance 14 又被扫走128 ETH 和50多种代币
06:55 币安开始把剩下的币转进冷钱包，但到06:57，攻击者的委托还挂着没撤
被盗之后转进 Binance 14 的2199 ETH，被扫走2198 ETH；进来2.06亿USDT，被扫走2.04亿。
最大的疑点是，每个授权都要用 Binance 14 的私钥签，Binance 16 也是用自己的私钥签名转出去的。这看起来不像被骗签了一次，更像是签名系统整个被攻破了。
信息来自链上数据整理，以币安官方公告为准。

quoted_text:
Grok按照时间总结的这次币安被盗的全部细节，原来黑客昨晚就开始准备了：
1、准备阶段
1）10月28日：攻击者地址（标记为发起方，如 0x7c86…5ca0）从Tornado Cash分多次获得少量ETH作为gas费（约三笔0.1 ETH级别），提前布局。
2）10月29日下午至傍晚：攻击者部署专门的清扫（sweeper）合约。期间有测试/演练交易，使用自身地址验证EIP-7702委托与扫荡流程。最终清扫合约约在下午部署完成。

2、主攻击阶段（10月30日凌晨）
1）约04:20：攻击者通过EIP-7702对Binance 14热钱包提交委托授权。交易中携带了约50个连续nonce的授权签名（全部由Binance 14自身私钥签署），确保即使nonce快速变化也能命中其中一个。授权生效后，Binance 14临时/持续执行攻击者部署的清扫合约代码。

2）04:24：主扫荡开始。Binance 14在一笔交易中转出约16.7万枚ETH（约3.8–3.9亿美元）+ 约16.15亿USDT + 60多种其他代币（包括RLUSD、wBETH、UNI、ENA、PEPE、LINK、AAVE等）至新地址（接收方被Etherscan标记为Binance Hot Wallet Exploiter）。单笔规模巨大。

3）约04:24:47（24秒后）：Binance 16热钱包直接用自身私钥签名，转出约2.8万枚ETH至同一接收地址。

4）约04:39–04:41起：部分ETH被二次转移至新地址。Hot Wallet 34等通过已委托的Binance 14权限，转出约7.8亿USDC + 后续约4300万USDC。

5）后续几十分钟内：多链持续流出，包括比特币网络、波场（Tron）、Arbitrum、Optimism、Base、Avalanche等。部分山寨币开始被抛售换ETH。

3、应急响应与冻结（凌晨5点后）
1）约1小时内：Tether与Circle紧急行动。Tether累计冻结超过15.67亿USDT；Circle冻结约8.23亿USDC。合计冻结稳定币超23亿美元，后续官方核实数字约25.4亿美元（含其他稳定币如USD1等）。Ripple、World Liberty Financial等也协助冻结部分资产。

2）约05:15：
CZ发帖称“用户资金安全”“看起来确实像针对币安的黑客攻击”，感谢Tether和Circle快速冻结。

约05:29起：币安官方发文，称已注意到潜在安全问题并积极调查，用户资金完全安全，提醒警惕诈骗。随后宣布进行安全检查、暂停多链提现，直至确认环境安全。

约06:00–07:00：何一等回应，感谢相关团队协助冻结；CZ回应净损失估算“可能略高一点，但会覆盖”。

损失规模与现状（截至目前公开数据）
1）总流出：与币安标记钱包相关的资产流出约56.43亿美元（以太坊约35.28亿、比特币约14.49亿、波场约6.28亿，其他链合计约3800万）
2）冻结：稳定币冻结至少23–25.4亿美元。
3）净损失估算：扣除已冻结部分后，DefiLlama等测算约10亿美元左右（占币安托管资产约0.69%）。CZ表示可能略高，但会覆盖。用户资金被官方声明为安全，历史上SAFU也多次兜底。

其他动态：
攻击者持续抛售部分山寨币换ETH；
有地址在Aave抵押USDT借ETH；
部分热钱包委托曾持续未及时撤销，导致新进入资金可能被二次扫荡。

攻击手法总结
主流观点认为这是利用以太坊EIP-7702机制（Pectra升级后的账户委托功能）对币安热钱包进行的攻击，核心是攻击者获取了相关热钱包私钥或签名能力，而非单纯智能合约漏洞。

不是传统智能合约漏洞，而是EIP-7702委托：普通钱包通过自身私钥签名后，可临时/持续执行指定合约代码。链上证据显示授权签名来自币安热钱包自身私钥，因此主流判断是私钥被获取，或签名系统/流程被突破/欺骗（类似过往交易所签名流程被操纵的案例）。攻击者提前用Tornado Cash洗gas、部署合约、用连续nonce保护授权，手法专业。
官方尚未公布完整入侵路径。

现在看起来用户资产应该是安全的、这个量级的损失对于币安来说并不是很大，应该能完全兜底。但不得不说，AI时代加密货币面临的安全环境，会越来越严峻。攻击门槛大幅降低、事件频率上升，总体呈现“更频繁、更智能化、更系统化”的特征。

AI并没有“创造”全新的根本漏洞，而是把已有的弱点（密钥、人、运营流程、新协议功能）放大并工业化。安全环境因此变得更动态、更高频：小规模、自动化攻击更常见，高价值目标（交易所热钱包、大型协议）仍可能出现单次数亿美元级别事件（这次更是到了数十亿级别）；

当然防守方也在大规模部署AI防护，用同样的技术反击。长期看，密钥管理（多签、阈值签名、硬件安全模块）、最小权限原则、AI agent的隔离与权限控制、这些都是最关键的系统性防线。

text:
The Binance drain took four minutes. The preparation took 18 hours, in public, on three empty wallets that rehearsed the exact move. All of it is on chain, Oct 29 UTC.

02:28 The operator address deploys sweeper v1, 0x19bee294a6daab49c9e5ab69a5da6c035c70f2bf. Unverified, drain function callable only by the operator.

13:51 Two fresh wallets with zero history get EIP-7702 delegations to sweeper v1:
0x837810e3be7a3e89c570e7a01a13d3b566aafbc3, two authorizations, nonces 0 and 1
0x9c29ba2de4b2d6c3630685650663cfe7b70dbb6b, three authorizations, nonces 0, 1 and 2
A fresh wallet's nonce is always zero, so one authorization would do. He sent two and three. He was testing whether a list with invalid nonces still goes through. Six minutes later a third address sends them dust. At 14:19 and 14:24 the operator runs the drain on both. They were empty, so nothing moved. The path works.

15:59 Sweeper v2 deployed, 0x63e842b054bd624a465454d533c33f573e9c6fae. This is the one that will sit on Binance 14.

16:20 and 16:25 Third fresh wallet, 0x43aedb9bad6219677a2c8d6858321c16988404bd, delegated to v2 twice. Between the two, 1.01 ETH arrives from 0xe4F9070e1316de2988fc6f869feaD8fb99cC74cd. 16:30 the sweeper moves 0.01 ETH out. 16:47 it moves the remaining 1.0 ETH back to 0xe4F9070e. Full rehearsal with real money, then the money goes home.

18:20 The same 0xe4F9070e sends 1.08 ETH to the operator. Gas for the real thing.

20:20:59 Binance 14 receives fifty authorizations in one transaction, nonces 18914775 to 18914824, sweeper v2. One matches.

20:24:23 167,464 ETH and 63 token transfers leave in a single call.

What this proves: the nonce spray was designed, not improvised. He knew in the morning that he would not have the live nonce of the target in the evening.

The rehearsals were public but anonymous, three empty wallets among the dozens of phishing delegations the chain sees every day. The alarm was the next step: a labeled Binance hot wallet accepting a 7702 delegation to a six-hour-old unverified contract. That is one rule in any monitoring system. From that transaction to the first sweep there were three minutes and twenty-four seconds. Nobody flagged it in that window.
author: zacodil
quoted_text:
Binance 14 signed fifty authorizations handing itself to a sweeper contract. The signatures are on chain. The read that fits best: a signing machine was compromised, the attacker could not take the keys out and could not pass the transfer policy, whitelists and limits, but could get it to sign one short message that policies written before May 2025 do not recognize. EIP-7702 did not open the door. It walked around the guard.

What 7702 is: a wallet can attach contract code to itself by signing (contract, nonce) with its own private key. Anyone can submit that signature and pay the gas. It only works if the nonce matches the wallet's live nonce at that moment. After that the code moves funds with no signer involved.

What happened, all on chain, Oct 29 UTC:
> 13:51 the attacker delegates two fresh empty wallets to a sweeper and drains them. A dry run.
> 15:59 deploys a second sweeper. 16:20 to 16:47 repeats the drill on a third empty wallet.
> 18:20 receives 1 ETH for gas.
> 20:20:59 one transaction to Binance 14 carrying 50 authorizations signed by Binance 14 itself, nonces 18914775 to 18914824. Whoever got them signed did not know the live nonce of a hot wallet that fires withdrawals every block, so they got fifty in a row and let the chain pick. Gas accounting shows exactly one matched.
> 20:24:23 first sweep: 167K ETH and 63 tokens including 1.6B USDT in one call. 20:41 the delegated wallet used its owner role on a separate smart wallet and moved 780M USDC from there too.

Binance has not said how the signatures were obtained. But the question for every custodian used to be "can this signer move a billion". Now it is "can this signer sign anything that is not a transfer".

text:
having operated custody systems at scale, here are my thoughts on what happened today and some suggestions for @binance. many people think using multi-party computation or a hardware security module automatically makes a system secure, but the reality is far from that. authorization runs throughout the stack, and that’s often where things go wrong.

the fact that the attacker was able to get 50 arbitrary 32-byte digests signed points to a compromise of the signing system’s authorization controls, though not necessarily the private key itself.

binance has revoked the malicious contract delegation from binance 14 and appeared to have starting using this address again. but unless it has a complete, tamper-proof log of everything signed during the compromise and can rule out outstanding malicious authorizations, the binance 14 key should be permanently retired. otherwise, the attacker may still hold pre-signed authorizations for future nonces, potentially a million nonces down the road, allowing them to delegate the account again to another contract they control. revoking the current delegation alone would not eliminate that risk. for the same reason, all keys accessible through the compromised signing system should be rotated. @cz_binance 

what’s interesting is that binance scheduled ethereum wallet maintenance for october 28, shortly after reporting dprk-linked infiltration attempts reported over the preceding week. this raises the question of whether some attack vectors remained undetected. if the maintenance involved new code or secrets, a supply chain compromise or an already compromised authorization path could have provided an opening.

today’s incident happened after binance had already identified infiltration attempts. given the attacker’s sophistication, we should assume they may have left additional ways back in. i expect binance will identify the immediate attack vector quickly, but i suspect there may be other footholds it has yet to uncover. binance should conduct a full sweep of its systems to identify any backdoors or other persistent access that could enable another attack.

another issue is tss node level payload validation. binance 14’s signing infrastructure appears to have allowed signatures without adequately enforcing what the payloads actually authorized. a signing service should not sign arbitrary bytes simply because the caller has permission to access it. the signing servers should independently validate the payload and enforce policies on exactly which actions are allowed. policy violations should trigger alerts and, where appropriate, pause signing for human investigation before operations resume.

given binance 14’s role in deposit consolidation and its limited set of outbound destinations, stronger checks should be enforced at each signing node. assuming a threshold signing architecture, each node should independently validate the payload and enforce transaction policies. these checks should create independent barriers to unauthorized signing, so that compromising a shared authorization layer alone is not enough to obtain a signature. if every node simply trusts the same authorization decision, distributing the key across multiple nodes leaves the system only as secure as a single authorization key.

binance 16 may use a different system from binance 14. its transfer of 28,005.6 eth to the attacker appears consistent with an internal withdrawal request following the same path as a legitimate user withdrawal, rather than the attacker gaining direct access to the signing server.

text: 이번 조정을.. AI가 자본만 잡아먹는 기술이 아니라는 것은 누구나 공감하기 때문에.. 결국 과거 철도 버블과 마찬가지로 자본이 재편되는 과정이라고 생각합니다.
author: mindmoon_108
quoted_text:
[ AI 투자는 끝나지 않았다, 부가 재편되고 있을 뿐이다. ]

"철도 버블도 30%~50% 조정을 거치며 3번 올랐다."

1. AI 수요는 늘고 있는데 반도체 주가는 왜 떨어질까.. 수요가 꺾인 것이 아니다. 마켓이 다시 계산하기 시작한 것은 성장률이 아니라, 성장을 유지하는 데 드는 자본의 비용과 기업에 최종적으로 남는 이익의 크기다.

2. 테슬라가 먼저 보여줬다. 모델 Y는 생산 효율이 높아졌지만 중국 전기차와 가격 경쟁이 붙으면서 판매가를 계속 내려야 했다. 원가가 20% 내려도 판매가가 30% 내리면 수익성은 오히려 나빠진다. 생산성 향상이 곧 주주 이익은 아니라는 얘기다.

3. 메모리도 같은 길을 갈 수 있다. 중국 CXMT는 삼성-하이닉스보다 기술이 앞서야 위협이 되는 것이 아니다. 범용 D램에서 일정 품질과 생산능력만 갖추고 점유율을 우선하면 가격 경쟁은 충분히 생긴다. 슈퍼사이클은 수요가 줄어야 끝나는 것이 아니라, 공급이 수요보다 빨리 늘어도 끝난다.

4. AI 토큰도 마찬가지다. 사용량은 폭발적으로 늘지만 토큰당 가격은 DeepSeek 같은 중국 모델과 경량화 경쟁으로 계속 내려간다. 사용량이 10배 늘어도 가격이 90% 내리면 매출은 제자리다. 중요한 질문은 사용량 증가 속도와 가격 하락 속도 중 어느 쪽이 빠르냐는 것이다.

5. 여기에 고금리가 겹친다. 미국 10년물이 5%를 넘고 실질금리가 높게 유지되면, 신용 스프레드 4%p를 얹은 AI 인프라 기업의 차입금리는 9%에 이른다. 투자수익률 8%짜리 데이터센터 프로젝트는 조달비용 4%일 때는 남는 장사였지만 9%가 되면 성장할수록 가치가 훼손된다.

6. GPU를 확보하는 것과 고객에게 팔 수 있는 컴퓨팅 서비스를 완성하는 것은 다르다. 한 AI 연구소 관계자는 최고 모델을 못 만들어도 일찍 확보한 GPU 임대료가 2~3배 올랐으니 되팔면 돈이 된다고 했고, 머스크는 부분 완공된 데이터센터에서 쓰지 못하고 묶이는 컴퓨팅 자원이 상당할 것이라고 했다. 두 발언은 같은 현실을 가리킨다. 바로 가동되는 시설은 부족해서 임대료는 오르는데.. 미완성 시설에 투자한 기업은 현금을 벌지 못한다.

7. 코어위브처럼 차입 의존도가 높은 사업에 적용하면 순서가 분명해진다. GPU와 시설에 돈이 먼저 나가고, 완공이나 전력 연결이 늦어지면 매출도 늦어지며.. 그동안 금융비용은 계약대로 계속 나간다. 추가 자금이 필요한 시점에 채권마켓이 더 비싼 금리를 요구하면 버티기 어려워진다. GPU 임대료가 높다는 것과 GPU 보유 기업의 재무가 위험하다는 것이 동시에 성립하는 이유이고.. 최근 기업채권 금리와 CDS가 오를 수밖에 없는 이유다.

8. 정리하면.. AI 산업은 두 방향의 압박을 동시에 받고 있다. 기술 발전과 경쟁은 제품과 서비스 가격을 내리고, 높은 실질금리는 자본의 가격을 높게 유지한다. 파는 값은 내려가는데 만드는데 드는 돈은 비싼 구조다. 메타는 CAPEX를 늘리고 테슬라는 줄였는데.. 이제 평가 기준은 투자 규모가 아니라 투자한 돈으로 얼마를 벌고 얼마나 빨리 회수하느냐로 옮겨갔다.

9. AI 혁명은 계속되겠지만.. 혁명을 주도하는 기업과 주식에서 가장 높은 수익률을 내는 기업은 다를 수 있다. 인터넷이 그랬듯 가치는 인프라를 깔았던 기업에서 인프라를 활용하는 기업으로 옮겨갈 수 있다. 지금 조정은 AI 성장의 끝이 아니라.. AI가 만든 부가 어디로 흘러갈지 재편되는 과정일지 모른다.

<첨부 차트: 철도 버블도 30%~50% 조정을 거치며 3번 올랐다.>

text:
币安被盗引发EIP-7702争议，神鱼、余弦称根源在签名环节而非协议

今天凌晨币安热钱包被盗，攻击者在以太坊上用的是EIP-7702授权，把钱包交给自己的程序批量扫币。7702是以太坊去年升级上线的功能，能让普通钱包委托一段代码来操作。争议就此而起：这次被盗，该不该怪7702？

一派认为7702是祸根。有人翻出2024年的旧帖，当时就有开发者警告，这个提案可能让攻击者抽走钱包里的全部资产，签名还更难看懂。

另一派认为7702只是工具，真正的问题是签名权失守。Cobo联合创始人神鱼 @bitfish 复盘发现，这次授权用的正是币安热钱包自己的私钥签名，问题出在签名环节，不是合约漏洞。

慢雾创始人余弦 @evilcos 也表示，黑客用7702只是为了方便批量清扫。

text:
OpenAI and Google both ship voice models. So why does anyone still build on AssemblyAI?

Dylan Fox (@YouveGotFox), founder, says it comes down to three things the big labs won’t bother with:

1) The last 10%. “It’s kind of easy to get 90% of the way there with an AI product, but the last 10% is what creates product market fit.”

2) The one-word utterance. A user says “yes” and the model misses it. “If you don’t get that correct, the whole agent experience will fail.” That’s one of hundreds of edge cases they track.

3) Latency at scale. The models have to stay fast at 100M API calls a day.

Go deep on a narrow thing, or get averaged into the big model.

text:
Google DeepMind 刚发表了一篇很有意思的研究，哪怕 AI 在所有专业技能上都超过人类，整个经济的结构也可能暂时没有太大变化。

这篇《The Economics of Intelligence》由 DeepMind 的 AGI 经济学负责人 Alex Imas、研究员 Andrew Koh，以及联合创始人 Shane Legg 共同撰写。

他们提出了一个很重要的问题，过去几年，AI 的能力几乎呈指数级增长，但为什么现实中的企业组织、就业市场和整体生产率看起来还没有发生那么大的变化？

研究团队认为，我们可能一直在用错误的方式衡量 AI。

现在几乎所有 Benchmark 都在测试单个模型能完成什么任务。但现实经济中，真正参与竞争的是企业。一个 AI 即使比任何人类专家都聪明，也未必能打败一群懂得分工协作的人。

因此，他们把 AI 的能力划分为两个维度：

一个是 Competence，也就是完成具体任务的能力。AI 在编程、数学、写作等领域不断进步，会让企业变得更精简，让许多工作变得更便宜，但整个产业结构未必发生根本改变。

另一个是 Coordination，也就是多个 Agent 之间的协作能力。

这个维度的变化可能更加剧烈。一旦 Agent 的协作能力突破某个临界点，组织规模就可能不再受到人类沟通成本和管理能力的限制。成千上万个 Agent 可以形成高度协调的生产组织，在软件、金融等能够大规模扩张的市场中，少数 AI 企业可能迅速取得压倒性优势。

更值得注意的是，他们预测 AI 对经济的冲击，很可能先体现在工资上，然后才是失业率和企业结构。

很多人可能还在原来的岗位上工作，但随着 AI 能够复制他们的技能，他们的劳动价值已经开始受到算力成本的影响。

我觉得这篇研究最有价值的地方，是提供了一个观察 AGI 进展的新角度。

现在大家都在关注模型的智力上限，关注下一代模型能不能解决更难的数学题、写出更好的代码。但真正决定 AI 会如何改造经济的，可能是另外一件事：

当一万个 Agent 可以像一家真正的公司那样高效运转时，今天的企业、就业和产业竞争格局会变成什么样？

当然，这还是一套经济模型推演，但我觉得这个问题值得所有 AI 创业者认真思考。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
I joined @GoogleDeepMind to develop a research program on the economics of AGI. Today, together with Andrew Koh (@andrewjkoh) and Shane Legg (@ShaneLegg), we are incredibly excited to release The Economics of Intelligence, the first in a series of projects from our group on how AGI will change the economy.

How do capability improvements transform the economy, and when? In this project, we define thresholds of economic capabilities, e.g., minimal AGI, based on how they transform the economy. We then track how the economy–market structure, employment, and wages–changes during the transition across capability regimes.

We have seen exponential increases in what AI agents can do but the broader economy seems almost remarkably unchanged. Part of the reason is that the solo AI agent is the wrong economic object; economic transformation is an equilibrium outcome where organizations compete. Looking at how intelligence functions within organizations, transformation will depend on when two key capability thresholds are crossed: competence (gains on individual skills, e.g., coding, math) and coordination (gains on ability of agents to cooperate and work together).

We show that what economic transformation looks like depends on whether AI becomes supercompetent, supercooperative, or both—the regime of artificial superintelligence (ASI). Tracking this transition shows why the real visible transformation may come from improvements in coordination—a capability most benchmarks don’t yet track. Past a certain threshold, AI capabilities can break the Coasian ceiling on firm size and lead to an economy that looks drastically different than the one we see today.

Two main takeaways:
1. To understand the path of transformation, we should be tracking agentic coordination more closely.
2. The impact of AI will likely show up in wages before market structure or employment.

We are really excited about this paper. Excited to hear people’s thoughts.

text:
The recent security incidents involving Bybit, Bitget, and now Binance should serve as a wake-up call for every leader in the crypto industry.

Security should never be an area of commercial competition. It is a shared responsibility to protect our customers and the entire industry.

Over the past decade, major crypto exchanges have made significant progress in protecting private keys. We have seen relatively few incidents involving direct private key compromises in recent years. So far, we have not seen conclusive evidence that Binance’s hot wallet private key was leaked. The greater concern may lie in vulnerabilities in access controls and wallet management systems.

Companies that have never experienced a major security incident should not assume they are inherently safer or immune to attacks.

At OKX, we have built multiple layers of sophisticated security protection and maintained a strong security track record over the past decade. But we also recognize that no system is absolutely secure. We must remain humble, vigilant, and constantly challenge our own security assumptions.

A major security breach at any exchange undermines trust in the entire crypto industry, ultimately hurting every company and every customer.

I believe CEOs across the industry need to come together, just as we did during the Bitcoin fork crisis in 2017, to establish stronger industry-wide security standards and coordinated response mechanisms.

For example, transfers and settlements between verified exchanges could be processed in real time, while large withdrawals to unknown or unverified addresses, as well as transactions granting smart contract permissions, should be subject to additional verification and appropriate security delays.

Crucially, these safeguards should be enforced at the cryptographic signing layer, rather than relying solely on application-level controls. Even if an attacker compromises an exchange’s wallet management system, they should not be able to bypass these fundamental security restrictions.

We should also establish industry-wide mechanisms for real-time security incident notifications, coordinated monitoring of suspicious funds, and rapid responses to potential attacks. Exchanges, stablecoin issuers, and other major industry participants should work together to enable the rapid, lawful temporary freezing of suspected stolen assets when necessary.

We should also work together to accelerate the industry’s transition to quantum-resistant cryptography and strengthen our defenses against emerging AI-powered security threats. These are long-term challenges that no single company can solve alone, and they require coordinated research, shared standards, and collective action across the industry.

Security is everyone’s responsibility. No company can protect the future of crypto alone.

text:
Aave protocol will be fine.

The hacker supplied 60M USDT and borrowed 19,762 wETH (~44.9M$) in 3 minutes, before Tether froze their address and before the Aave Guardian froze the Aave V3 Core reserves (46 min later).

But USDT is real money backed by dollars, and the position is criminal but overcollateralized in the eyes of the protocol: health factor 1.04, 59.9M$ of collateral against 44.9M$ of debt.

Sure, we now have a large borrower with little incentive to repay their loan, but liquidations work as usual: if ETH goes above ~2,365$ (+4%), the position gets liquidated like any other.

The Aave V3 Core wETH reserve is 2.16M wETH, so the hacker's debt is "only" 0.9% of it as I'm writing this.

I don't think Aave needs to take specific action against the hacker.

345k wETH is available right now (81.6% utilization), so wETH liquidity is sufficient if wETH depositors want to withdraw

There's no reason or need for a bank run.

The situation is much less dire than during the Kelp hack (zero-value collateral), and we should not expect a re-run of "DeFi United".

On paper, a governance proposal could force-liquidate the hacker by upgrading the Pool to target this single position (lowering the USDT liquidation threshold would hit every USDT supplier),

but I see no real upside in doing that as normal liquidation can eat this up without sweat.

The reserves are frozen now, but no need to panic; you can repay and withdraw. This isn't the first time this has happened, and it won't be the last, and Aave is still there.

Just another day in crypto.

text:
🚨 GoPlus Security Alert: Binance Multi-Chain Hot Wallet System Compromised

Approximately $5.8B has been stolen from Binance’s multi-chain hot wallet system. Roughly $3B of the stolen funds have been frozen so far.

Binance US is an independent platform and is not affected. BNB Chain was not attacked, and no Ethereum or EIP-7702 vulnerability is involved.

On-chain evidence strongly supports unauthorized outflows. The attacker obtained valid EIP-7702 authorization signatures for the Binance 14 hot wallet, delegated the wallet to a malicious contract, and then batch-transferred ETH and 63 tokens. The attacker further took control of USDC held in Hot Wallet 34.

EIP-7702 was used to increase the efficiency of asset movement. The malicious EIP-7702 delegation on Binance 14 was cleared at 00:10:35 UTC.

The root issue appears to be abuse of the signing or withdrawal system. Authorization signatures across 50+ consecutive nonces, direct signed transfers from other wallets, and simultaneous multi-chain theft make “signing infrastructure compromise” more likely than “raw private-key leakage.” Multiple private-key leaks or a software supply-chain attack cannot yet be ruled out.

Attacker-related IOCs:
Primary attacker address: `0x7C8601d4645b93cea45F71e118A729332e6B5CA0`
Malicious EIP-7702 implementation contract: `0x63e842B054Bd624a465454D533C33F573e9c6fAe`
Ethereum main consolidation address / Exploiter 2: `0x5227f603C1eE34CE3C06eFe6477003BDfCCB2f8c`

📌 Security Recommendations:
1. Exchanges, custodians, and high-value wallets should block EIP-7702 authorizations from high-value EOAs by default. When use is required, enforce an implementation-contract allowlist, chain-ID restrictions, independent approvals, and spending limits. Do not sign authorizations for consecutive future nonces.

2. Avoid letting one hot wallet serve as a full operator for other smart wallets. Apply least privilege by target contract, function, asset, amount, and time window. Separate signing policies and approval domains across chains, wallets, and business lines. Limit hot-wallet balances so a single signing authority cannot reach dozens of tokens or billions of dollars in assets.

3. For regular users: watch for phishing that exploits this incident. Trust only official Binance channels. Do not give passwords, verification codes, private keys, or seed phrases to any “compensation support.” When withdrawing, confirm the token and network status, test with a small amount first, and do not switch to unsupported chains out of panic.

text:
OpenAI 刚刚重写了 Model Spec（模型行为规范），这次最值得关注的变化，是开始为越来越自主的 AI Agent 制定行为准则。

过去，AI 主要负责回答问题、执行指令。但随着 Agent 开始独立完成复杂任务，越来越多的决策会发生在人类无法实时监督的情况下。OpenAI 认为，模型必须学会理解人的真实意图，并在指令没有覆盖的情况下自行判断。

新版 Model Spec 确立了五个核心价值：忠于人的意图、减少伤害、诚实透明、保障人的自主权，以及关照受到影响的人。

具体有几个值得关注的变化：

1. 模型需要结合对话历史、记忆和上下文理解用户的真实需求，而非机械执行字面指令。
2. 更加重视自主行动的边界。比如花钱、发送邮件、修改文件时，必须考虑潜在后果，尤其是那些难以撤销的操作。
3. 新增了支持人类自主决策、遵守社会规范等要求。AI 应该帮助用户建立自己的判断，而不是悄悄替用户做决定。
4. 删除了大量关于语言风格的具体规定，让模型更多根据用户的文化背景、个人偏好和反馈调整表达方式。

我觉得这份文件最有意思的地方，是它实际上触及了 Agent 时代一个很难回答的问题：

当 AI 已经足够聪明，可以在没有人类监督的情况下独立工作时，我们究竟应该允许它拥有多大的自主裁量权？

一个 Agent 如果根据你的历史偏好，擅自拒绝了一份工作邀请，或者替你给客户发了一封邮件，它可能完全相信自己理解了你的意图，但这未必是你真正想要的结果。

理解意图、主动行动和越权之间的界限，会变得越来越难划分。

OpenAI 也承认，目前的模型还没有完全达到新版规范的要求。

随着 Agent 真正进入现实世界，我觉得接下来 AI 安全领域最重要的讨论之一，就是如何让模型拥有足够的判断力，同时确保人类始终掌握最终决定权。

🧐还原币安黑客攻击路径：EIP-7702 授权机制被滥用

据 Cointelegraph 报道，Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan 表示，币安今日黑客事件可能源于签名系统被入侵，而非私钥被盗。攻击者据称将 50 个 EIP-7702 授权打包进一笔交易，以劫持币安钱包。币安尚未确认具体攻击方式。

市场流传的主要判断指向 EIP-7702 的权限委托功能被滥用。EIP-7702 是 2025 年以太坊升级引入的功能，允许普通钱包临时执行智能合约逻辑。

Cobo 创始人神鱼 @bitfish  表示，攻击者于 10 月 30 日凌晨 4 时 20 分广播一笔包含 50 项授权请求的交易，约 3 分钟后开始批量转移资产，涉及以太坊、波场等多条链，按当时币价估算，转移资产总额约 58 亿美元。

攻击者利用 EIP-7702 授权机制实施资产转移，事前已制定涵盖 64 种代币的转移清单，并使用测试钱包进行了两次演练，最后一次演练距正式攻击约 3 个半小时。攻击过程中，攻击者还将部分 USDT 等可冻结资产兑换为 ETH，以规避发行方冻结措施。

神鱼认为，从链上数据来看，此次事件的核心问题可能出在签名环节，目前未发现合约漏洞。究竟是私钥泄露还是签名系统遭利用，仍有待币安进一步确认。他同时提醒，各交易平台应排查签名系统是否存在签署非预期授权的风险。

也有分析指出，攻击的准备阶段可追溯至更早：攻击者地址先通过 Tornado Cash 获得少量 ETH 作为 gas 费，并部署了用于清空钱包的恶意 sweep 合约。关键一步发生在 UTC 时间 10 月 29 日约 20:20，攻击者通过 EIP-7702 提交授权，将标记为「Binance 14」的热钱包委托给自己部署的 sweep 合约——而这份授权是由币安热钱包自身的私钥签署并在链上验证的。

随后，约 167,464 枚 ETH 及数十种代币在极短时间内被转移至新地址，后续又有多个热钱包持续转出资金，资金流出覆盖以太坊、比特币、波场等至少 9 条链。这一路径的性质更接近签名基础设施或授权流程被攻破，而非单纯的合约漏洞。

币安方面表示会在事件结束后发布复盘报告，截至发稿上述分析均无法确认为黑客攻击过程。

if u wanna know what crypto to hold for the next bull run, apparently all u gotta do is look at today’s reported $5.6B Binance hack

guys no wonder $ETH is Kim Jong Un’s favorite pookie 

So bullish on my ETH babies😭

but jokes aside, I’d keep a very close eye on the market over the next 72 hours. wouldn’t be surprised if we get another leg down. I’m already getting ready to DCA.

this whole thing reminds me of 2022.

remember, LUNA collapsing in May wasn’t the bottom. Celsius and 3AC blew up in June, BTC flushed to around $17.6k, and then FTX happened in November and took us down to ~$15.5k.

looking back, those were some of the best accumulation opportunities of that entire cycle. but they didn’t all happen at once.

major blowups tend to cluster around periods of forced deleveraging. when institutions are scrambling for liquidity, they sell whatever they can, not necessarily what they want to. that’s when prices can temporarily disconnect from fundamentals.

now, I don’t think it’s fair to call this FTX 2.0 just yet.

FTX was fundamentally a solvency and credit contagion crisis. so far, the Binance situation appears to be a security breach, with roughly $2.4B in stablecoins reportedly frozen and Binance saying user funds are safe.

that’s encouraging, but we still don’t know the final losses or whether there are any second-order effects. frozen funds aren’t necessarily recovered funds either.

and remember, BTC was already under pressure before the hack news broke. we’ve got a hawkish Fed, weakness in tech stocks, and a market that’s still extremely sensitive to liquidity.

the hack just added another layer of uncertainty and triggered a pretty brutal long liquidation cascade.

so over the next few days, I’m watching withdrawals, any signs of contagion, whether futures leverage gets properly flushed out, and most importantly, whether real spot demand starts absorbing the selling.

a big red candle alone doesn’t mean we’ve found the bottom. I wanna see whether the forced sellers are actually running out.

I’m not interested in catching the exact bottom or levering myself into another disaster lol. just keeping dry powder and preparing to DCA in stages if we get another proper liquidity sweep.

and please, every time something blows up in crypto, people start screaming that the entire industry is finished.

we heard enough of that shit in 2022.

the industry survived, but plenty of individual companies and tokens didn’t. there’s a difference.

anyway, I’m watching closely and getting ready to buy the fear, fam. 🥒

二是散户靠一个币暴富的机会越来越少了。早年随便买点什么都能翻几十倍，现在机构、ETF、量化都进场了，散户能吃到的越来越少。

信的人说，这只是又一次黑天鹅。不信的人说，这就是币圈的宿命。再一次证明，在币圈真正的聪明人都是早就出金座资产配置甚至闲庭信步看一次次的闹剧，活下来比赚多少更重要。

author: MartinShkreli

text:
亚马逊过去一年创造了 1683 亿美元经营现金流，结果还是花超了 424 亿美元。而且，它还准备继续加大投入。

刚刚公布的三季度财报显示，截至今年 9 月底，亚马逊过去 12 个月的自由现金流为 -424 亿美元，去年同期还是正的 148 亿美元。

主要原因就是 AI。

过去一年，亚马逊的设备及基础设施净支出达到 2107 亿美元，同比增加了近 948 亿美元。大量资金被投入 AI 数据中心、芯片和算力基础设施。

但亚马逊的业务其实很好。AWS 三季度营收达到 460 亿美元，同比增长 39%，创下近五年来最快增速。集团营业利润率也达到历史最高的 13.9%。

即便如此，亚马逊仍然维持今年 2200 亿美元的资本开支计划。CEO Andy Jassy 甚至表示，2027 年的支出还会显著增加。

这个数字挺夸张的。2200 亿美元，已经接近亚马逊整个第四季度预计能创造的收入。

现在的 AI 军备竞赛已经进入了一个很有意思的阶段：云业务增长正在加速，企业的盈利能力也在改善，但赚到的现金仍然赶不上资本开支的速度。

对亚马逊而言，AI 带来的增长已经看得见了。接下来真正需要证明的是，这些以千亿美元计的基础设施投资，到底需要多少年才能收回成本。
